why: Taiwan runs on Google Maps reviews; iFoodie and Dcard are local but not linkable by search.

spots.name: Taipei 101
spots.desc: (臺北國際金融大樓) is rich in symbolism. This 101-floor, 508-meter high skyscraper is designed to resemble bamboo rising from the earth, a plant recognized in Asian cultures for its fast growth and flexibility. The building is divided into eight distinct sections, with eight being a number associated with prosperity in Chinese culture. The internal architecture of Taipei 101 is similarly awe-inspiring.…

spots.name: Yushan
spots.desc: Yushan (玉山 Yùshān), also known as Jade Mountain or Mt. Jade, at 3952m, is the highest mountain in Taiwan. It has also been claimed to be the tallest mountain in East Asia, but this depends on how one defines "East Asia".

spots.name: Sun Moon Lake
spots.desc: Sun Moon Lake National Scenic Area (日月潭國家風景區; rìyuètán) is in Nantou County of Taiwan.

spots.name: Taroko Gorge
spots.desc: Taroko Gorge (太魯閣: Tàilǔgé) is a deep, rocky, tree-lined canyon with a boulder-strewn, blue-green river at the bottom. Its magnificent scenery makes it an incredible place for hiking, and it welcomes visitors with trails ranging from flat and leisurely to strenuous and heart-pumping. The 19-km-long canyon in Xiulin Township near Taiwan's east coast is protected as Taroko National Park (太魯閣國家公園…

spots.name: Yangmingshan National Park
spots.desc: The National Park is famous for its cherry blossoms, hot springs, sulfur deposits, fumaroles, venomous snakes, and hiking trails, including Taiwan's tallest dormant volcano, Seven Star Mountain (1,120 m).

spots.name: Kenting National Park
spots.desc: Kenting National Park (墾丁國家公園 kěndīng gúojiā gōngyuán) is in at the extreme southern tip of Taiwan. It is famous for its beautiful beaches and lush vegetation.

spots.name: Anping Fort
spots.desc: In the early 17th century, European seafarers came to Asia to trade and develop colonial outposts. In 1624, the Dutch occupied today's Anping and took ten years to build a fort named "Fort Zeelandia." After 1662, because Koxinga and his son lived here, it was named "King Castle," "Anping Castle" as well as "Taiwan Castle." The Japanese rebuilt it and named it "Anping Old Fort." Today, the only…

spots.name: Kaohsiung Mosque
spots.desc: The 2nd mosque to be built in Taiwan.

spots.name: Beigang International Music Festival
spots.local: 北港國際音樂文化藝術節
spots.desc: A project of the Beigang Philharmonic Association, the festival takes place in Beigang. The festival has a series of concerts, mostly wind music, and an educational program within the Chia-Hu Conservatory. The festival also organizes an intercultural program for musicians from different countries.

spots.name: Taipei Grand Mosque
spots.desc: The first and largest mosque in Taiwan.
spots.addr: No. 62, Sec. 2, Xing Sheng South Road, Da'an District

spots.name: Shifen Waterfall
spots.desc: The broadest waterfall in Taiwan, 40 m wide and 20 m high.

spots.name: Shei-Pa National Park
spots.desc: The park covers a wide range of ecosystems between 760 meters at the lowest point, the Da-an River Valley (大安溪) and 3,886 meters elevation at the highest point, the top of Xueshan (雪山主峰).

spots.name: Xueshan (雪山)
spots.desc: At 3,886 m, Xueshan is one of Taiwan's Top 100 Mountains and Taiwan's second highest mountain. To hike it, you need two permits: (1) a National Park Headquarters Park Entry Permit, (2) and a National Police Agency Mountain Entry Permit (Chinese only). There is no charge for either permit.

spots.name: Alishan
spots.desc: Alishan National Scenic Area (阿里山國家風景區 Ālǐshān guójiā fēngjǐng qū) is a national park in Chiayi County, southern Taiwan. Located high up in Taiwan's mountainous spine, Alishan — "Mount Ali" — is Taiwan's most-visited national park. The historic Alishan Forest Railway brings passengers from the lowlands through the mountain village of Fenqihu (just before the park), alongside groves of…

spots.name: Taipei Zoo
spots.desc: Nestled in a tight, lush valley, Taipei zoo has all the leisurely charm of a large park, but you also get the enjoyment of wandering through trees and along lanes with a variety of animals and birds. Unlike many traditional zoos, the animals here are not confined to cages, but allowed to roam freely in open paddocks, and it is a very clean and well maintained facility. However, some of the animal…

spots.name: Chihkan Tower
spots.desc: Chihkan Tower is the landmark of Tainan and its most famous historic site. In 1653 the Dutch built Fort Providenti in the area, and the Chinese named it Tower of Savages or Tower of Red-haired Barbarians. Even though Chihkan Tower has survived different historical periods, with part of it turned into a temple to the sea god, it retains its rich and graceful architectural aspects. Crammed with…

spots.name: Longshan Temple
spots.desc: This temple is where countless generations of Taipei citizens have come to pray and seek guidance at times of trouble. As the temple is dedicated to Guanyin (the Buddhist representation of compassion) it is officially defined as Buddhist, but there is a great amount of folk religion mixed into the fabric of the beliefs at this temple.
spots.addr: No.211, Guangzhou Rd, Wanhua Dist. (near junction with Guilin Road)

spots.name: Fo Guang Shan Buddha Museum and Memorial Building
spots.desc: One of Taiwan's largest and most impressive Buddhist monasteries, founded in 1967. Arrive early (09:00) before the hordes of tourists.

spots.name: Dabajian Mountain
spots.desc: Dabajian Mountain is known for its steep grade, beautiful surroundings, and rugged terrain, making it a popular rock climbing mountain. There are many companies in the area that offer rock climbing tours to the mountain.

spots.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Constructed in the memory of Dr. Sun Yat-sen who is the founding father of the Republic of China. The construction of the Memorial commenced in 1965 in conjunction with the 100th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. It was opened on 16 May 1972, with the majestic architecture and placid landscape covering an area of some 115,500 m². The park named Zhongshan Park marks the front yard of the Hall.…

spots.name: Hehuan Mountain
spots.desc: This mountain has 7 peaks, which you can climb. There are short tracks and longer ones, even connected to each other. The bus ride here is a great and funny scenic drive – sit on the right side of the bus. In case you want to do more than just going up and down the peak, consult OpenStreetMap, which many mobile Apps like OsmAnd or Mapy.cz use. It has comprehensive and reliable tracks around…

spots.name: Taipei Film Festival
spots.desc: An international festival with two award sections – Taipei Award Nominees and International New Talent Nominees. Films are shown at several venues throughout the city.

spots.name: Hongmao Castle (Fort Santo Domingo)
spots.desc: constructed by the Dutch as 'Fort Anthonio' in 1641, and gained its present name in reference to the red-haired Dutch. The compound also served as the British Consulate in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It enjoys commanding views over the mouth of the Tamsui (Danshui) River.

spots.name: Beimen Metro Station
spots.desc: Displays some archeological remains from the Qing Dynasty. Arguably not worth a detour, but keep your eyes peeled when changing trains.

spots.name: Xingtian Temple
spots.desc: The temple was built in 1967 and was devoted to Guangong (AD 162-219), a famous deified general who lived during the Three Kingdoms period, and he is an important character in the Chinese classic Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The temple forbids the killing of animals as an offering, so you will see offerings of only fresh flowers, fruits and tea on the main altar. Many believers feel that this…
spots.addr: Corner of Minquan East Road and Songjiang Road

spots.name: South Penghu Marine National Park
spots.local: 澎湖南方四島國家公園
spots.desc: South Penghu Marine National Park (Chinese: 澎湖南方四島國家公園) is a marine park in the Penghu islands of Taiwan.

spots.name: Eternal Golden Fortress
spots.desc: A 19th-century coastal fortress, it was built during the Qing dynasty and armed with cannons to defend against the threat of Japanese invasion. Bricks from the remains of Fort Zeelandia were used during the fort's construction. The squarish fort feels like a very big park inside of its thick walls and gate tunnel and a visit will take not much more than 5 minutes. Paddle boats are available for…

spots.name: Longgang Mosque
spots.desc: The fifth mosque built in Taiwan, built in 1967.

spots.name: Yehliu
spots.desc: A 1,700m long rocky outcropping that contains a number of interesting rock formations.

spots.name: Lanyang River
spots.desc: The river flows through Yilan County for 73 km.

spots.name: Feng Chia Night Market
spots.local: Chinese: 逢甲夜市; pinyin: Féngjiǎ Yè Shì

spots.name: Cihu Mausoleum
spots.desc: The temporary resting place of former President (the first President of ROC) Chiang Kai-shek.

spots.name: Confucius Temple
spots.desc: A serene destination surrounded by a small park. The temple was built in 1665 as a place to perform rituals and cultivate intellectuals, and is regarded as the first academy of Taiwan. Explore the temple, then go to the incredibly popular shaved-ice store right on the opposite side.
spots.addr: No. 2, Nanmen Rd, West Central District

spots.name: At-Taqwa Mosque
spots.desc: The seventh mosque built in Taiwan, built in 2013.
spots.addr: No. 8-2, Zi Li 1st Road, Dayuan District

spots.name: Lalu Island
spots.desc: In the middle of the lake. Lalu (lit. "Lake Island") is the name the Thao tribe, the original inhabitants of the area, gave to this sacred land, though it was changed to Guanghua (光華 or "Glorious China") during Chiang Kai-shek's rule of Taiwan. After 1999's September 21 earthquake the Taiwanese government, attempting to show greater respect and political awareness towards the Thao, reverted the…

spots.name: Kavalan Distillery
spots.desc: This award-winning whisky distillery is named after the indigenous Kavalan people, who originally inhabited the Kabalan Plain of modern-day Yilan County. The distillery was completed in December 2005.

spots.name: Mount Guanyin
spots.desc: A volcano named after a female Buddha of Compassion called Guanyin.

spots.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.desc: MOCA Taipei is Taiwan's first art space dedicated to contemporary work. The red brick building was erected by the Japanese in 1921 and formerly served as Taipei City Hall as well as an elemantary school.

spots.name: Ama Museum
spots.local: 阿嬤家-和平與女性人權館
spots.desc: The museum is dedicated to the comfort women during the Japanese rule of Taiwan.
spots.addr: No.32, Sec. 3, Chengde Rd, Datong Dist

spots.name: Taipei Confucius Temple
spots.desc: Just next to Bao'an Temple, the Confucius Temple was built in 1879 when the Qing Court changed Taipei into a prefecture of the Province of Fujian, China. It was established to serve as the largest educational center in northern Taiwan. Every September 28, a large number of people from Taiwan and abroad come here to watch a solemn Confucius birthday ceremony and eight-row dance.

spots.name: Taipei Cultural Mosque
spots.desc: The third mosque built in Taiwan.
spots.addr: No. 3, Lane 25, Sec. 1, Xinhai Road, Zhongzheng District

spots.name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts
spots.desc: A large and elaborate modern arts museum, featuring rotating visual exhibits. The museum also has a very elaborate children's section, featuring hands-on art exhibits and creative playthings. There's also a children's reading room in the basement with Chinese and English books. Bring your children.

spots.name: National Taichung Theater
spots.desc: A world-class opera house designed by famous architect Toyo Ito.
spots.addr: No.101, Ln. 56, Sec. 2, Hueilai Rd. Situn Dist

spots.name: Taichung Intercontinental Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: The stadium opened in 2006, replacing the antiquated Taichung Baseball Field. The stadium is also a venue for rock concerts.

spots.name: Rainbow Village
spots.addr: No.25, Ln. 56, Chun’an Rd., Nantun Dist

spots.name: National Museum of Taiwan Literature
spots.desc: Located in a restored colonial-era Japanese building, even with the limited English on display this museum is fascinating. The coffee shop is good too.

spots.name: Hualien Al-Falah Mosque
spots.desc: The 9th mosque built in Taiwan.

spots.name: National Museum of Marine Biology and Aquarium
spots.desc: Opened in 2000, the complex features an aquarium as well as a water park.

spots.name: Wanchin Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: The first basilica church in Taiwan, built in 1870.

spots.name: Daan Forest Park
spots.desc: The park rests on 26 hectares in central Taipei bordered by Xinyi Road, Jianguo South Road, Heping East Road, and Xinsheng South Road. Due to its size and location, it is also known as Taipei Central Park. Bus lines 15, 52, 235, 278, 284, 20, 22, Xinyi Main Line service this park.

spots.name: Jibei Island
spots.desc: Jibei wharf is on this island.

spots.name: Luce Memorial Chapel
spots.desc: Designed by the renowned architect I.M. Pei, the Luce Memorial Chapel is an architectural landmark on the campus of Tunghai University. Today, it is a popular tourist destination and a place of worship regardless of visitors' religion. It's only open on Sunday, but it doesn't prevent seeing the outside, which takes 5-10 min.

spots.name: Taichung Park
spots.desc: The oldest park in Taichung. It was built when Taiwan was under Japanese rule and is also called “Chungshan Park” ('Sun Yat-sen park').

spots.name: Hsinchu Railway Station
spots.desc: Built in 1913 in the classic Baroque style that was popular in Taiwan at the beginning of the 20th century. There is nothing to see inside, but the facade provides a good backdrop for souvenir photographs of the city.

spots.name: National Museum of Taiwan History
spots.desc: The museum covers a broad overview of Taiwan's history from prehistoric beginnings to the present, illustrating various eras with large-scale interactive displays and dioramas. Temporary exhibits focus more of the museum's historical artifacts. Most of the exhibitions have clear English explanations. Besides the museum, the building sits in a large park and is architecturally interesting…

spots.name: Tainan Art Museum
spots.desc: The museum is divided into two buildings. Building 1 focuses on modern art and is housed in the former Tainan police headquarters. The building features 16 exhibits on a range of arts. Building 2 houses a number of arts facilities such as a theatre, a children's arts centre, and an arts research centre.
spots.addr: Building 1: No. 37, Nanmen Road; Building 2: No. 1, Section 2, Zhongyi Road

spots.name: Leofoo Village Theme Park
spots.desc: A theme park and a safari located in Guanxi Township. It features three roller coasters, as well as an old mining railway.

spots.name: St. John's Cathedral
spots.desc: The cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiayi.

spots.name: Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village
spots.desc: A theme park and cultural village showcasing the cultures of nine of Taiwan's indigenous ethnic groups, namely the Amis, Atayal, Bunun, Paiwan, Puyuma, Rukai, Sasiyat, Tao and Tsou.

spots.name: National Museum of Prehistory
spots.local: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館
spots.desc: In the 1980s and 1990s, a team of archaeologists from National Taiwan University excavated over 1,500 stone coffins and more than 20,000 stone and pottery artifacts belonging to the Peinan culture. This museum is dedicated to this discovery and is located a few kilometers from the actual archaeological site. It also houses an extremely in depth exhibit on the current aboriginal groups in Taiwan.…
spots.price: NT$100 (main museum), NT$30 (Peinan cultural park); discounts for students and groups

spots.name: Eluanbi Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse constructed in 1883 and located on Cape Eluanbi, the southernmost point of Taiwan, which separates Taiwan's South Bay from Banana Bay and the Taiwan Strait and the South China Sea from the Philippine Sea. The lighthouse is also known as "The Light of East Asia" because its light is the most intense of those on Taiwan.

spots.name: An-Nur Tongkang Mosque
spots.desc: It is the eighth mosque built in Taiwan. It is also the first mosque in Pingtung County, completed in 2018.

spots.name: Hobe Fort
spots.desc: Built in 1886, it is one of the best preserved forts of its type in Taiwan.

spots.name: Dulan Mountain
spots.desc: Dulan mountain is a mountain in the region that is 1190 m at its peak.

spots.name: Tamkmang University Lanyang Campus
spots.desc: It is located on Linmei Mountain, this modern campus has a different view at day and at night. At daytime, visitors can watch all of the Lanyang Plain and also Turtle Island (Guishan Island). At night, visitors can see the lights throughout the Lanyang plain.

spots.name: Penghu Great Bridge
spots.desc: This bridge connects Siyu Island and Baisha Main Island. It was constructed because the sea current between the two islands was too harsh to sail between them. The bridge is 2,494 m long.

spots.name: Chaotian Temple
spots.desc: A temple to the Chinese sea-goddess Mazu. Constructed in 1700, it became one of the most important Mazu temples in Taiwan and is known for its extravagant temple architecture. It is visited by more than a million pilgrims every year.

spots.name: National Museum of Natural Science
spots.desc: A large and elaborate science-themed museum, actually composed of seven museums in one. Its Science Center features a huge assortment of "hands-on" exhibits that demonstrate scientific principles. The separate Life Sciences section is also very large. There's also a large botanical garden with an impressive greenhouse and a giant mosquito, an earthquake museum, greenhouse, global cultures, global…
spots.price: Galleries NT$100; Space Theater (IMAX) NT$100; 3D Theater NT$70; Tropical Rainforest Greenhouse NT$20; Science Center…

spots.name: Chihou Lighthouse
spots.desc: The lighthouse was built by English technicians during the rule of the Ching Dynasty (1883). In 1916, the Japanese remodeled it into Baroque style and painted it white. This renovation was made as part of the expansion of Dagao port. The lighthouse has played a crucial role in guiding ships since 1918 during night sailing.

spots.name: Chihou Fort
spots.desc: Chihou Fort is a battery which was designed by an English engineer. It was after the Ching (Qing) government took over Taiwan that the fort became a military base. The fort stationed a naval commander and one hundred soldiers. The battery was also armored with four British-made Armstrong breechloaders weighing 6.5 tons each. The fort was occupied by the Japanese army in 1895. Subsequently, the…

spots.name: Liouhe Night Market
spots.desc: The most popular and touristy night market, full of Japanese and Korean tourists. Lots of seafood, some local dishes but more stuff for tourists, from Turkish doner to "Thai" banana pancakes. Don't expect the food to be particularly good—the practice seems to be to display a tank of live prawns to prove how fresh they are, all the while sticking frozen ones on the grill. Open pretty much every…

spots.name: Qixingtan Beach
spots.desc: One of the most popular attractions of Taiwan, although maybe not the most spectacular one. Crescent bay and clear blue waters with a beach full of colorful agates. This used to be a small fishing village but has now multiple scenic trails, pagodas, beach pavilions, and a star-gazing square. Excellent vistas of the ocean, delicious seafood, friendly people. The beach is not popular for swimming…

spots.name: Dapeng Bay
spots.desc: The largest lagoon on the southwest coastline of Taiwan Island.

spots.name: Da-xi Honeymoon Bay
spots.desc: Famous site that you will approach when you first enter Toucheng township. It offers surfing and it has national surfing competitions annually. Honeymoon Bay has a great view of Turtle island. The name "Honeymoon Bay" refers to the many couples that can be seen walking along this stretch of coast.

spots.name: New Taipei City Gold Museum
spots.desc: Formerly known as the Gold Ecological Park, the site is an open-air museum consisting of a number of buildings and facilities to document the history of the gold mining industry in Taiwan. The museum is accessible by bus from Ruifang Station.

spots.name: Gupo Island
spots.desc: An uninhabited island which is used by locals to harvest edible seaweed.

spots.name: Cape Santiago
spots.desc: The cape is the easternmost point of the island of Taiwan.

spots.name: Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Department Store
spots.desc: Sets in Taiwan Boulevard and besides Top City, Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Taichung is the most popular department store in Taiwan.
spots.addr: 臺中市西屯區臺灣大道三段301號

spots.name: Koxinga Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine on the western portion of the island dedicated to the military figure Koxinga.

spots.name: Gugang Lake
spots.desc: The lake features the Gugang Pavilion which was built in 1964 by Zhuang Wu-nan from Tamsui, Taipei. The pavilion is 16 meters in height.

spots.name: Dawulun Fort
spots.desc: A very important military base to safeguard the west side of Keelung Harbor. During the Opium War in 1840 and the Sino-French War in 1884, the court of Ching Dynasty sent military forces to guard this place. However, looking at the current structure and feature, the fort was probably renovated during the colonial period. The provincial historic site was located on Mount Tawulun. Located 231 m…

spots.name: The Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts
spots.desc: The museum hosts a permanent collection and temporary exhibits, mainly of paintings and sculptures from the 19th and 20th centuries.

spots.name: Fangyuan Museum of Arts
spots.desc: A small art museum housed in an old clinic building.

spots.name: Chiayi Municipal Museum
spots.desc: The founding of the museum was a collective community effort in the hope to establish a cultural public space for all of the residents of Chiayi City. Among its displays are silk wrappings used to cover Tibetan Buddhist texts and an Islamic jade collection of the Qing emperors.

spots.name: Longteng Broken Bridge
spots.desc: A red-brick bridge that was built in 1906, but became unusable after being damaged in an earthquake. A new bridge was built nearby, and the remains of the former bridge were left as a monument to those who have died in the most deadly earthquakes in Taiwan's history.

spots.name: Shengxing railway station
spots.desc: A railway station that was closed to normal service in 1998 due to a route change and is now a tourist spot surrounded by a cluster of tea shops and traditional Hakka restaurants.

spots.name: High-Heel Wedding Church
spots.desc: The building is shaped like a high-heel shoe 17.76 meters in height, 11.91 meters in width, and 25.16 meters in length. It is composed of over 300 pieces of blue-tinted glass. The church is famous for its use as a wedding venue. However, the building is not consecrated and has no religious function.

spots.name: Gaoshi Shrine
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine located in Gaoshi, a Paiwan village in Mudan. With the original shrine destroyed by typhoon in 1946, a new shrine was rebuilt in 2015, making it the only Shinto shrine constructed in Taiwan in the post–World War II era, following the end of the island's Japanese rule. The current shrine is not affiliated with the Shinto religion (or any other deity) but serves as a memorial for…

spots.name: Sichongxi Hot Spring
spots.desc: Housed in a Japanese-style building, the water is of alkaline type and rich in sodium carbonate.

spots.name: Janfusun Fancyworld
spots.desc: The park occupies an area of approximately 60 ha. Janfusun Fancyworld is the home of the 88-m tall Sky Wheel, a giant Ferris wheel. It has 50 passenger capsules and offers views across the Chianan Plain. The park's roller coasters include Diving Machine G5 and Insane Speed, both built by Swiss manufacturer Bolliger & Mabillard.

spots.name: Honey Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to honey and beekeeping.

spots.name: Zhaori Hot Springs
spots.desc: One of only 3 salt-water hot springs in the world with rocks surrounding them. The sea is heated by the energy from underwater volcanic activity. The hot spring consists of three open-air pools, a spa pool and five terrace-like pools, each with a different water temperature. Vendors there sell eggs and shrimps. People can boil eggs and roast shrimps. While soaking in it, visitors can listen to…

spots.name: Lin Family Mansion and Garden
spots.desc: One of the best examples of Qing-era Chinese architecture in Taiwan. It was built in 1888.

spots.name: Wulai Waterfall
spots.desc: An 80-m-high waterfall with a viewing deck.

spots.name: Bihu Park
spots.desc: A large park of 13 ha surrounding the Dapi lake.

spots.name: Longshan temple
spots.desc: Built in the Qing Emperor Qianlong period, Lugang Longshan Temple has a long history, large scale, exquisite carvings, no delicate decoration, only simple characters, flowers and birds clay sculpture, with ancient colors, more elegant taste.

spots.name: Bashian Caves
spots.desc: A series of caves caused by water erosion that house a number of tamples.

spots.name: Sanxiantai
spots.desc: An area containing a beach and several islands. The beach stretches for 10 km in length. A popular tourist attraction for its rocky coastal views, as well as its long footbridge in the shape of a sea dragon that connects the coast to the largest island. The name Sanxiantai means "three immortals platform", referring to the island with three large standing rocks.

spots.name: Dongyong Lighthouse
spots.desc: In the late 19th century, Qing Dynasty opened a port in the area, thus the Dongying Lighthouse was built by British engineers to guide ships. The construction was completed in 1902.

spots.name: Fulong Beach
spots.desc: A beach in Fulong village which plays host to the annual Hohaiyan Rock Festival.

spots.name: Ju Ming Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the renowned Taiwanese sculptor Ju Ming.

spots.name: Bitan
spots.desc: (emerald lake) a stretch of the naturally emerald-turquoise Xindian River that has been dammed and turned into a recreational area. Paddle boats can be hired, and there are some great river-side coffee shops (the ones furthest from the station, such as 'Waterside Bistro', are recommended) offering views over the river and the lush green mountains beyond. While it is not worth traveling a long…

spots.name: Xinzhuang Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: A 12,500-seat stadium which hosts games for the Chinese Professional Baseball League.

spots.name: Red House
spots.desc: Near the Ximending shopping area, the Red House was Taiwan's first modern market as well as a theater. Now, the renovated structure is home to an exhibition hall and a market selling innovative handicrafts.

spots.name: North Gate
spots.desc: Of the five ancient city gates, four are still standing. But of the four, only one is a true historical relic from the Qing Dynasty: the salmon-colored north gate, whose formal name in Cheng'en Gate (承恩門). It was built in a traditional South Fujian architectural style. Its external walls were built with granolithic and brown mosaic tiles from Beitou Kiln.

spots.name: Dalongdong Baoan Temple
spots.desc: Construction began on this temple in 1805 and was completed 25 years later. Baoan is a Taoist temple and one of the leading religious sites in Taipei. The temple's main deity is the emperor Baosheng, the god of medicine. The mural paintings and sculptures that adorn the building are considered some of the most impressive in Taiwan, and the temple won acclaim in the 2003 UNESCO Asia-Pacific…

spots.name: Martyr's Shrine
spots.desc: temple memorializing those who gave their lives for the Republic of China (ROC) during its tenure on mainland China and it's later existence on Taiwan. A changing of the guard ceremony is performed at the top of the hour where a military honor guard performs an impressive series of gun twirling and tossing in front of astounded tourists. To get to the shrine take the MRT to the Jiantan Station…

spots.name: Mudou Island
spots.desc: The island was named Mudouyu because the shape resembles an eye of a man or an ink marker of a carpenter.

spots.name: Taiping Mountain
spots.desc: One of Taiwan's three major forest recreation areas at 1,950m above sea level, Taiping Mountain is one of Taiwan's major ecological treasures.

spots.name: Jhihben National Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: A 110 hectare area of recreational forest.

spots.name: Losheng Sanatorium
spots.local: 衛生福利部樂生療養院
spots.desc: A former isolation center for leprosy sufferers.

spots.name: Zhiben Hot Spring
spots.desc: One of the most famous of Taiwan's hot springs.

spots.name: 921 Earthquake Museum of Taiwan
spots.desc: You may know that Taiwan has earthquakes, but how bad can they be? This museum is the answer. This museum was once a school, but was totally destroyed by the Chi-Chi earthquake in 1999. The government later decided to leave the ruins as they were and subsequently established a museum to preserve memories of the Chi-Chi earthquake. You can imagine the hard time and know how to deal with…

spots.name: Guning War History Museum
spots.desc: On the 1949 battle, including many paintings, tanks, jeeps. The villages next to it (Nanshan and Beishan, 南山/北山) have a few buildings still riddled with bullet holes from the battle. Line B tourist bus and bus 9, 10, and 11.

spots.name: Jiangong Islet
spots.desc: The island has a statue of Koxinga which was built in 1968 to commemorate the Ming Dynasty hero who led the resistance against Manchurian invaders. The islet also has a viewing platform offers a view of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Baimiwong Fort
spots.desc: It's in the northwest of Keelung harbor, safeguarding the harbor with the fort on the east shore. It was an important military base since the Ching Dynasty. The rectangle-shaped fort facing the sea is comprised of three sections: barbette, control center and observation station with the control center on the west of barbette and the observation station on the right. Both places are great choices…

spots.name: Republic of China Air Force Museum
spots.desc: The overall exhibition area of the museum spans over an area of 3 hectares, which consists of various collections of artifacts, archives, weapons and airplanes.

spots.name: Pier 2 Art Center
spots.desc: This former warehouse district has been converted into a series of contemporary art galleries. As these are commercial galleries and not museums, admission tends to be free. Between the warehouses there are numerous outdoor sculptures. The district is near Fishermen's Wharf, which can serve as a great place to grab a meal after a day looking at art.
spots.addr: between Hamasen Metro Station and Yanchengpu Metro Station

spots.name: Tianhou Temple
spots.desc: Erected soon after Koxinga's successful invasion of Dutch Taiwan, it is thought to be the oldest extant Mazu temple in Taiwan. Mazu is the Goddess of Sea and Patron Deity of fishermen, sailors and any occupations related to the sea.

spots.name: Old Tainan District Court
spots.desc: The former district courthouse is now used as a museum of legal matters and history for Southern Taiwan. The museum traces the history of Taiwan's legal system since the period of Japanese colonisation. Few of the displays are in English, but the museum and the building are worth a stroll around regardless.
spots.addr: No. 307, Section 1, Fuqian Road, West Central District

spots.name: Taiwan Salt Museum
spots.desc: A small museum focusing on the production of salt in Taiwan, housed on the site of what used to be the largest salt production facility in the country.

spots.name: Shihmen Reservoir
spots.desc: One of Taiwan's major reservoirs, near the Daxi Old Street.

spots.name: Dongdamen Night Market
spots.local: 花蓮東大門國際觀光夜市
spots.desc: Not quite as spectacular as other larger cities night markets, the Dongdamen Night Market still exudes a fun and frenetic vibe and offers a huge number of activities and culinary treats. The back lane is dedicated to indigenous aboriginal vendors and features live music and dance performances on weekends.

spots.name: Sun-Shooting Tower
spots.desc: The tower exterior designed was inspired by a giant sacred tree in Alishan. The brown aluminum pattern mimics the wood grain of the tree and the center is left with a 40-m-high empty space that mimics the crack in the center of that giant sacred tree. The interior bronze sculpture is inspired by the "Sun-Shooting" legend of Taiwanese aborigines. This bronze-made sculpture is 24 meters tall and 3…

spots.name: Chiayi Old Prison
spots.desc: A former prison building which now houses a museum of the prison system in Taiwan.

spots.name: Chiayi City Municipal Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: A 10,000-seat stadium built in 1918, and refurbished frequently since. The stadium regularly holds Chinese Professional Baseball League (CPBL) games.

spots.name: Lantan Lake
spots.desc: The lake is also called the Holland Lake, Dutch Lake, and Hong-Mao Pei (see ang mo) because the lake was dug by the Dutch around 300 years ago during the Dutch Formosa rule. The lake covers 2km2 and is the main water resource of Chiayi City.

spots.name: Wenhua Road Night Market
spots.desc: The night market features famous Chiayi snacks and delicacies. Many popular restaurants and traditional dishes can be found along the night market road.

spots.name: Taitung Railway Art Village
spots.desc: Taitung City converted several buildings of the old railway station into an exhibition space for local artists and artist in residence..

spots.name: Tropic of Cancer Monument
spots.desc: The first monument was built in the 34th year of Guangxu Emperor's reign. The current building was completed in 1995. The monument is on the Tropic of Cancer line which cut across Taiwan.

spots.name: Fongtien Temple
spots.desc: A multi-storey Mazu temple with a very ornate roof. There is a festival dedicated to Mazu held every year on 23rd day of the third month of the lunar calendar.

spots.name: Meishan Park
spots.desc: The park spans over an area of 6 hectares consisting of around 3,000 trees. The park is equipped with the sky corridor walking paths and tree house platform.

spots.name: Penglai Waterfall
spots.desc: The waterfall used to feature a cable car system but was destroyed during the 921 earthquake in 1999.

spots.name: National Radio Museum
spots.desc: A museum about radio broadcasting in Minxiong Township.

spots.name: Dapengbay International Circuit
spots.desc: A motorsports venue featuring a 3.5 km long circuit.

spots.name: Miaoli Railway Museum
spots.desc: A national level museum of the TRA system in Taiwan. The museum is only a short walk south from Miaoli station.

spots.name: Banqiao Stadium
spots.desc: A walkable distance from Banqiao station, the stadium has a seating capacity of 30,000. The stadium hosts a number of events (mostly football).

spots.name: Mount Jilong
spots.desc: The elevation of mountain is 588 m, which is Jiufen and Jinguashi’s dividing line. On the peak, people can overlook the whole Neihu district, Taipei City, Keelung and northeast coast seascape. Seen from Jinguashi or Fushan Temple, the mountain shape looks like a pregnant woman lying on the land, with her hair spread on the East Sea. Therefore, it is known as Big-Belly Beauty Mountain. There is a…

spots.name: Lingnan Fine Arts Museum
spots.desc: The museums features the first professional archive of Lingnan paintings in Taiwan.

spots.name: I-Tien Temple
spots.desc: An ornate, multi-layered temple.

spots.name: Jinguitou Fortress
spots.desc: A former fort that was an artillery battery.

spots.name: Chang Yu-sheng Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum about singer Chang Yu-sheng

spots.name: Lukang Folk Arts Museum
spots.desc: The museum houses a collection of Ming and Qing dynasty artifacts, such as: photographs, lacquerware, porcelain, carved stones, embroidery, and musical instruments. The building, and all the contents of the museum, were donated by local residents, particularly the Koo family. The building is an unusual combination of Asian architecture and Western architecture.

spots.name: Jiujiufeng Forest Trail
spots.desc: Checkout this 1.9-km-long hiking trail. The small road north of it dives into this picturesque and interestingly looking mountain range, which bends up and is round at the top, a little like stalactites. Also, the river valley nearby and the mountains across reveal the geological movements in this area, or are simply great for a picture.

spots.name: Sun Link Sea Forest Recreational Area
spots.desc: This commercially-run forest recreation area is located at an elevation of 1,600-1,800 meters above sea level, higher than Xitou, with an area of 40 hectares. It consists of herb and flower garden as well as three waterfalls.

spots.name: Fuyuan National Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: The forest recreation area is located at an elevation of 225–750 metres (738–2,461 ft) above sea level with a total area of 191 hectares (470 acres). The recreation area is equipped with BBQ area, camping ground, jungle trekking trails, etc.

spots.name: Eternal Spring Shrine
spots.desc: A mountainside memorial shrine that was built in honour of those who lost their lives building the nearby highway. The site offers picturesque views of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Qingshui Cliff
spots.desc: An impressive 21-km-long coastal cliff that rises 800 m above sea level on average. Its tallest peak, the Qingshui Mountain, rises 2408 m above sea level directly from the sea.

spots.name: Liyu Lake
spots.desc: A scenic lake good for a stroll or lunch, with boats for rent. There is also a mountain trail around the lake.

spots.name: Dongquan Lighthouse
spots.desc: The lighthouse was built by the British Empire in 1872 to guide ships to Fuzhou during the Qing Dynasty when they were forced to open up along with four other treaty ports for trading. It can cast a beam of light that can be seen up to 16.7 nautical miles away.

spots.name: Matsu Folk Culture Museum
spots.desc: A museum showcasing the history of the island and its inhabitants.

spots.name: Yanliao Beach Park
spots.desc: The beach spans 80 hectares and reaches all the way to Fulong Beach. The beach is easily accessible by bus from Keelung Station.

spots.name: Li Mei-shu Memorial Gallery
spots.desc: A gallery dedicated to Taiwanese painter, sculptor and politician Li Mei-shu.

spots.name: Yingge Ceramics Museum
spots.local: 新北市立鶯歌陶瓷博物館
spots.desc: Museum dedicated to preserving the history of ceramics in Taiwan, through imaginative and beautiful displays. The downstairs exhibit explains the fundamentals of ceramics, the various materials, categories, glazes, and production methods. The upstairs includes history exhibits, and galleries for rotating contemporary artistic exhibits. All exhibits have English signage, and an English web-based…
spots.hours: 09:30-17:00, Sat Sun 09:30-18:00. Closed 1st Mon of month and national holidays

spots.name: Baishatun Mazu Pilgrimage
spots.desc: A major Taoist folk event which has been held since 1863. It is usually held annually between lunar January and April in the western plains of Taiwan. After every lunar new year, the Mazu statue of Gongtian Temple at Baishatun, Tongxiao of Miaoli County, is placed in a palanquin and carried in procession to visit the Chaotian Temple. The distance covered is approximately 400 km total.

spots.name: Xiluo Bridge
spots.desc: Construction on the 2-km-long bridge originally began in 1936, but was halted after the outbreak of the Second World War. Construction resumed with the help of the US government following the end of the war. This bridge also has historically held significance for the pro-independence movement in Taiwan. The area to the south has been the seat of the People's Democratic Party while the area to the…

spots.name: Cape Santiago Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse built in 1931 for ship navigation.

spots.name: Linkou metro station
spots.desc: The station is situated on the Taoyuan Airport MTR Line.

spots.name: Zushi Temple
spots.desc: A Taoist temple along Sanxia Old Street.

spots.name: Mingzhi Academy
spots.desc: A former educational hall built in 1763.

spots.name: New Taipei City Art Museum
spots.desc: An art museum that opened on 25 Apr 2025.
spots.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:30, Sat Sun 10:00-18:00 (closed Mon, except on public holidays)
spots.price: Adult NT$100, student or senior (65+) NT$50, 16 and under or disabled free

spots.name: Wuling Farm (武陵農場)
spots.local: Wuling Recreation Area, pinyin: Wǔlíng Nóngchǎng

spots.name: Lecheng Temple
spots.desc: Mazu is the main deity worshipped here; the sea goddess is known as the "Hanxi Mazu" after the nearby Han River.

spots.name: Yizhong Street
spots.desc: A night market type of area northwest of Taichung, nearing Chungyo Department Store. The street consists of a college, a high school, and many cram schools from the Shuei Li building in the area. As a result, it is always teeming with students. Shops and restaurants are there to serve the youthful population and cater for their tastes with low prices and a casual atmosphere.

spots.name: Asia University Museum of Modern Art
spots.local: 亞洲大學附屬現代美術館
spots.desc: The museum building, which consists of three floors, houses a café, a shop and a lecture hall on the ground floor and art galleries on the upper and topmost floor.

spots.name: Chungyo Department Store
spots.addr: 臺中市北區三民路三段161號

spots.name: Juguang Tower
spots.desc: Memorial building with a small military museum and views of surrounding areas, near downtown Jincheng.

spots.name: Kinmen cultural village
spots.desc: Also referred to as Shanhou Culture Village (山后民俗文化村), it's a great little place to poke around, with Kinmens 2 best antique stores being located within the walls. It is only NT$50 to get in and a beautiful and well maintained example of South Fujian style traditional Chinese houses with swallow tail roofs and was built towards the end of the 1800s.

spots.name: Mofan Street
spots.desc: The street gets its name from the uniform hybrid architecture of Chinese and Western styles which means Model Street. The 75-m-long street features buildings with brick exteriors and arched door fronts modeled after the Japanese, Fujian and Western architecture. There are 16 buildings at each side connected by a common arcade.

spots.name: Ershawan Fort
spots.desc: Also called Haimen Tiansian (海門天險), which means very dangerous gate to the ocean in Mandarin. It was built by the Qing government in 1840. This fort saw action in the 1884-85 Sino-French War. Visitors can view Keelung Harbor from the gun emplacement to feel its significance. Buses: 101, 103 from Keelung Train Station, get off Haimen Tiansian (海門天險) bus stop.

spots.name: Gongzih Liao Fort
spots.desc: Built in the Qing Dynasty at the northeast of Keelung City. This old fort is as significant as the other forts considering its history and architecture. After World War II, it was used as a military facility by the ROC government until a few years ago when it was named a provincial historic site. During the colonial period, the fort was renovated and garrison was placed here after Taiwan was…

spots.name: Koxinga's Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine dedicated to Koxinga, with plaques and information about his life. Locally known as Zheng Chenggong, Koxinga is an intriguing iconic hero of Taiwan, symbolic in different ways to different people and his image bent to fit whoever is in charge. He was a pirate to the Dutch, a brave and loyal general to the Chinese, a brutal conqueror to the Aboriginal tribes and a favored son to the…

spots.name: Former Tainan Weather Observatory
spots.desc: A former meteorological station that was built in 1897 which is now used as a museum.

spots.name: Hilltop Garden Watercourse Museum
spots.desc: A large complex which used to be the water supply and treatment station for the city. The grounds of the museum span 20 hectares.

spots.name: Museum of Archaeology
spots.local: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館南科考古館
spots.desc: The museum is a branch of the National Museum of Prehistory and covers the prehistory฿ and heritage of the area. The museum features a number of artifacts which were unearthed during construction of the Southern Taiwan Science Park.

spots.name: Yeh Shih-tao Literature Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A museum constructed by the city government to commemorate the life and works of the Taiwanese literary figure Yeh Shih-tao.

spots.name: Taoyuan Martyr's Shrine
spots.desc: One of the best-kept Shinto shrines outside Japan.

spots.name: Chihsing Tan Katsuo Museum
spots.desc: A museum in Xincheng Township dedicated to dried bonito fish. The museum is accessible east from Beipu Station.

spots.name: Hualien Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: A 5,500-seat stadium that regularly features professional baseball games.

spots.name: Rareseed Ranch
spots.desc: A tourist attraction ranch in Wuhe Village, Ruisui Township.

spots.name: Tapung Old Fort
spots.desc: Constructed in 1912, during the period of Japanese occupation, the fort was built by the then governor to help with the effort to subjugate the local Altai indigenous people.

spots.name: Chiayi Confucian Temple
spots.desc: A Confucian temple within the Chiayi Park which was built in 1706, but relocated to its current site in 1961.

spots.name: Museum of Ancient Taiwan Tiles
spots.desc: A tiling museum housed in an old Japanese-era lumbermill building.
spots.addr: No. 282, Linsen West Road, West District

spots.name: Chiayi Park
spots.desc: A large 26.8-ha park in the city which contains a number of local landmarks within its grounds.

spots.name: Chiayi Botanical Garden
spots.desc: A botanical garden which spreads across 8.6 ha of land. It is an experimental ground for planning and developing economical tropical trees. As of 2020, there are 140 tree species in the garden, which is further classified into 47 families and 107 classes.

spots.name: Lintianshan Forestry Culture Park
spots.desc: The forest consists of former offices and residential buildings, dormitories, logging tools and machines, rail tracks, an elementary school, and a church. The site is divided into the forestry exhibition area, early settlement buildings, and the remains of Kangle New Village, administration and management area, and hiking trails.

spots.name: Green World Ecological Farm
spots.desc: A theme park in Beipu Township that focuses on ecological education. Covering 70 hectares, the park includes an educational farm, a house, a zoo, and a botanical garden that occupies about 173 acres and hosts over 2,000 species of plants and animals.

spots.name: Daodong Tutorial Academy
spots.desc: A tutorial academic built in 1857, the complex still contains the original establishment documents, as well as some of the materials and tools used to build it.

spots.name: Baozang Temple
spots.desc: It was built during the Qing dynasty. The temple displays several historic objects and almost 100 statues of gods.
spots.addr: No. 100, Lane 135, Section 3, Zhangnan Road, Fenyuan Township

spots.name: Hakka Round House
spots.desc: A large round building built in the Hakka traditional style with an observation deck on the third floor.

spots.name: Tongxiao Shrine
spots.desc: Built in 1937, the shrine has served a number of purposes over the years.

spots.name: Yingtsai Academy
spots.desc: A Southern Min-style tutorial academy featuring a bridge, garden, and pond.

spots.name: Taiwan Historica
spots.desc: Taiwan Historica was established on 1 June 1948 to compile the common history of Taiwan Province.

spots.name: Peitian Temple
spots.desc: The Peitian Temple was established in 1682 and is largely responsible for the growth of the surrounding area. The Peitian Temple is a center of Mazu worship and pilgrimage on Taiwan.

spots.name: Southwest Coast National Scenic Area
spots.local: 雲嘉南濱海國家風景區
spots.desc: In addition to ecological attractions, the scenic area has several remnants of Taiwan's now-defunct salt industry.

spots.name: Chiayi Performing Arts Center
spots.desc: The center is built in 6.1 hectares of land, which consists of auditorium, theater hall, rehearsal classroom, open air theater, art gallery, tourist service area, restaurant, shop, stage, pavilion etc.

spots.name: Pingtung Tutorial Academy
spots.desc: A former tutorial academy in Taiping Village, built in 1815.

spots.name: Yang Family Ancestral Hall
spots.desc: The building was constructed with traditional Hakka architecture style in quadrangle shape. It features a heart-shaped Tai chi pond located in front of the hall.

spots.name: Liudui Hakka Cultural Park
spots.desc: A cultural center focusing on Hakka people and culture. The two main concepts of the park are Hakka village life and natural ecology.

spots.name: Museum of Traditional Theater
spots.desc: A museum of traditional performing arts, particularly puppetry which remains popular in Taiwan.

spots.name: Beautiful Maiden Cave
spots.desc: An explorable cave complex that requires a fee for admission which also allows entry to the nearby Mountain Pig Ditch and Black Dwarf Cave.

spots.name: Erlun Story House
spots.desc: The story house building was built as the Erlun Police Station in 1899 during the Japanese rule of Taiwan. It was the first police station in Yunlin.

spots.name: Yong'an Temple
spots.desc: This is a temple dedicated to the deity Chen Yuanguang, who his followers refer to as the "Sacred Prince, Developer of Zhangzhou".

spots.name: Changhua County Art Museum
spots.desc: An art museum which serves the local area.

spots.name: Zhonggang Cihyu Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1685, it is the oldest Matsu temple in the county.

spots.name: Miaoli Park
spots.desc: A cultural center in Tongluo Township about Hakka people.

spots.name: Black Dwarf Cave
spots.desc: A large explorable cave on Liuqiu Island.

spots.name: Longluan Lake
spots.desc: The biggest fresh water lake in Taiwan.

spots.name: Green Island Human Rights Culture Park
spots.local: 白色恐怖綠島紀念園區
spots.desc: A museum established to remember the victims of the White Terror. Guided tours available daily at the following frequency: May-Sep: hourly 10:30-17:00, Oct-Apr: hourly 08:30-16:00

spots.name: Tofu Cape
spots.desc: The cape got its name because the rock on the area resembles tofu.

spots.name: Su'ao Cold Spring
spots.desc: The cold spring was discovered by the Japanese army in 1928. It has a spring water temperature of 22 °C and is both batheable and drinkable, and it has a pH of 5.5.

spots.name: Yilan Museum of Art
spots.desc: The original museum building was destroyed during World War II. In 1949, it was reconstructed as the Yilan branch of the Bank of Taiwan. The Yilan County Government later designated the area a historic landmark. The bank donated the building in 2012. The museum exhibits works made by local artists and also promoting local culture.

spots.name: Watziwei Nature Conservation Area
spots.desc: A small mangrove forest located on one end of Bali Left Bank Park. The unique ecosystem has made the governess put it under protection. But you can still get really close to it by the viewing trail.

spots.name: Shihsanhang Museum of Archaeology
spots.local: 新北市立十三行博物館
spots.desc: A modern-looking museum dedicated to an ancient culture that once existed on the north coast of Taiwan. It also displays collections related to Taiwan's archaeology developments. The museum has had free admission since 2010.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:00 (opens longer on weekends and summer)

spots.name: Formosa Fun Coast
spots.local: 八仙海岸 or 八仙樂園
spots.desc: Formerly one of the most successful water parks in Taiwan, it is "temporarily" closed after a catastrophic and fatal fire in 2015. The slides and pools now sit abandoned, crumbling and full of algae.

spots.name: Shengping Theater
spots.desc: The original theatre on this site was constructed in 1916, and the current building was completed in 1961. The theatre has frequent showings of films, traditional opera performances, among others.

spots.name: Tamsui Customs Wharf
spots.desc: Completed in 1861, this wharf was constructed to serve the Tamsui Customs Office.

spots.name: Tamsui Fisherman's Wharf
spots.desc: Downstream from the town, it offers a boardwalk, chic coffee shops and food windows, and some seafood restaurants with prices that the average local would consider outrageous (but may seem reasonable to visitors from Western countries). Fisherman's Wharf is also a departure point for tourist boats traveling along Taiwan's scenic northeast coast. The "Lover's Bridge", a single slanted tower cable…

spots.name: Tamsui Lover's Bridge
spots.desc: Completed in 2003, the bridge is designed to evoke the image of the sails of a ship.

spots.name: Tamsui Church
spots.desc: A mock-Gothic style Presbyterian church that was built by the Japanese and expanded later.

spots.name: Museum of World Religions
spots.desc: This 8,000-m² museum was inaugurated in 2001 by a Taiwanese Buddhist monastery. It is dedicated to the preservation of all sacred knowledge and aims to foster an understanding and respect among the different beliefs. The museum has permanent displays of sacred texts and artifacts representing all the major religions, short-term exhibitions and, in addition, hosts talks and discussions. It is a…

spots.name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
spots.desc: in 2011, the park turned into a full fledged art center. Now it is a hub for cultural activities and exhibits. You can walk around the park and see the old structures as well as the new exhibits, restaurants, and the Eslite mall. Within the Eslite mall you can participate in various activities including glass blowing, jewelry and soap making.
spots.addr: No. 133, Guangfu South Road, Xinyi District

spots.name: Fudekeng Environmental Restoration Park
spots.desc: The park houses the first photovoltaic power station in Taipei.

spots.name: Sun Yun-suan Memorial Museum
spots.local: 孫運璿科技人文紀念館
spots.desc: The museum displays permanent exhibitions of handwritten diaries, manuscripts, photographs and personal items of the ROC's former Premier Sun Yun-suan.
spots.addr: No. 10, Lane 6, Section 2, Chongqing South Road

spots.name: Huashan 1914 Creative Park
spots.local: 華山1914文化創意產業園區
spots.desc: What is now Huashan 1914 Creative Park opened in 1916 as Taihoku Winery during Japanese rule. It was privately owned winery that produced sake and ginseng wines, and bred moth orchids. The park as it is now was opened in 2005 and features a number of facilities for public use.

spots.name: Magong Old City Wall
spots.desc: The remains of the old city walls and one of the gates which were completed in 1889.

spots.name: Mazu Temple
spots.desc: The temple claims to be the oldest in Taiwan, possibly dating to the early Ming in the 15th century.

spots.name: Penghu Living Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the customs and culture of Penghu built in 2010.

spots.name: Penghu Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: Established in 1696 and dedicated to the goddess Guanyin, the temple is a popular attraction during the annual fireworks festival held between April and June.

spots.name: Hengshun South Gate
spots.desc: This palace-like gate is worth a visit when you are in Hengshun. Located in the middle of a roundabout.

spots.name: Drop of Water Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Contains collections of Taiwanese and Japanese literature.

spots.name: QingJing Scenic Area
spots.desc: This place seems particularly popular with locals. It has a 1 km long scenic bridge/walkway, a grassland with sheep and great views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. If you go by car or scooter, it is worth stopping here.

spots.name: Chulu Ranch
spots.desc: A cattle ranch where tourists can take part in a number of activities.

spots.name: Amis Folk Center
spots.desc: The center showcases the culture and history of the Amis indigenous people. The main buildings were reproduced based on hand drawings by a Japanese ethnologist. The buildings are the imitation of Shaman's house in Taibalang community in Hualien County.

spots.name: Chiaming Lake
spots.desc: It is the second highest lake area in Taiwan; the lake surface is 120 meters long and 80 meters wide at an elevation of 3,310 meters. In Bunun language, Chiaming Lake is called "cidanuman buan", meaning "Mirror of the moon"; in Taiwan, it is traditionally referred as "Angel's teardrop" or, due to its deep blue color, "God's lost sapphire".

spots.name: Mingchi National Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: The forest features an artificial lake surrounded by Chinese-style gardens.

spots.name: Old Caoling Tunnel South Information Spot
spots.local: 舊草嶺隧道南下資訊站
spots.desc: A converted railway tunnel that has been converted into a cycleway connecting Toucheng Township to Gongliao District, New Taipei City. The tunnel is 2.167 km in length.

spots.name: Beihai Tunnel
spots.desc: The tunnel was created in 1968 for amphibious landing, 10 years after the end of the Second Taiwan Strait Crisis between the Republic of China Armed Forces and the People's Liberation Army. The construction lasted for around 3 years and claimed the lives of over 100 soldiers. After the Matsu National Scenic Area Administration was established, it took over the management of the tunnel. It…

spots.name: Chin Pao San
spots.desc: A large hillside cemetery which overlooks the East China Sea. The cemetery is famous for the numerous artworks which adorn many of the graves.

spots.name: Twin Candlestick Islets
spots.desc: A rock formation that features two 60-m columns of rock jutting out of the sea.

spots.name: Pinglin Tea Museum
spots.desc: One of the world's largest tea museums. There are three main exhibition halls which show the history and process of growing tea, as well as an exhibition about tea leaves. Describing this as a museum that is just about tea ignores some of the incredible strangeness this place has on offer, including a selfie-setup where you can pretend to be Diogenes hiding in his bucket, and an interactive game…

spots.name: Taiwan Coal Mine Museum
spots.desc: A museum about coal mining in Pingxi District. The museum used to be the coal mining site during the later stage of Pingxi Era of Tai-Yiang Mining Inc called the New Pingxi Mine. It was first opened in 1965 and the first coal extracted was done in 1967. In 1997, the mining activity was halted due to the more competitive price from imported coal to Taiwan.

spots.name: Remains of the 13 Levels
spots.desc: The building used to be a copper and gold smelter plant called the Shuinandong Smelter that used to process refined ore from Jinguashi and Jiufen. The facility was shut down after the minerals in the area were exhausted.

spots.name: Bitoujiao Lighthouse
spots.desc: The lighthouse was built by the Japanese in 1897. The lighthouse is at the end of a trail that offers spectacular views of the ocean and eroded landforms.

spots.name: New Taipei City Hakka Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the Hakka people. The museum total area spans over 4.03 hectares.

spots.name: Sanxia History Museum
spots.desc: The first floor has an exhibition area that periodically hosts art activities. The second floor has an exhibition area of Sanxia historical items, old time implements and memorabilia.

spots.name: Shenkeng Old Street
spots.desc: A narrow street of old brick buildings giving an impression of how the town looked in a bygone era. The street also contains a number of shops and stalls where you can sample the districts' famous tofu.

spots.name: Jing-Mei White Terror Memorial Park
spots.desc: A former detention center for prisoners during the White Terror, the building is now a museum to human rights and the history of Taiwan's path towards democracy.

spots.name: Wuzhi Mountain Military Cemetery
spots.desc: Located approximately 700m above sea level, it is the largest military cemetery in Taiwan.

spots.name: Huaxi Street Night Market
spots.desc: This area had long been Taipei's most notorious red-light district, filled with brothels, pornography shops and snake meat restaurants in which the snakes would be killed and skinned in the street to attract potential customers. However, prostitution was banned by the Taiwanese government 1991 and the area has been thoroughly gentrified, with the last snake meat restaurant closing down in 2018.…

spots.name: Little Taiwan
spots.desc: a wave-cut platform that resembles the outline of the main island of Taiwan.

spots.name: Shouqia
spots.desc: A low mountain pass in the Central Mountain Range of Hengchun Peninsula between Daren in Taitung and Shizi in Pingtung. The term Qia(Cia) is derived from the Chinese pronunciation of the Japanese word 峠. Shouqia is also spelled as "Shouka" or "Shoucia".

spots.name: The National Center for Traditional Arts
Yehliu Ocean World
spots.desc: An oceanic theme-park.

spots.name: Temple of the Goddess of Mercy
Taichung Prefectural Hall
spots.desc: Located in the most developed district of the city is built by world-class architect, Weber+Hofer AG Architects. The city hall has a big plaza with water, trees, birds, and flowers.

spots.name: Martyr’s Shrine
spots.desc: Adjacent to the temple is the Martyrs' Shrine, dedicated to the heroes of the Republic of China.

spots.name: Wanhe Temple
spots.desc: This temple was built during the Qing Dynasty in thanks to the goddess Matsu. It is noted for exquisitely-designed carvings.

spots.name: Beitun Wenchang Temple
spots.desc: In 1864, the Wenwei and Wenping community school raised funds to construct the temple to raise the cultural standards, promote Confucianism, improve local literacy, train scholars for the imperial examinations and encourage education in the area. The temple was completed in 1871 as a Confucian Temple, retaining the two original shrines in name, operation and assets distribution, which were the…

spots.name: Second Market
spots.local: Chinese: 臺中市第二市場; pinyin: Táizhōngshì Dì'èr Shìchǎng
spots.desc: This market opened in 1917, and in the late 20th century became a tourist attraction known for its wide offerings of Taiwanese cuisine.

spots.name: Wufeng Lin Family Mansion and Garden
spots.desc: The former residence and grounds of the Wufeng Lin Family in Wufeng District. Owing to the size of the Lin family clan, the vast site can be divided into two sections, the Upper and Lower Mansions.

spots.name: Lihpao Land
spots.desc: A large amusement place with a waterpark (opens in hot summer months), an amusement park, a racing site, and famously, the tallest Ferris wheel in Taiwan.

spots.name: Xiyu Eastern Fort
spots.desc: Xiyu Eastern Fort was constructed in 1889 during Qing Dynasty rule of Taiwan to defend the area following the Sino-French War.

spots.name: Xiyu Western Fort
spots.desc: Built together with the Eastern Fort, following the SIno-French war, Xiyu Western Fort was important in delaying Japanese attacks during the Japanese invasion of Taiwan in 1895 but was abandoned during Japanese rule. The fort contains an inscription from Li Hongzhang.

spots.name: Mitsui Outlet Park Taichungport
spots.addr: 臺中市梧棲區臺灣大道十段168號

spots.name: Taichung Jazz Festival
spots.desc: An annual jazz music festival in Taichung, usually held in October and around Calligraphy Greenway for 10 days. Besides inviting jazz groups, many street food vendors and stores are around the festival, creating a strong picnic culture during the festival. You can also enjoy drinks there.

spots.name: 8-2-3 Artillery battle museum
spots.desc: Small but excellent museum, with a large amount of English signage to help explain the exhibits. A short loop telling the story of the Second Taiwan Strait Crisis of 1958, in which the Nationalists in Kinmen and Communists on the mainland shelled each other with artillery almost non-stop for months, a decade after the end of the Chinese Civil War. There is also a Virtual War room where you can…

spots.name: Zhaishan tunnels
spots.desc: Historic underground navy pier, where boats could offload supplies out of reach of Mainland artillery. Artillery guns and boats on display outside.

spots.name: Deyue Gun Tower
spots.desc: The tower was built in 1931 by Huang Hui-huang, a wealthy merchant from Shuitou.

spots.name: Kinmen Military Headquarters of Qing Dynasty
spots.desc: It was built as a study house during the Ming Dynasty, it was then transformed into the Kinmen Military Headquarters of Qing Dynasty during the rule of the Kangxi Emperor when Commander of Kinmen relocated his office from Jinmencheng to Jincheng.

spots.name: Jinshui Primary School
spots.desc: In Shuitou, with a small emigration and overseas Chinese museum. Line A tourist bus and bus 7/7A/7B.

spots.name: Gulongtou Zhenwei Residence
spots.desc: A historical building and a good example of the architecture of the time.

spots.name: Mashan Broadcasting and Observation Station
spots.desc: A historical broadcasting station and observation tower in Jinsha Township. The station used to send out propaganda message to the People's Liberation Army soldiers on Mainland China to surrender and join the Republic of China Armed Forces.

spots.name: Xu Jiang Xiao Wo Stone Inscription
spots.desc: A large stone inscription which dates back to the Ming Dynasty.

spots.name: Chiou Lianggong's Mother Chastity Arch
spots.desc: A stone arch erected in 1812 by Qiu Liang-gong to honour his mother, who had raised him after his father's early death.

spots.name: Chen Jing-lan Western House
spots.desc: It was built in 1917 by a local businessperson who built up his success in Singapore. During World War II, the house was used as a military hospital. It is the largest 'Western-style' house in Kinmen.

spots.name: Wentai Pagoda
spots.desc: Erected for the observation of the stars to make feng shui predictions in 1387. The current tower is a restoration.

spots.name: Zhengbin Fishing Port
spots.desc: A fish port with colourful houses. Good for photography and can bring some relief before walking into Hoping Island.

spots.name: Miaokou Night Market
spots.local: Keelung Night Market, 基隆廟口夜市
spots.desc: Miaokou Night Market is famous throughout Taiwan for its large selection of food. It meanders through lanes and alleys in the downtown area surrounding the Dianji Temple (奠濟宮). The night market is easily accessible on foot for most travelers arriving from other cities.
spots.hours: 24/7, but most active in the evening

spots.name: Anping Tree House
spots.desc: Anping Tree House was built as the warehouse of Tait & Co. During the Japanese occupation it was the office and warehouse of the Japan Salt Company. After World War II, the salt industry in Anping declined, and this area was abandoned. Over time, the aerial roots and branches of banyan trees wrapped around the building. Combined with the soil, red brick and partial concrete wall, this creates an…
spots.price: NT$70 for Tait&co merchant house, Anping tree house, and Zhu Jiu-Ying Residence, NT$35 for students with ID

spots.name: Yongcheng Theater
spots.desc: It was built as a rice mill, and was repurposed as a theatre after the Japanese occupation of Taiwan ended. The theatre was closed in the 2000s and acquired by the Tainan city government who redeveloped and reopened it.

spots.name: Sacrificial Rites Martial Temple
spots.desc: A large temple complex with a mix of Taoism and Buddhism. Among the numerous statues in the temple are the 18 arhats (look for the one with the long eyebrows). There's a steady flow of worshippers moving through the temple, some lighting incense or casting divination blocks. Behind it is a temple to the sea goddess Matsu.

spots.name: Hsinchu Museum of Military Dependents Village
Great South Gate
spots.desc: One of Tainan’s most well preserved city gates.

spots.name: Tainan City Zuojhen Fossil Park
spots.desc: A museum complex showcasing paleontological exhibits.

spots.name: Hualien Cultural and Creative Industries Park
spots.desc: A pedestrian area made up of 26 old factory warehouses which hosts a number of cultural establishments, mostly showcasing local arts and crafts.

spots.name: Hualien Martyrs' Shrine
spots.desc: Built on the site of the Karenkō Shrine, this is a memorial to those who have lost their lives in service of Taiwan.

spots.name: Pine Garden
spots.desc: A peaceful garden with 63 pine trees built around a historic building originally constructed to house the Japanese military.

spots.name: Former Residence of Zhang Xueliang
spots.desc: A museum about Zhang Xueliang, the person who declared the Chinese reunification in 1928 after the end of the Northern Expedition by the National Revolutionary Army led by Chiang Kai-shek to unite the Beiyang Government under the Republic of China. The house spans about 150 m2 in area. It is decorated with Zhang's old furniture and more than 500 pictures donated by his two nieces. A bronze statue…

spots.name: Liu Hsing-chin Comic Museum
spots.local: 劉興欽漫畫暨發明展覽館
spots.desc: A museum about the comics creator Liu Hsing-chin, located in Hengshan Township.

spots.name: Zhudong Timber Industry Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: The exhibition hall features the history of timber industry in Taiwan and traditional logging equipment.

spots.name: Cihtian Temple
spots.desc: A small temple built in 1835, dedicated to the Bodhisattva Guanyin which was constructed to promote peace with the local aboriginal populations.

spots.name: Little Ding-Dong Science Theme Park
spots.desc: An outdoor natural science park in Taiwan intended to promote scientific knowledge and creative thinking in children.

spots.name: Hinoki Village
spots.desc: Also referred to as the Cypress Forest Life Village, the village consists of 28 wooden Japanese-style dormitories as well as the Alishan Forest Club, director's official residence, guest house, public bathhouse, etc.
spots.addr: No. 1, Linsen East Road, East District

spots.name: Chiayi Jen Wu Temple
spots.desc: A smaller temple built in 1677 using materials imported from Fujian Province on the Chinese Mainland.

spots.name: Art Site of Chiayi Railway Warehouse
spots.desc: An artists' space constructed from a former railway yard where visitors can view works from local artists.
spots.hours: Last Sat of every month: 14:00 to 17:00

spots.name: Chiayi Cultural and Creative Industries Park
spots.local: 嘉義文化創意產業園區
spots.desc: A multi-purpose park area which also contains facilities for community education programmes.

spots.name: Hualien Railway Culture Park
spots.desc: An open-air museum to Taiwan's narrow gauge railway.

spots.name: Wuhe Temple
spots.desc: A Mazu temple in Yilin county that was constructed in 1796.

spots.name: Taiwan Hinoki Museum
spots.local: 希諾奇台灣檜木博物館
spots.desc: A museum about hinoki trees.

spots.name: Baozhong Yimin Temple
spots.addr: No. 360, Section 3, Yimin Road, Xinpu Township

spots.name: Yi Yuan Mansion
spots.desc: Also known as the Maxing Chen Yi-Yuan Family Mansion, the house was built by the Chen family in 1846 using money from their trading business with mainland China. It is the largest historic manor in the county.

spots.name: Luocuo Church
spots.desc: The original church structure was built in 1875 when a local resident invited Father Vinte Gomar of the Dominican Order to come to Puxin. Father Gomar then bought the land for 100 dollars in 1877. After the original structure was destroyed, the current structure was erected in 1996 using a Fujianese red-brick architectural style.

spots.name: Xizhou Gardens
spots.desc: The park used to be called the Changhua Fitzroy Gardens, designed for and named after the Fitzroy Gardens in Melbourne, Australia. The park covers an area of 123 hectares, making it the largest plain park in Taiwan. The park is the venue for the annual Flower Exhibition.
spots.addr: No. 138, Section 3, Zhongyang Road, Xizhou Township

spots.name: Lukang Ai Gate
spots.desc: The gate was built in 1839 so that the town could be closed off at night and prevent those from neighbouring areas from entering and causing trouble.

spots.name: Old Qiding Railway Tunnels
spots.desc: A pair of railway tunnels built in the 1920s that now allow visitors to stroll through them and the surrounding natural grounds.

spots.name: Miaoli Ceramics Museum
spots.desc: A museum cataloguing the traditions and culture of pottery production in the area.

spots.name: Museum of Saisiyat Folklore
spots.desc: The museum is dedicated to the culture of the Saisiyat indigenous people.

spots.name: Taiwan Oil Field Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: A museum of the petroleum industry in Taiwan established by the CPC Corporation, and sitting on the site where oil was first discovered in Taiwan.

spots.name: Jufang Hall
spots.desc: A historical building, built in a Western architectural style, which was completed in 1920.

spots.name: Nantou County Culture Park
spots.desc: The park's main building, County History Hall, was built in 1937 as the Wude Temple. Adjacent to the County History Hall is the Art Archive Hall which was built in 1952. It was later changed to its current use in 2003.

spots.name: Orchid Island Weather Station
spots.desc: A good place to see the whole island from one place and can help to orient yourself for your journey around the other attractions.

spots.name: Beinan Cultural Park
spots.desc: Associated with the Museum of Prehistory the Beinan Cultural Park contains the largest and most important prehistoric archaeological site in Taiwan. Beyond the archaeological site the park also consists of beautiful grounds with a commanding view of the surrounding area. Tours in Chinese begin twice a day at 10:00 and 15:00. English tours must be planned in advance.
spots.addr: Wenhuagongyuan Rd., Nanwang Village, Taitung City

spots.name: Tianhou Temple
spots.desc: While there are seemingly temples on every block this one dedicated to Mazu (Matsu) is ornately decorated and quite popular, especially on Mazu's birthday (23rd day of the 3rd lunar month — generally April or May).

spots.name: Château De Jourdeness
spots.desc: An industrial plant with a European-style garden and castle. It is the largest beauty biotechnology plant in the Asia-Pacific region.

spots.name: Chingchen Temple
spots.desc: An ornate temple structure; the original building was constructed in 1809, but collapsed in an earthquake a century later. The current structure was rebuilt using donations from the local community in 2000.

spots.name: Chukou Nature Center
spots.desc: A nature center in Xinfu Village. The site of the center was originally the sugar farm of Taiwan Sugar Corporation. It was then later turned into Chukou Nature Center.

spots.name: Siraya National Scenic Area
spots.desc: The scenic area is named after the Siraya people, an indigenous ethnic group that populated this region until well into the 18th century. Among the area's attractions are Zengwun Dam, Wusanto Reservoir, and the coffee plantations of Dongshan.

spots.name: Zhong-Sheng-Gong Memorial
spots.desc: The memorial was constructed in 1929 by the Zhen clan family members who moved to Taiwan from Guangdong during the Qing Dynasty in the 18th century.

spots.name: Pingtung Performing Arts Center
spots.desc: The arts center consists of music hall, multipurpose theater and open air plaza.

spots.name: Kucapungane
spots.desc: A Rukai aboriginal village in the mountains of southern Taiwan. Virtually abandoned since the 1970s, the village is well-known for its slate houses.

spots.name: Old House of Siiao Family
spots.desc: The house was constructed during the reign of Emperor Xianfeng during the Qing Dynasty. After the handover of Taiwan to Japan in 1895, a conflict broke out between the local residents and the Japanese. Some of the bullet holes from this conflict are still visible in the room walls.

spots.name: Wukou Village Liou Family Ancestral Hall
spots.desc: The Hakka-style hall spans over an area of 1 hectare. It was built with two internal wings, two external wings and Baroque-style walls.

spots.name: Checheng Fuan Temple
spots.desc: The largest temple in Taiwan whorshipping Tudigong (土地公 "Lord of the Soil and the Ground").

spots.name: Donglong Temple
spots.desc: The current temple complex was completed in 1887. The temple organises the Donggang King Boat Ceremony every three years on the 2nd, 5th, 8th and 11th year of the Chinese calendar.

spots.name: Three Mountains King Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1651, the temple name refers to three mountains in Mainland China: Mount Du, Mount Ming, and Mount Jing

spots.name: Zhaoan Hakka Cultural Hall
spots.desc: The cultural building was designed around the traditional Hakka circular building style.

spots.name: Sanyi Wood Sculpture Museum
spots.desc: A museum of woodworking and sculpture.

spots.name: West Lake Resortopia
spots.desc: A small theme park in Sanyi township.

spots.name: Lanyu Lighthouse
spots.desc: A 15-m-tall lighthouse, built in 1982.

spots.name: Mei-Ling Fine Arts Museum
spots.desc: An art museum in Puzi Art Park.

spots.name: Haomeiliao Wetland
spots.desc: The wetland spreads across 1,171 hectares of area.

spots.name: Cihfong Temple
spots.desc: A highly decorative temple built in 1775.

spots.name: Chenglong Wetlands
spots.desc: An area of scenic wetland spanning over 50 ha.

spots.name: Lüdao Lighthouse
spots.desc: The original lighthouse was built in 1939 and funded by the American Red Cross, but was destroyed during the Second World War. The current lighthouse was rebuilt by the ROC government in the 1940s.

spots.name: Su'ao Fortress
spots.desc: A fort built in the late 19th century to defend the area from invasion by the French.

spots.name: Neipi Beach
spots.desc: A large beach facing the Pacific Ocean which has coral reefs offshore.

spots.name: Wulaokeng Scenic Area
spots.desc: The park spreads across 400 hectares of area and features camping grounds and barbecue areas.

spots.name: Qing'an Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine by the side of the mountain highway with views directly out over the Pacific Ocean.

spots.name: Former Yilan Prison
spots.desc: The prison was founded in 1898 with the name Yilan Branch Institute of Taipei Punishment Institute.

spots.name: Memorial Hall of Founding of Yilan Administration
spots.desc: A memorial hall dedicated to the founding of Yilan County Government. The memorial hall building was built in 1900 where it used to be the official residence of magistrates. The building was later converted into a memorial hall and was inaugurated in 1997.

spots.name: Yilan Brick Kiln
spots.desc: A former brick manufacturing factory in Beijin Village. The Yilan Brick Kiln was established as Chen He Cheng Kiln Factory. It was later changed to Yilan Brick Kiln and ended its operation in the 1980s.

spots.name: Institute of Yilan County History
spots.desc: A local institute of history in Yilan City, built to collect, access, record, research and promote the local history of Yilan County. The institute regularly holds exhibitions, symposiums, seminars and forums about the research of Yilan County.

spots.name: Yilan Distillery Chia Chi Lan Wine Museum
spots.local: 宜蘭酒廠甲子蘭酒文物館
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the history of wine and wine-making in the region. The museum building was built in 1935.

spots.name: Yilan Literary Museum
spots.desc: The museum building was built as a principal's quarter of a school of agriculture. The museum was constructed with Japanese architectural style.
