It consists of two buildings, which are the principal's quarter of the former school of agriculture and the old secretary-general mansion building. The signage has limited English, but the grounds are pleasant for a stroll around.

spots.name: Hsinchu County Stadium
spots.desc: Also referred to as the Zhubei Dome (竹北巨蛋). The stadium consists of an outdoor arena used mostly for football and track and field events and outdoor concerts, and an indoor stadium for multiple sports events, exhibitions, conferences and performances.

spots.name: Xianse Temple
spots.desc: A large, ornate Taoist temple built during the 18th century.

spots.name: Tamsui Old Street and waterfront
spots.desc: Located along the Tamsui (Danshui) River, this pedestrian shopping area offers tourists a wide selection of restaurants, arcades, and stores specializing in traditional handicrafts. Visitors can sample Tamsui's local specialties: A-Gei (crystal noodles stuffed in fried bean curd, served with a mild hot sauce), fish ball soup, and "iron eggs" (eggs which have been stewed in a mix of herbs and…

spots.name: Former British Merchant Warehouse
spots.desc: The area used to be a warehouse to store tea-related products by the British tea merchants. It was then later bought by Shell Oil Company and expanded into four large warehouse and oil tanks. After the bombing by United States in 1944, the warehouse burned for three days and was half destroyed. It was eventually retired as a backup storage since and donated by Shell.

spots.name: Tamsui Customs Officers' Residence
spots.local: 前清淡水關稅務司官邸
spots.desc: The residence is a white-colored building built in a colonial style nicknamed Little White House. It was constructed in 1870 by the Qing government to handle the customs from the rapidly increasing trade with foreigners.

spots.name: Tamsui Red Castle
spots.desc: Built in the Victorian style in 1899 as the residence of a local businessman, it houses cafes and restaurants.

spots.name: Teng Feng Fish Ball Museum
spots.desc: The museum displays the production and environmental impact of creating fish ball products. The museum building is divided into two exhibition halls. The first exhibition hall is located on Tamsui Old Street consists of three floors. The second exhibition hall is where the Weixiang Fish Ball Shop used to be.

spots.name: Fuyou Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1782, it is one of the oldest temples in Tamsui. You can find it near the Old Street.

spots.name: Yonghe Baofu Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1822, the temple is dedicated to the Baosheng Dadi, a Chinese god of medicine. Among the first groups of migrants to the area from China were people from Quanzhou, to whom Baosheng Dadi was particularly important. Prior to the construction of the temple, worshipers were forced to cross the hazardous river to the Dalongdong Baoan Temple in Datong district.

spots.name: Guo Ziyi Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A Japanese-era building, built in a baroque architectural style, that exhibits various documents on Tang Dynasty poets, calligraphy and paintings.

spots.name: Central Street
spots.desc: The oldest street in the city, buildings along this street also show a mixture of Western and Fujianese elements.

spots.name: First Guesthouse
spots.desc: An historic guesthouse which was frequented by the President of the ROC, Chiang Kai-shek.

spots.name: Four-eyed Well
spots.desc: A historical water well, it is thought to have been dug during the Yuan or Ming dynasties.

spots.name: Penghu Reclamation Hall
spots.desc: The building was constructed in 1935 as the official residence of the Hōko Prefecture governor. After the handover of Taiwan from Japan to the Republic of China in 1945, the building became the official residence of the Penghu County magistrate.

spots.name: Daguankou Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: A smaller temple at the tip of a peninsular jutting out into Magong harbour.

spots.name: Magong Beiji Temple
spots.desc: A temple primarily devoted to the god Xuanwu. The date of construction of this temple is unknown, but the date of some repairs is recorded to be 1791.

spots.name: Shigong Temple
spots.desc: Commemorating Shi Lang (Navy during the Qing dynasty), the temple was established some time between 1683 and 1696.

spots.name: House of Citizen-Memorial Hall of Attendance
spots.desc: A 19th-century building that regularly hosts arts performances and film screenings. The hall was built to commemorate the Crown Prince Hirohito's visit to Taiwan in 1923. Wu Keming initiated the construction of the hall with funds he raised from community donations and government. It was also used as a public gathering venue for residents for meetings, seminars, banquets, and performances.

spots.name: Qidong Street Japanese Houses
spots.desc: A street of well-preserved Japanese-style wooden houses which date back to various periods during and before the Japanese colonial periods.

spots.name: Magong Chenghuang Temple
spots.desc: Completed in 1779, the temple serves the Taoist city god.

spots.name: Lukang Rimao Hang
spots.desc: The former building of a trading house established in 1784 by a Fujianese businessman.

spots.name: Lukang Culture Center
spots.desc: The local cultural centre for the town. The building was built in 1928 during the period of Japanese occupation of Taiwan.

spots.name: Yu Jen Jai
spots.desc: Established in 1877, the Yujhenjhai cakes are famous local specialties, as are Lukang's ox tongue cakes (牛舌餅) and oyster pancakes.

spots.name: Yusan Hall
spots.desc: A private house built in 1872, during the Qing dyansty period.

spots.name: Zinan Temple
spots.desc: The temple was established in 1745. It is believed that borrowing money from the Land God will bring good luck, good fortune, and prosperity.

spots.name: Chelungpu Fault Preservation Park
spots.desc: The park was established to commemorate the 921 earthquake in 1999.

spots.name: Jiji Weir
spots.desc: A large modern overflow dam. On land near the dam's north end is a stone inscribed with a slogan during the Qing Dynasty era (1800s) to commemorate the opening of the Nantou frontier to Chinese industry (the county had previously been self-governed by its Formosan aboriginal inhabitants).

spots.name: Chuping Archaeological Site
spots.desc: An archeological site that houses relics of the first prehistoric mountain settlements in Taiwan.

spots.name: Hualien Sugar Factory
spots.desc: It's been called a tourist trap by published travel guides, but don't let that stop you from checking it out. There are lots of little shops selling things from Hualien County, but the main attraction is the ice cream, which there may be a long (but fast-moving) line for, even at 10:00. It's worth stopping here for the ice cream, along with the general chaos that surrounds the factory (there are…

spots.name: Old Donghe Bridge
spots.desc: The bridge was designed and built in 1926 by the Japanese under the name Jikuen Bridge as a suspension bridge. It was the longest bridge designed during the Japanese rule of Taiwan. In 1953, the bridge was rebuilt due to damage caused by typhoon by maintaining the original height of the towers at each end. As of Dec 2020, the bridge is opened only for pedestrians.

spots.name: Chenggong Fish Harbor
spots.desc: The harbour features a fish market where locals can buy the catch directly from the fishermen. There are also restaurants in the area where you can bring your freshly bought fish and they will cook it for you.

spots.name: Dapo Pond
spots.desc: The area around the lake features several facilities, such as bike routes, footpath, pavilions, fishing area, bird watching area and garden.

spots.name: Dulan Site
spots.desc: An archaeological site excavated during the Japanese rule of Taiwan.

spots.name: Dulan Hsintung Sugar Factory
spots.desc: The culture park used to be a private sugar refinery operating in the region which was built during the Japanese rule of Taiwan. The refinery was destroyed during the Second World War and after it was closed, a group of art workers moved in and revived the building with the help of Taitung County Government. The culture park consists of bed and breakfast, handicraft shop, coffee house etc.

spots.name: Bunun Cultural Museum
spots.desc: a museum showcasing the history and culture of the Bunun indigeneous people. The museum establishment makes Haiduan the first indigenous township in Taiwan to construct a local museum. Outside the museum is a performance area for important Bunun tribal and cultural events.

spots.name: Meihua Lake
spots.desc: A suspension bridge connects an island in the middle of the lake to the walking trail through the surrounding area.

spots.name: Toucheng Old Street
spots.desc: A street featuring a number of houses of different architectural styles, from different periods stretching back to the Qing dynasty. They show a snapshot of Toucheng's history.

spots.name: Lee Rong-chun Literary Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the literary history of the area housed in a heritage-listed Japanese-style building.

spots.name: Erjie Rice Barn
spots.desc: The barn displays the early original tools used for agricultural activities at that time, including a 3-story high rice huller.

spots.name: Fushan Botanical Garden
spots.desc: A botanical garden managed by the Taiwan Forestry Research Institute. It is the largest botanical gardens in Asia and features over 700 species of pants. The botanical garden features a nature center which displays the information regarding the garden It has a 20 km-long walking path for visitors to explore the garden.

spots.name: War and Peace Memorial Park Exhibition Center
spots.local: 戰爭和平紀念公園主題館
spots.desc: The area around the center used to be the Stronghold #12 during the Chinese Civil War. The center displays history about Matsu under military rule, from the origins, chronology of military events, military items and military-citizens social culture display areas.

spots.name: Turtle Island
spots.desc: The island composes of granite rock which rises above sea water level. Its cracked surface makes it look like a gigantic turtle resting in the sea.

spots.name: Andong Tunnel
spots.desc: The tunnel path was constructed with 30 degrees angle downwards with 464 steps at a length of 260 meters. The tunnel itself is 640 meters long. It features military utilities, such as dormitories, ammunition depots, viewing platform etc.

spots.name: Mysterious Little Bay
spots.desc: The bay consists of many wave-cut gullies which were historically used by the local residents to hide from pirates. It is also a popular gathering place for birds.

spots.name: Dahan Stronghold
spots.desc: A former ROC military fort which has since been redeveloped as a tourist attraction. The site was completed in 1975 when the island was still under direct administration by the military.

spots.name: Tunnel 88
spots.desc: This tunnel was built centuries ago to defend the locals from pirates. Later it was used by the military and now it is used by the Matsu Distillery. The timings are odd and change frequently. Keep in mind the floor is sticky and the tunnel has a strong scent of Gaoliang.

spots.name: Matsu Distillery
spots.desc: The distillery features an exhibition room which exhibits several different Kaoliang liquors from different period, discontinued medical liquors, as well as tools used for liquor production..

spots.name: Hohaiyan Rock Festival
spots.desc: An annual rock music festival held on Fulong Beach. The festival is free-of-charge and attracts acts from around the world.

spots.name: Lingjiao Waterfall
spots.desc: The waterfall is easily accessible, within walking distance from the rail station.

spots.name: Shen'ao Fishing Port
spots.desc: A fishing port with views of both Jinguashi and Jiufen. The area is popular for its seafood restaurants, as well as its views.

spots.name: Sanxia Old Street
spots.desc: Buildings along the street are the baroque-style architecture from the Japanese period.

spots.name: Mudouyu Lighthouse
spots.desc: It stands 39.9 meters tall, making it the tallest lighthouse in Taiwan. The lighthouse has a water collecting facility to collect rainfall from its rooftop.

spots.name: Qimei Lighthouse
spots.desc: The lighthouse was built in 1939. It was the last lighthouse built by the Japanese government.

spots.name: Double-Heart of Stacked Stones
spots.desc: a stone fishing weir located on the north side of Cimei Township, Penghu County, Taiwan. It is a well-preserved ancient fish trap made by stacking stones to form a trap that resembles a flying heart.

spots.name: Wangan Green Turtle Tourism and Conservation Center
spots.local: 望安島綠蠵龜產卵棲地保護區
spots.desc: A conservation center for turtles in Tungan Village. The center exhibits the natural ecology in Wangan and exhibitions on turtles, environment and ecology.

spots.name: Beigang Fuxing Bridge
spots.desc: A small bridge, which was severely damaged in 2006, which was constructed during the Japanese colonial period to transport materials to and from the nearby sugar factory.

spots.name: Dounan Shun'an Temple
spots.desc: A larger complex, much of the inside is gilded and ornately decorated. A temple that is primarily dedicated to Mazu that was constructed in 1736.

spots.name: Yunlin Hand Puppet Museum
spots.desc: The building covers many aspects of hand puppets and related entertainment, which remains very popular throughout Taiwan. The museum building was built in 1931 as the Huwei District office. After the handover of Taiwan from Japan to the Republic of China in 1945, the building was converted into a police station.

spots.name: Yunlin County Private Yongnian High School

spots.desc: Established in the 51st year of the Republic of China, the campus architectural style is Western classical architecture. The Wenyin Building was established in 1961. spots.name: Shuntian Temple
spots.desc: It is the central temple of the Tuku settlement, dedicated to Mazu. It is a county-designated historic site. "Mazu Yingwaixiang" and so on reflect the people's trust in the temple's efficacy. In addition to ancient wood carvings, stone carvings, Jiaozhi pottery, etc., the temple also houses many cultural relics from the Tuku area during the Japanese occupation period, such as the Japanese-style…

spots.name: Jhen Wen Academy
spots.desc: A former tutorial academy where scholars in the area would gather to study classical poetry. The building was constructed in 1813.

spots.name: Xiluo Theater
spots.desc: The theater building was built in 1940 under the name Xiluo Opera House with the funds from the prestigious Lin Guang-he clan. It was then later renamed as Xiluo Old Theater. The theater building was closed in early 1990s.

spots.name: Xiluo Guangfu Temple
spots.desc: A prominent Mazu temple built in 1764. Because of the courtyard house was constructed from the worshiper's donations, the temple was named Guangfu which means wide blessing.

spots.name: Yu-hsiu Museum of Art

spots.desc: This park is dedicated to presenting a more traditional Taiwanese way of life. It includes a combination of authentic and recreated buildings and streets in an attempt to recreate a more rustic Taiwan. It is small, but well worth the visit at NT$50 and the lack of these kinds of buildings anywhere else in Taichung. To get here, you can take buses 31, 33 or 105, but these will take you a long time…

spots.name: Taichung Metropolitan Park
spots.desc: On the west side of the mountain. Great place for the weekend. Good night view.

spots.name: Fulfillment Amphitheater
spots.desc: A large-scale outdoor amphitheater in Wen-Hsin Forest Park on Wenxin Road. Every year, Taichung City Government holds "MidTaiwan Lantern Festival" here.

spots.name: Wugi Fishing Port
spots.desc: The port features the fish trading area, food center, recreational park by the sea, a sculpture park, parking lots and yacht wharf.

spots.name: Erkan Chen Residence
spots.desc: A former residence in Erkan Village, built in 1910. The residence was built with the classic southern Fujian style, featuring relief carvings, windows, doors and eaves. It forms a rectangular shape over an area of 330 m2 which includes three halls.

spots.name: Yuwengdao Lighthouse
spots.desc: The Yuwengdao Lighthouse is the oldest lighthouse in Taiwan. It was built by British engineer, David Marr Henderson, in 1875 on the site of the earlier "Xiyu Pagoda Lighthouse" (Chinese: 西嶼塔燈; pinyin: Xīyǔ tǎdēng), which had been built in 1778. The earlier Xiyu Pagoda Lighthouse structure was a stone tower with an oil lamp light source, and is mentioned on a stone stele that still stands within…

spots.name: Xiaomen Geology Gallery
spots.desc: The gallery exhibits information, history and geological features of Penghu Islands. The gallery is divided into eight sections, which are guide of Xiaomen Island, geomorphology of Penghu Islands, landscape model, rocks and minerals, ecology, marine ecology, culture of Xiaomen Island and showcase of specimens.

spots.name: Whale Cave
spots.desc: A natural arch worn into the cliff face which. From the side, it roughly has the shape of a whale.

spots.name: Chuwan Crab Museum
spots.desc: The museum displays various kinds of crabs around Penghu Islands.

spots.desc: A Buddhist & Taoist temple at Dachi Village.

spots.addr: 臺中市西區臺灣大道二段459號

spots.name: Siwei Tunnel
spots.desc: On Little Kinmen is even longer and quieter than Zhaishan Tunnel. It's located just to the left of the ferry terminal as you get off.

spots.name: Yu Da Wei Xian Sheng Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A small museum in Zhongzheng Park, next to the 8-2-3 Artillery Battle Museum, commemorating the life of the general who is credited with winning the 8-2-3 artillery war.

spots.name: Hujingtou Battle Museum
spots.desc: The museum displays the battle history, an observation post, and a broadcasting station.

spots.name: Maoshan Pagoda
spots.desc: Just to the west of Shuitou, it is not particularly impressive structure compared to many pagodas in China/Taiwan, but the views of the surrounding area are quite impressive and it's a very quiet place with very few tourists.

spots.name: Chiayi City Historical Relic Museum
spots.desc: A museum of local history within the main park in the city. There is a limited amount of material in English, so it may not be as engaging for non-Mandarin speakers.

spots.name: Jin Guang Fu Hall
spots.desc: An old Chinese-style mansion built in 1835.

spots.name: Lian-Hua Mountain San-sheng Palace
spots.desc: A hillside temple complex that was constructed in 1902.

spots.name: Mount Jiuhua Kshitigarbha Temple
spots.desc: A large, red, multi-storey temple complex.

spots.name: Former Nanzhuang Post Office
spots.desc: An old Japanese-style post office that is no longer in use. Some small souvenirs can be purchased here. The tiles used in the roof are supposed to have been made during the Tokugawa period.

spots.name: Wugu Cultural Village
spots.desc: Focused on the history, culture, and industry of ceramics in Taiwan.

spots.name: Nantou mother and daughter tree
spots.desc: A pair of camphor trees that were used by locals as a temple to the gods of the land and therefore were spared the logging that removed almost all other such trees from the area as land was cleared for agriculture.

spots.name: Bishan Temple
spots.desc: An impressive-looking wide white Buddhist temple with a large green tile roof. The temple dates back to 1752 and overlooks Caotun Township and the Bagua Plateau.

spots.name: Dongshi Natural Ecological Exhibition Center
spots.desc: The center exhibits the history of the local rural villages, fishing tools, and wetland ecology.

spots.name: Bantianyan Ziyun Temple
spots.desc: A moderately sized Buddhist temple that houses a large statue of the Bodhisattva Guanyin.

spots.name: Dashiye Temple
spots.desc: A relatively small Buddhist temple that was built in 1923. It is listed as a Grade III historic building by the government.

spots.name: Dongshi Fuling Temple
spots.desc: A large, ornate Buddhist tample that traces its history back to 1684; the current temple complex was moved to this site in 1871.

spots.name: Dongshi Xiantian Temple
spots.desc: An impressive temple structure that was erected in 1721 and dedicated to the worship of Taibai Jinxing.

spots.name: Guogou Jiande Temple
spots.desc: A rather drab temple building from the outside, the original building was constructed during the late Qing dynasty, however the current structure was rebuilt in 1959.

spots.name: Kaiyuan Temple
spots.desc: A relatively young temple (built in the 1970s), this is notable for housing the world's largest statue of the notable Chinese admiral Koxinga (Zheng Chenggong).

spots.name: Shouzhen Temple
spots.desc: The temple was built shortly after the end of the Japanese colonial period for the workers who built the Alishan railway. The temple is famous for the many moths that visit the temple that, it is claimed, do not to try to eat the offerings or adornments of the statues.

spots.name: Tiger Riding Temple
spots.desc: The temple is named for the 5 statues of the deity riding a tiger. The history of the temple dates back to 1762, although it has been reconstructed several times since then.

spots.name: Wufeng Temple
spots.desc: A small, but locally significant, temple dedicated to the local merchant Wu Feng that was erected in 1820. The legend says that he made effort to establish more friendly relations with the local indigenous tribes in the area.

spots.name: Chonglan Xiao Family Ancestral Temple
spots.desc: Built in the 19th century, this scenic temple is a popular, architecturally notable landmark.

spots.name: Former Pingtung Tobacco Factory
spots.desc: The site of the former state tobacco factory which closed down after the government lifted its monopoly control over tobacco production.

spots.name: Pingtung Baseball Field
spots.desc: The county's main sports stadium which can seat up to 10,000 people. While mostly used for baseball, there are occasionally also cricket matches held here.

spots.name: Wugou Shui Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine for the Liuk-tôi Hakka people who died in armed conflicts with the Pepo people in 1833.

spots.name: Linhousilin Forest Park

spots.desc: The park was created as a lowland forest reserve. It spans over a total area of 1,005 ha.

spots.name: Beidou Red Brick Market

Longpan Park

spots.desc: A multi-storey temple painted in gold.

spots.name: Fude Temple
spots.desc: A small temple dedicated to the Land God of the local area. Due to the high number of worshippers burning incense on important festival days, particularly the first and fifteenth day of the Lunar New Year, the air around the temple becomes so thick with smoke that it exceeds the air quality standards and had to be granted a special dispensation from the government.

spots.name: Toufen Stone Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: The small house was built by a local farmer who found 3 strangely shaped stones in a nearby stream and felt that the stones were connected to the Buddhist Bodhisattva Guanyin, also called the 'Goddess of Mercy'.

spots.name: Wu Fu Temple of baki' Soro:

spots.name: Chike Fude Temple
spots.desc: A small temple to the Lord of the Soil and the Ground (土地公), a Chinese folk deity.

spots.name: Sika Deer Ecological Park
spots.desc: A recreational area established around the Sika deer which used to be farmed on the island and were released when the industry was no longer sustainable. There are activities related to the deer, and a paintball area.

spots.name: Zhu Dayu Culture Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to marine life and fisheries in the area.

spots.name: Jinan Temple
spots.desc: The oldest temple in the area which is dedicated to the god of Fujian province, which is where most of the settlers who built the temple originated.

spots.name: Taiwan Theater Museum
spots.desc: The museum is dedicated to Taiwan's theatrical arts and operas. It is the first public theater museum in Taiwan and the first museum established in Yilan County. The museum periodically hosts live Taiwanese opera and puppet shows as well as other cultural activities.

spots.name: Sanchong Airforce Village No1
spots.desc: A former residential village for member of the Taiwanese air force and anti-air batallions that has been granted heritage status and is now open to the public.

spots.name: Yu Youren's Tomb
spots.desc: A monument to the educator, scholar, calligrapher, and politician Yu Youren.

spots.name: Longshan Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1858, it is one of many temples dotted around Taiwan which share the name "Longshan".

spots.name: Yinshan Temple

spots.name: Wulai Atayal Museum

spots.name: Wulai Forestry Life Museum
spots.desc: The museum used to be the Wulai Tram Museum, but now focuses on forestry.

spots.name: Nanshan Fude Temple
spots.desc: An ornate temple complex that looks good during the day, or illuminated at night.

spots.name: Taipei Extreme Sports Training Center

spots.desc: A sportsground for skateboarding and other more 'extreme' sports.

spots.name: Taipei Water Park
spots.desc: The park is built around the Museum of Drinking Water, housed in the former pumping station building and showcasing some of the machinery used to provide water to the city. Many facilities are all about water. The most popular are water slides and swimming spas. But the facilities are open only in summer (entry included with the museum ticket)

spots.name: Courbet Memorial
spots.desc: A memorial to the French admiral Amédée Courbet who was involved in several naval engagements between France and China in 1885.

spots.name: Ziwei Palace

spots.name: Coral Museum

spots.name: Yixian Park

spots.desc: Built in 1928, the series of 16 barns was constructed to store and process rice from around the colony. The architectural style incorporates high windows which dissipated heat without allowing moisture to enter and cause the rice to spoil or ferment.

spots.name: Yongjing Koxinga Temple
spots.desc: A park with a temple dedicated to the famous admiral Koxinga. The park contains a number of playgrounds, exercise equipment, and decommissioned military hardware.

spots.name: Zhunan Wugu Temple
spots.desc: A temple dedicated to the Shennong Emperor which features a large red statue of the aforementioned deity atop the temple roof.

spots.name: General Chen Temple
spots.desc: A temple which, according to local legend, was constructed in honour of a rich local man who used his own resources to provide food to the people during a famine, but was later accused of extortion and beheaded by the local elite.

spots.name: Caotun Longde Temple
spots.desc: A large temple complex that was built in 1793, during the Qing dynasty.

spots.name: Caotun Night Market
spots.desc: The night market sells various delicacies in their food stalls.

spots.name: Wushe Incident Memorial Park
spots.desc: A memorial erected to commemorate members of the Seediq indigenous group who were massacred by the Japanese colonial government in the 1930s.

spots.name: Matai'an Wetland Ecological Park
spots.desc: This is a beautiful area with a lot to offer those who are willing to spend a little time exploring and walking or biking around. The wetland is located at the foot of Mount Masi and spans over an area of 12 hectares, making it the largest wetland in the county. The wetland consists of around 100 types of water plants.

spots.name: Danongdafu Forest Park
spots.local: 大農大富平地森林園區
spots.desc: The forest consists of various outdoor sculptures and statues depicting the culture of Taiwanese indigenous peoples as well as over a million trees with almost 20 different types commonly found at low altitude. It was developed from reclaimed agricultural land.

spots.name: Ruisui Tropic of Cancer Marker
spots.desc: A monument marking the Tropic of Cancer. The monument was built in 1933 west of Ruisui Railway Station. Due to the Hualien–Taitung line tracks replacement work carried out in 1981, the monument was relocated to Wuhe Terrace and placed along the Provincial Highway 9.

spots.name: Tianxiang
spots.desc: The final village inside of Taroko Gorge most tourists will encounter.

spots.name: Stone Umbrella

spots.local: 悟饕池上飯包文化故事館

spots.name: Sietian Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1804, IT is the oldest and largest Kuankung Temple in Northern Taiwan.

spots.name: Luodong Confucian Temple
spots.desc: The local Confucian temple which includes the temple building and is surrounded by an area of ponds and gardens.

spots.name: Toucheng Leisure Farm
spots.desc: A farmhouse with accommodation for 500 guests where visitors can learn about farming and ecology.

spots.name: Jim and Dad's Brewing Company
spots.desc: The brewery was opened in September 2015 after the founder won a brewing competition. The ground floor hosts the tasting area. It features a restaurant, outdoor playground and an observation tower.

spots.name: Yixiantian Cliff
spots.desc: Erosion has created a narrow pass between two rock faces, leading to the Chinese name which roughly translates as "a thread of sky".

spots.name: Wu Tien Yow Memorial
spots.desc: A monument erected to a Confuician scholar who ran a medicine shop in the area and later donated the land for a school to be built.

spots.name: Jingtong Mining Industry Museum
spots.desc: The ground floor of the museum displays permanent exhibitions on the landscape of Pingxi Township and the development of coal mining industries in the area. The upper floor of the museum displays artifacts related to coal mining activities and the local culture. The museum building was originally the dormitory of Taiwan Railways Administration employees. In 2001, the building underwent renovation…

spots.name: Fufudingshan Shell and Coral Temple

spots.name: Turtle Temple
spots.desc: A temple at the foot of the Bilong mountain, it is named after the 'Green Turtle Stone' which is contained within the temple complex.

spots.name: Dongjiyu Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse with a height of 24.4 meters, built in 1911 by the Japanese during the times of the Japanese colonial empire.

spots.name: Blue Cave

spots.name: Hua-Zhai Old-Style Historical Houses
spots.desc: A series of old, one-story stone houses which often feature colourful painted rooves.

spots.name: Tuku Story House

spots.name: Tuku First Market

spots.desc: An historic wooden market building where you can still pick up some local crafts.

spots.name: Cenotaph for Erjie Paper Factory

spots.name: Li Tien-lu Hand Puppet Historical Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the art of puppetry, which is still popular in Taiwan, mostly consisting of antique puppets which belonged to puppetier Li Tien-lu. There are also regular performances of Taiwanese puppetry here.

spots.name: Boar Ficus superba
spots.desc: An ancient banyan tree which worshippers believe is an incarnation of Baijie, the pig character from the famous tale Journey to the West.

spots.name: Fourteen Zhang Sixin Temple

spots.name: Former Dounan Police Precinct Building

spots.name: Huwei Sugar Factory

spots.desc: The city's main art gallery and performance space.

spots.name: Beishi River Historical Trail
spots.desc: The trail follows the paths along Beishi River for a distance of 2.6 km.

spots.name: Pingxi Historical Trail
spots.desc: The trail follows the paths along Pingxi River for a distance of 1.8 km.

spots.name: Beigang Cultural Center
spots.desc: The center showcases the cultural heritage of the local area.

spots.name: Yunlin County Stadium
spots.desc: A multi-use stadium that is able to hold 10,000 people.

spots.name: Old Houses of Yang
spots.desc: Similar to the Erkan Chan Residence, but less well managed, and therefore fewer other visitors.

spots.name: Hello Market
spots.desc: A big, old-fashioned outdoor market selling all manner of food, plus clothing and household goods. See the fish flopping out of their bins and frogs trying to escape from their bags.

spots.name: Anping Old Street
spots.desc: A street lined with stands selling snacks, drinks, souvenirs, and even medicinal herbs. Preserved plums (酸梅 suānméi) are a popular item. Other specialties include shrimp cakes and dried fruit.

spots.name: Taichung Winery
spots.desc: Dating back to the Japanese era, this still-operational winery also includes a wine museum, which has displays on wine-making and the history of the winery.

spots.name: Triangle Fortress
spots.desc: in Guning west of Zi lake (滋湖) to the north of Jincheng, overlooking the passage to Jincheng town between Kinmen and small Kinmen island, with a group of M41 tanks on display outside. The adjacent beach is a good place to see views of the Xiamen skyline, as well as the rows of steel spikes that the Nationalists lined the coast with to prevent an amphibious invasion. Line B tourist bus and bus 9.

spots.name: Lion Mountain
spots.desc: With an underground howitzer base and museum, in Shanhou in the northeast of Kinmen, near Shanhou Culture Village. Bus 31 from Shamei (沙美, bus 5 or 5A from Kincheng to Shamei)

spots.name: Military Brothel Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: A small museum detailing Kinmen's history of legalized brothels set up by the government for soldiers, many of whom were stranded on the island for the rest of their lives after retreating from Mainland China. Glosses over the darker aspects of the story, and is told largely from the point of view of the men, but still has some interesting information. Many, but not all, signs are in English as…

spots.name: Shuitou Deyue Tower
spots.desc: With the surrounding buildings, in Shuitou, previously the highest building in Kinmen, old buildings built by rich overseas Chinese merchants, including a Peranakan family, resulting in a complex of buildings with a mix of local and Western architecture. Line A tourist bus and bus 7/7A/7B

spots.name: Eighteen Peaks Mountain
spots.desc: best described as a large hill or small mountainous area circling the eastern and southern suburbs of Hsinchu. The highest of the 18 peaks is 131.79 m and the lowest 50 m. It has a lot of well-maintained stepways, concrete paths and Tarmac pathways, making it ideal for walks in the forest without the hardships of true country hiking. It can get very crowded at weekends or in the early morning…

spots.name: Hsinchu Botanical Garden
spots.desc: has some great hiking trails and provides the opportunity to become acquainted with more than 300 varieties of Taiwan's indigeneous flora.

spots.name: Green Grass Lake
spots.desc: Also called Qing-cao Hu, off Ming-hu Road is a parkland surrounding a lake - a great place to relax and watch water fowl gliding with the clouds.

spots.name: Hsinchu Zoo
spots.desc: This is the oldest and smallest zoo in Taiwan, founded by the Japanese in 1936. The zoo has been very tastefully renovated and proudly displays 250 animals and 70 species, including tigers, crocodiles, monkeys, bears and all kinds of birds. The grounds are lovely and garden like and the animals seem to be having a good time. A great place to bring children.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 08:30 to 17:00 all year, closed on Chinese New Year's Eve

spots.name: City God Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1748, on the corner of Zhongshan Road and Dongmen Street. It is a typical Taoist temple with lots of colorful frescoes.

spots.name: Guan Di Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1776, on the corner of Wenchang St. and Zhongshan Road. It is noted for its refined ornamentation and inscriptions carved by local scholars on the temple pillars.

spots.name: East Gate
spots.desc: Constructed from granite and with a distinctive arched entrance, the historic East Gate is the city center's most well known landmark. It is at the junction of Dongmen and Zhongzheng Roads.

spots.name: Craft Glass Museum
spots.local: 新竹市玻璃工藝博物館
spots.desc: The, sec 1. A gallery dedicated to Hsinchu's long association with the craft of glass making. It is in the park directly behind the railway station.
spots.addr: No.2, Sec. 2, Dongda Rd., East Dist

spots.name: Hsinchu City Fire Museum
spots.desc: A small museum in a converted fire station dedicated to the history of firefighting in Taiwan.

spots.name: Image Museum of Hsinchu City
spots.desc: The museum is in the renovated former movie theater building, and in addition to images and documents of film and theater in Taiwan, the museum also has an auditorium where movies and plays are performed.

spots.name: Hsinchu City Black Bat Squadron Memorial Hall
spots.local: 黑蝙蝠中隊文物紀念館
spots.desc: A memorial dedicated to those who lost their lives in the conflict between Taiwan and Mainland China.

spots.name: Hsinchu Playhouse and Gallery
spots.desc: Sec 2 (corner of Beida Road). A large concert hall and gallery featuring local and international events.

spots.name: Kanziding Fish Market (Kanzihding)
spots.desc: The oldest continuously operated and largest fishery distribution center in Northern Taiwan.

spots.name: Zhongzheng Park
spots.desc: This white 22.5-m-high statue of Guanyin (the Buddhist emanation of compassion and peace) overlooks the town and harbor entrance from the top of Zhongzheng Park.

spots.name: Keelung French Cemetery
spots.desc: A remnant of the Sino-French War of 1884-85, it is about 2 km from the train station, but still very close to the harbor.

spots.name: Keelung Islet
spots.desc: An easy-to-find islet outside Keelung City. You can see the islet from Keelung, the north coast or northeastern coast, which makes it an important landmark of Keelung.

spots.name: Heping (Hoping) Island
spots.desc: It used to be called She-liao Island. It is the doorway island to Keelung Harbor. It was a main fort built by Spanish in 1626. Inside the park, you can see many eroded rocks and coasts have formed special shapes by the wind and sea. There is a Bridge connects the island to Keelung City, and you can also take bus 101 at Keelung Railway Station, get off at Hoping Island station and walk for about 5…

spots.name: Yong Heng Creative Park
spots.desc: A scenic outdoor art park. In 2013, they transformed the mountainside into several large drawings of a panda, duck, and several smaller figures created using thousands of colored wind spinners,

spots.name: National Museum of Marine Science and Technology
spots.desc: Kid-friendly marine science museum with exhibition galleries housed in a former power plant, an IMAX theatre, and several educational trails in the adjoining seaside park.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, closed Mondays and Lunar New Year's Eve
spots.price: NT$200 adults (main exhibition only, IMAX theatre NT$150 extra)

spots.name: Shihciouling Fort
spots.desc: Built in 1884, this fort was constructed to enhance coast defense when the French attacked Taiwan for the Vietnam problem. Shihciouling is the highest fort among all the forts in Keelung. It is an essential place for the defense of the harbor. The fort was made with solid mountain rocks and the structure was kept well. It is important because it is the only remaining small fort built in late…

spots.name: Waimu Shan seashore
spots.local: 外木山情人湖濱海大道
spots.desc: the longest natural seashore remained in Keelung City with a total of 5 kilometers from Waimu Shan Fishery Harbor to Aoditong Village. The seashore includes open seashore and marine cliff to make a spectacular scenery. Swimming facilities are available near Waimu Shan Fishery Harbor for experienced swimmers to go scuba diving and swimming. The beach near Aoditong Village is the only remaining…

spots.name: Lovers Lake
spots.desc: located at the mountainside of Mount Dawulun at the western part of Keelung. It is the only highland in Keelung with dense woods, beautiful lake and refreshing scenery. The park offers different facilities including kiosks, suspension bridge, observation platform, windmills and pathways for visitors to take a walk and enjoy the natural scenery, the beauty of plants and green shower. It is also a…

spots.name: Lee Hu Pastry Shop
spots.desc: In business since 1882, it is the most famous traditional pastry shop in Taiwan.

spots.name: 35 Yuhuo Fish Market
spots.desc: Excellent fresh seafood, the boats dock nearby. You choose the fish, they cook it for you.

spots.name: Dharma Drum Mountain
spots.desc: A large and modern chan monastery and monastic college. Impressive buildings and gardens.
spots.addr: No. 14-5, Lin 7, Sanjie Village, Jinshan district (金山區)

spots.name: Ju Ming Museum
spots.local: Zhū Míng Měishùguǎn - 朱銘美術館
spots.desc: A museum with indoor and open air exhibits of the works of the Taiwanese sculptor Ju Ming.
spots.addr: No.2, Xishihu Road, Jinshan district (金山區)

spots.name: National Immigration Agency
spots.desc: Visa applications/extensions for foreign residents of New Taipei City should be made at this agency.

spots.name: Yangmingshan National Park
spots.desc: A favourite destination, particularly during spring when thousands of calla lilies, peonies and cherry blossoms bloom in the valleys. Besides that public hot springs, as well as hot sulphur blow holes and sources are equally worth the visit. There are dozens of hiking trails in the park, most marked out on maps from the visitors centre. Qixingshan is the highest peak in Yangmingshan, and looks…

spots.name: Eslite
spots.desc: (誠品) – Eslite offers a good selection at most of their branches, although the 24 hour flagship store (2F, 245 Dunhua South Rd. has the best selection. Eslite Book Store and shopping mall (11 Songgau Road), which incidentally is the largest book store in Taiwan, have the greatest selection. The Songgau Rd branch is next to MRT Station 'Taipei City Hall'.

spots.name: Lai Lai
spots.desc: This shop has a small but interesting selection of English material.

spots.name: Crane Publishing Company
spots.desc: Specialists in English language textbooks and teaching material.
spots.addr: 200 Section 2, Jinshan S Rd, Da’an District

spots.name: Bookman Books
spots.desc: This is an excellent collection of English literature books, albeit a little expensive.

spots.name: Dasi CKS Residence
spots.desc: Built in Japanese colonial time. President Chiang used it a residence. King Hussein of Jordan stayed here with President Chiang before.

spots.name: Window on China Theme Park
spots.desc: One of Taiwan's earliest theme parks. A small-scale replica of many famous landmarks (mostly Asian) and a small amusement park - south of Longtan, next to Aspire Technology Park.

spots.name: Lala Shan Nature Reserve
spots.desc: Lalashan is one of natural protection zones in Taiwan. There are 500– to 2800-year-old divine trees and the No.5 divine tree is older than Confucius.

spots.name: Fugang Village
spots.desc: A Hakka village in Yangmei Township noted for its traditional dwellings.

spots.name: Zhongli Xinming Night Market
spots.desc: One of the largest night markets in the Taoyuan area, it's possible to have a full dinner's worth of food on a very tight budget. Add to that a number of stalls selling trinkets (albeit cheap ones) and the sights and sounds of fairground style amusement games, the market makes an ideal way to spend an evening and understand this key part of Taiwan culture. There are additional nightmarkets in the…
spots.addr: Between Xinming Rd and Zhongyang West Rd, Zhongli, Taoyuan

spots.name: Tigerhead mountain
spots.desc: A popular spot for first dates and also has well-maintained hiking trails. Watch out for snakes if you're hiking. There are a few snack shops at the top of the mountain.

spots.name: Decor House
spots.desc: Serves as a one stop shopping center for multiple furniture stores under one roof. Ideal for 'travelers' staying long term and need furniture, appliances and/or housewares to furnish where they are staying. There are other stores and restaurants that are an interest to other travelers passing by such as Mos Burger, Starbucks, Poya, Sushi Express, My Steak House (我家牛排), Farmers Market (鮮綠市集)…
spots.addr: No.1, Zhong Zhen Rd, Luzhu District

spots.name: MetroWalk Shopping Center
spots.desc: Eslite Bookstore, H&M, Gallery M, SBC International Cinemas, Muji, Uni Qlo, Zara and many smaller stores and restaurants on multiple stories, under one roof in Zhongli District.
spots.addr: No.501, Section 2, Zhongyuan Rd, Zhongli District

spots.name: TaiMall
spots.desc: One of the largest malls in Taiwan, off Nankan Rd, towardss the northern part of Luzhu.
spots.addr: No.112, Section 1, Nankan Rd, Luzhu District

spots.name: Tonlin Plaza
spots.desc: Streamlined multi-story mall, in a city block, with trendy stores for fashion & beauty products, Eslite Bookstore, plus diverse eateries within. Densely packed 'downtown' area with eateries/restaurants and shops surrounding the mall. Bus stops for multiple bus routes along north side of mall on Zhong Hua Rd.
spots.addr: No.61, Zong Zhen Rd, Taoyuan District

spots.name: Costco Taoyuan-Nankan
spots.desc: Costco is the largest membership warehouse club chain in the United States in the Luzhu District.
spots.addr: No.369, Section 1, Nankan Rd, Luzhu District

spots.name: Costco Taoyuan-Zhongli
spots.desc: Costco is the largest membership warehouse club chain in the United States in the Zhongli.
spots.addr: No.86–1, Lane 576, Section 6, Minzu Rd, Zhongli District

spots.name: Bistrot Latini
spots.desc: Latini offers simple but well-cooked Italian food. The owner and head chef, Dan Wu, speaks English and is very helpful and friendly. Try the pumpkin soup and panini. Also offers a good selection of fancy coffees, including espresso with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

spots.name: Cong dra bing
spots.desc: Pronounced tsong draw bing, it is a scallion pancake that the vendor cooks on a griddle and fluffs up before searing on scrambled egg and a variety of toppings like bacon and fresh basil. The traditional sauce they put on top is soy-based, but you can ask for spicy. Absolutely delicious. Usually a daytime snack, sold on the side of the street by SK II downtown or by Nova computer store.

spots.name: Carrefour
spots.desc: In addition to the obvious groceries, this French-owned grocery store has a food court on the top floor with good options. Sushi express, 8 things (Japanese with 7 small side dishes), a Thai restaurant, Meet Fresh, McDonald's and several noodle soup and fried chicken places.

spots.name: Frank's Texas BBQ
spots.desc: An American-style grill specialising in steaks, also provides soft drinks, draught beer and wines. The interiors are nicely decorated in the theme you would expect from a Texan BBQ.
spots.addr: No. 249-1, Section 2 Rui'an Road, Daxi Township

spots.name: Ciao-Lyon
spots.desc: A restaurant serving surprisingly good French cuisine (as well as a pasta option or two) in this out-of-the-way location in Daxi. There is either a full set menu or à la carte (soup, main & drink) to choose from as well as a decent wine list. The interiors are simple but comfortable, and the staff extremely helpful.
spots.addr: No. 200, Section 1, Buding Road, Daxi Township

spots.name: The 3 Baboons Sports Bar & Grill
spots.desc: Restaurant featuring western cuisine, beer, wine, cocktails, and a large screen satellite TV for international sports. Foosball and pool table available. 10 minutes from Taoyuan International Airport in Taimall Shopping Center.
spots.addr: Taimall Shopping Center, 112 Nankan Rd, Sec 1. Luchu Hsieng

spots.name: 7Yunnan
spots.desc: A small restaurant chain local to Taoyuan City providing a vast range of Yunnan cuisine (somewhat like a mixture between Thai and Chinese), very affordable and good interiors. Most staff do not speak English, but all of the menus have pictures.

spots.name: Craftsman Chinese Restaurant
spots.desc: Nice restaurant. Photo menu. From Watsons, head towards the McDonald's staying on the same side of the street. English sign.

spots.name: The Jalapeno
spots.desc: A Mexican-themed bar around the corner from the Zhongli Night market, serving Mexican food best categorised as greasy bar food. Jack the owner makes the bar what it is, a fun place to spend an evening. Jack and many of his staff speak English, and the place is often frequented by expats and western visitors.

spots.name: Cowboy Hat
spots.desc: A bar on the second floor of a building overlooking the Tourist Pond. Very nice view, ok ambiance and price.

spots.name: The Elephant
spots.desc: Jungle-themed bar. Best patio in town. Good beer and ambiance.

spots.name: O Ya Cafe
spots.desc: Assorted food and cafe items. Walk along Wufu St, away from the day market. It'll be across from the giant Hess building. English menu.

spots.name: Cijin Coast Park
spots.desc: The Cijin Seaside Park is a long area of picturesque terrain along the west coast of Cijin Island. Take a leisurely stroll or cycle past intriguing architectural designs with a constant view of the Taiwan Strait. The park incorporates a long path for walking and cycling as well as an ecological area and Cijin Beach.
spots.addr: No. 990 Qijin Third Road, Qijin District

spots.name: TianHou Temple
spots.desc: Chihou area is the area in Kaohsiung where many fishermen live. This temple was built about three hundreds years ago and dedicated to the Goddess of Sailors, Matzu. People believe that Matzu can protect every fisherman who is going to sea. The temple is crafted with charming yet authentic folk art. TianHou temple is also regarded as the oldest temple in Kaohsiung.

spots.name: Lotus Lake
spots.desc: Take a walk or bike around Lotus Lake. The lake is surrounded by temples, some of which have built out onto the lake. Of note are the Dragon-Tiger Pavilion and Spring Autumn Pavilion, as well as Taiwan's largest Confucius temple. During the day the lake is surrounded with stalls selling food, drinks and trinkets. Across the street from the Dragon-Tiger Pavilion is a Taiwanese puppet shop that's…

spots.name: Pei Chi Pavilion
spots.desc: This large statue of Beiji sits on Lotus Lake. The plank connecting the statue to the shore is lined with a series of beautiful sculptures of animals. The statue is hollow and contains a temple within. Although relatively modern, this statue is colorful, colossal, and well worth a visit.
spots.addr: On Lotus Lake in Zuoying District

spots.name: Spring & Autumn Pavilions
spots.desc: This Taoist temple complex contains a large dragon that you can enter. The inside of the dragon is beautifully painted with murals. Once you are done sightseeing within the dragon, you can exit out its opposite end. The nearby Dragon-Tiger Pavilion is also worth seeing, and features two pagodas you can visit as well.
spots.addr: On Lotus Lake in Zuoying District

spots.name: The British Consulate
spots.desc: Sitting atop a hill, the red brick building offers beautiful views over the Kaohsiung harbor and the sea. While a nice structure representative of the era in which it was built, it is now thought to have been the official residence of the British Consul, and not the consulate proper.

spots.name: Syongjhen North Gate
spots.desc: This fort is built by the Qing dynasty to protect the harbor. It underwent renovation during 2018 and re-opened to the public in 2022. A small and quiet place to enjoy views of the sea and Cijin lighthouse. Nearby is the Former British Consulate, which sits right in front of the bus stop. From here, you can descend to the observatory deck of Sizihwan beach.

spots.name: The Takao Railway Museum
spots.desc: Turned into a museum in 2010, this was Kaohsiung's first railway station. There are exhibition rooms, a railway document archive and a platform and track area.

spots.name: Shoushan
spots.desc: Also known as Chaishan (柴山), this mountain sits at the westernmost point of Gushan, and boasts scenic view of the sea, the city, or both, depending on your location. It is full of macaque monkeys that is very sneaky and cheeky, so make sure to keep your food and drinks away. As a side note, try not to store them in plastic bags because the sound of plastic bags reminds them of food. There are…

spots.name: Sihzihwan Beach
spots.desc: A curved beach south of Shoushan, developed as a tourist attraction since Japanese colonial times. You can get beautiful views of Shoushan and the red-brick university buildings that perched right next to it. The beach comes with a parking space for bikes, scooters and cars (parking fees apply per use), and on the other side of the carpark is a concrete barrier that has become a ledge for people…

spots.name: The Pier-2 Art Center
spots.desc: The centre occupies several warehouses that were artfully converted into exhibition space and cafes. Many contemporary art exhibitions are held there, as well as occasional live music events. It is on the bicycle path that borders the harbor front.

spots.name: The Dome of Light
spots.local: 光之穹頂 / Guāng zhī qióngdǐng
spots.desc: A public artwork in the concourse area of Formosa Boulevard station. Created by Italian artist Narcissus Quagliata, it is the world's largest stained glass installation. The dome is divided into four sections: water, earth, light and fire. It also takes the form of a yin and yang symbol. An audio guide (available in several languages) can be borrowed from the KRTC Art Shop inside the station. It…

spots.name: Central Park
spots.desc: The park has a small hedge maze in the middle, a pond with some bridges and fish, clay tennis courts, and "Urban Spotlight," a café with a stage to display local talent.

spots.name: Dream Mall
spots.local: 夢時代購物中心 / Mèng shídài gòuwù zhòng xīn
spots.desc: A large mall that is a bit out of the way, but worth it to visit the Hello Kitty Ferris Wheel on the roof.

spots.name: National Science and Technology Museum
spots.desc: An enormous science museum, one of Asia's largest. It can easily keep kids entertained for a day.
spots.price: NT$100 adults, NT$70 students with ID

spots.name: Fishermen's Wharf / Banana Pier
spots.desc: This tourist area features a number of restaurants with live performers and seaside seating. There is also a free exhibit within Banana Pier about Taiwan's banana industry.

spots.name: i-Ride Experience Center
spots.desc: Panoramic flying attraction in Kaohsiung Software Technology Park. The ride brings you an amazing soaring experience across the Kaohsiung skyline with immersive 4D effect.

spots.name: Kaohsiung Lantern Festival
spots.desc: At the end of Chinese New Year, near the Kaohsiung harbour and along the Love River, the Kaohsiung Lantern Festival is filled with a variety traditional lanterns and more modern light sculptures, nightly fireworks shows, Taiwanese food stands and other art programs and live concerts.

spots.name: Urban Spotlight
spots.desc: Located at the corner of Central Park, Urban Spotlight is a cafe with a stage where local live bands perform in the evening. Take a walk around Central Park then stop at the cafe to cool off.

spots.name: Night Markets
spots.desc: Food, games, and shopping. Try the Liuho Night Market, which is a tourist market. Ruifeng night market, at the corner of YuCheng and Nanping, heaves with locals. Closed Mondays and Wednesdays.

spots.name: Jiu Pin Xiang Vegetarian
spots.desc: A chain of small vegetarian buffet restaurants with a delicious variety of mock meats, tofu, and vegetables. Tell the cashier if you want rice.

spots.name: Michino Diner
spots.local: Michino Diner米奇諾穿越食空美式餐廳大同總店
spots.desc: Serves popular breakfast and brunch. You can choose between burgers, sandwiches, salads, omelettes and real American breakfast and brunch.

spots.name: Sushi Express
spots.desc: Sushi train with good variety including healthy vegetarian options.

spots.name: Smokey Joes
spots.local: 冒煙的喬 高雄五福店
spots.desc: Serves Tex-Mex, including fajitas, tortillas and other Western staples at affordable prices (NT$170 and up). The menu is in English and the staff usually understands some English as well. They offer a 'VIP' card for people who spend over NT$1,000 on 20 separate meals which gives the holder at 10% discount at any store operated by Amy (the owner of Smokey Joes). This includes Mama Mia's, an…

spots.name: The Pantheon
spots.desc: Serves traditional Greek and Mediterranean food at good prices.
spots.price: Gyro lunch NT$200, 20% discount on takeout

spots.name: Cosplay Cafe
spots.desc: Offers a cosplay themed restaurant. 161, ChangMing St, SanMin District.

spots.name: Bull Fighter Restaurant
spots.desc: It mainly serves steaks and grilled seafoods and is suitable for most Western visitors at fair costs (NT$400-500 each, free salad bar included). Or, you can choose pastas (only NT$200, salad bar included).

spots.name: The Spice Shop
spots.desc: An Indian restaurant serving a-la-carte style meals, with each dish ranging from NT$120-270.

spots.name: 2 Coins Bar
spots.desc: 2 Coins Bar is a small bar down the street from the Lees Hotel. The bar owner is quite nice, but doesn't speak English. Good music and decent prices are standard for this relaxing bar.

spots.name: Shuang Fei Milk Tea
spots.desc: This outlet specializes in milk tea, and is a favorite shop for tourists to Kaohsiung. They have an English menu.

spots.name: Ou-jia Yin-pin
spots.desc: Located on the intersection, it is the first shop you see if you come out from Yanchengpu MRT Station Exit #2. They specialize in lotus tea, lotus milk tea, and milk tea made with lotus boba. Menu in Chinese only, but the owner is friendly and helpful, and will let you try out his drinks.

spots.name: Jiu-jiu Tea Shop
spots.desc: Milk tea shop specializes in white fungus flavored-drinks. Menu available in Chinese and English.

spots.name: Tianchi Donggua Tea
spots.desc: A traditional Taiwanese-style tea shop, specializing in winter melon (冬瓜, donggua) tea. Menu in Chinese only.

spots.name: Hua-da Milk Tea
spots.desc: Another famous milk tea shop which has operated for over 40 years. Since then it has expanded into a franchise with outlets all across Taiwan, but the Sinle Street shop remains its HQ. Menu available in Chinese, English, and Japanese. You can try out their signature milk tea, Pu-er milk tea, or Oolong milk tea.
spots.price: NT$60 each, NT$5 to add boba

spots.name: Chimei Museum
spots.desc: Started by a private collector who has a vast collection of violins, many of them antique in nature and made by masters like Antonio Stradivari and Nicolo Amati. There's also various exhibits about Western art, weaponry and natural history. The building and surrounding park are astonishing in their incongruence and could have been transported entirely from classical Europe.

spots.name: Ten Drum Culture Village
spots.desc: A former sugar factory that has been taken over by a troupe that puts on new age performances using traditional Chinese drums.

spots.name: Caoshan Moon World
spots.desc: An interesting region of mud hills and badlands surrounded by thick bamboo forest and some tropical fruit farms.

spots.name: Tainan Park
spots.desc: Beautiful park in a central part of the city. Great for a relaxing walk or a stay of a few hours. It has many beautiful trees, flowers and a pond.

spots.name: Uni-President Lions Baseball
spots.desc: Baseball games in Taiwan are lively and light-hearted with a lot of chanting and cheering in unison. Beer and barbecues are even allowed in the bleachers. Stadiums are divided into home and away crowd, infield or outfield. Wear green and orange to blend in with the home crowd. The team does travel between stadiums for games, so check the CPBL schedule. The season runs from March to June and July…

spots.name: Sicao Lushe Tunnel
spots.local: Sicao Green Tunnel; 四草綠色隧道
spots.desc: Found in Taijiang National Park, there are two boat rides to observe the marine life and migrant birds of a mangrove swamp reserve. The rare black-faced spoonbill can be seen here. The shorter route takes about 30 minutes, while the longer one is about 70 minutes. Queues are roughly the same time as the boat rides, and weekday boat schedules only run a few times per day.

spots.name: Yanshui Beehive Fireworks Festival
spots.desc: Meant to chase off evil spirits, fireworks are piled into a structure resembling a beehive and set off at street level, which makes it a racuous celebration that requires full-face helmets and fire-retardant jackets for participation.
spots.hours: 15th day of the first lunar month
spots.addr: 87 Wumiao Rd., Yanshui Dist., Tainan City

spots.name: Far-East Department Store
spots.local: 遠東百貨 台南公園店
spots.desc: The department store focuses more on midrange consumers. Downstairs food-court offers good selection of restaurants and Hong Kong-based supermarket Wellcome.

spots.name: Hayashi Department Store
spots.desc: Taiwan's oldest department store. On its opening in 1932, the building boasted a then state-of-the-art elevator, which still works. It was bombed during World War II and still has bullet marks to show on the rooftop, next to its Shinto shrine. Located on what was once the richest shopping street in Tainan, the site fell into disuse following the defeat of Japan and the end of World War II until…

spots.name: Shinkong Mitsukoshi
spots.desc: The department store focuses on both high end products and mainstream fashion. Luxurious brands such as Chanel, Hermes, Ferragamo can be found in the department store. Men's fashion includes Calvin Klein, Hugo Boss, Polo Ralph Lauren, Nautica, Esprit and more. There's also a movie theater inside. Two food courts offer various Asian, western cuisine and fast food chains. There is also a newer…

spots.name: Garden Night Market
spots.desc: The biggest and most famous open-air night market, there are tons of food stalls and game booths set up in a gigantic parking lot. This market can get very busy (i.e. mosh pit busy) on some days.
spots.addr: Haian Road, Sec. 3, between Lixian Rd and Hewei Rd

spots.name: Da Dong Night Market
spots.local: 大東夜市 dà dōng yèshì
spots.desc: Very popular among the local university students, especially on Friday nights.

spots.name: Wu Sheng Night Market

spots.desc: While also popular for its food, this night market stands out for its carnival-style games.
spots.addr: Lane 69, Wusheng Road, West Central District

spots.name: Du Hsiao Yueh
spots.desc: A famous purveyor of dan zai mian (擔仔麵), also known as peddlers' noodles because it was made to be sold by fishermen on the roadside. It's a small dish of noodles in pork-shrimp broth, decorated with a single shrimp and delicately balanced with a dash of garlic on top. This is the original branch, and they have opened more stores elsewhere in the country, including one on Yongkang St in Taipei…

spots.name: A Xia Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant famous for its crab sticky rice (紅蟳米糕), often patronized by government officials and foreign dignitaries whenever they visit Tainan.
spots.addr: No. 7, Lane 84, Section 2, Zhongyi Road, West Central District

spots.name: SongChun
spots.desc: Famous purveyor of traditional Taiwanese braised meats. What makes them stand out from other braised meat shops in Taiwan is that they smoke their meats before stewing, giving it a unique smoky flavor. They have three other branches in Tainan and one branch in Taichung but this is the main branch, just a simple stall inside a wet market, where you can buy their meats still warm. Takeaways only
spots.addr: No. 40, Chenggong Rd, North District (inside Yamuliao Market)

spots.name: Bar TCRC
spots.desc: A bar hidden in a little side alley, but probably one of the busiest in Tainan. They don't have any menus, with drinks made on request, though the standard cocktails are happily made strong.

spots.name: Speakeasy Bar
spots.desc: This newest creation of renowned bar entrepreneur Shorty Wu is on the east side alley way of Chikan street lane 45. Reservations are almost mandatory as it is very popular. English-speaking staff. The 'Sampler' is a beautiful array of several of their famous cocktails. Why come here with so many cocktail bars around? The atmosphere is done perfectly. Good food also served.

spots.name: The Secret
spots.desc: What are the chances to have two of the best bars next to each other? This bar starts with a different but equally exceptional atmosphere that combines a lounge feel with a long bar that's great for meeting people, having an upscale London and izakaya Japan feel. Anyone traveling in a group of 3 or fewer that want to meet others would do well to come here, and for larger groups it is a great…
spots.addr: Next door to the Speakeasy Bar 700台南市中西區赤嵌街 45巷6號

spots.name: Yongfu Mansion
spots.desc: It's not Western because it is an almost near-replica on a famous bar in Shanghai, but that original place was in the French Concession and is styled as such. Unique and outstanding atmosphere that takes you back to 1920s expat life in the Pearl of the Orient. The other endeavor of Shorty Wu in Tainan, this bar captures both a cozy darkness and a light energy. Outstanding cocktails and…

spots.name: Dirty Roger
spots.desc: Excellent small bar. Used to be very hip, still very good. Every music imaginable.

spots.name: The Hangout Bar
spots.desc: Nice bar to relax, play pool and watch sports. They also have good burgers and steak, free public computer and WiFi.

spots.name: Tin Pan Alley
spots.desc: Great partly outdoor pub and bar near Tainan. Wonderful friendly owners and delicious food ranging from pizza to falafel.

spots.name: Zhu Zi Ci

spots.desc: A nice Canadian/Taiwanese owned pub beside temple.

spots.name: Siouguluan River Basin
spots.desc: Soak in the RueiSuei Hot Springs for an evening, then wake up in the morning and River Raft down the incredibly beautiful Siouguluan River basin down to Big Harbor, where you can then hop on a yacht at #96 Shi Ti Bay and head out whale and dolphin watching. The seafood in Shi Ti Harbor is the freshest in Taiwan, caught twice a day by local (mostly Aborigines) fishermen and delivered fresh to your…

spots.name: Mugua River Gorge
spots.desc: This collection of rivers, waterfalls and lakes are an excellent place to swim and see the rich diversity of ecosystems in Hualien County. Most easily accessed by organized tour, the Mugua river gorge is home to Liyu Lake, Emerald Valley, Zimu Waterfall, Rainbow Waterfall and the Miyawan river.

spots.name: The Former Residence of Kuo Tzu-Chiu
spots.desc: The former residence of Kuo Tzu-Chiu, a famous musician and teacher from the area.

spots.name: The Abode of Still Thoughts
spots.desc: This small Buddhist temple at the foot of Mount North Jialiwan is the original facility of the world-famous Tzu-zhi Buddhist foundation. In keeping with the foundation's ideals, the temple is very simple, and incorporates a Japanese-style garden. Information on Tzu-chi's international activities is also available at the temple.

spots.name: Yenpin Prefectural Temple
spots.desc: Established in the Qing Dynasty, this is the oldest temple in Hualien.

spots.name: International Stone Sculpture Festival
spots.desc: An annual event featuring stone carving skills from around the world.

spots.name: Farglory Ocean Park
spots.desc: Hualien's biggest man-made tourist attraction. As well as Ferris wheel and cable car, the park contains eight zones showing different aspects of marine life. Children, in particular, will have an enjoyable time but for the more adventurous or those wanting a more local experience, there are many places that are much cheaper and provide a better experience of Taiwan.

spots.name: Cafe Jade
spots.desc: A spacious and very pleasant art cafe offering regular live music and art exhibitions.

spots.name: Bon Appétit Cafe & Dining
spots.desc: Serves espresso, spaghetti, handmade waffles and other brunch items.

spots.name: Hualien Distillery
spots.desc: The distillery has a shop where you can buy locally made drinks.

spots.name: The Huge Statue of Matsu
spots.desc: Near the Matsu Temple in Matsu Village is a huge statue of the goddess. Follow directions for Matsu Park and drive up, up, up. Great views of China on a clear day. A bit far from the harbor, but impossible to miss once you get close.

spots.name: Fuxing Village (NiouJiao)
spots.desc: Fantastic village with stone houses build against the mountain on the sea. Can spend hours wandering. A highlight is the village's picturesque temple, featuring an unusual bright red facade and views of Beigan Island in the distance.

spots.name: Beipu Old Street
spots.desc: An old Hakka street featuring stores selling local delicacies.

spots.name: Neiwan Old Street
spots.desc: An old street selling a variety of local snacks and delicacies.

spots.name: 6 Garden Restaurant
spots.desc: A 2-storey, vine-covered brick building nestled in the hills surrounded by gardens.

spots.name: Chiayi City Cultural Square
spots.desc: A complex containing a number of arts-related buildings and institutions.

spots.name: Chiayi Performing Arts Center
spots.desc: A multi-arts park space with performance halls and galleries.

spots.name: Fountain Turkey Rice
spots.desc: One of the most popular turkey rice joints in town, with a number of franchises. But the shop on Culture Road, around the corner, is the most famous -- and crowded.

spots.name: Chiayi East Market
spots.desc: A local market of fresh produce with a number of cooked food stalls.

spots.name: Chia-Le-Fu Night Market
spots.desc: Also called the Carrefour Night Market, situated along Bo Ai Rd near the Carrefour store offers a tasty variety of Taiwanese food dishes, and you can sometimes spot foreigners busking, juggling, miming, or selling their Chinese-language books there. The barbeque stall at the entrance is a must-try, as is almost every other stall in the market. The night market spans over an area of 1,800m2 and…
spots.addr: No. 467, Section 2, Bo'ai Road, West District

spots.name: Cha-no-Michi
spots.desc: Pleasant little modern tea shop right next to the Zhongshan Rd bus terminal, offering up a vast range of yummy Taiwanese drinks like milk tea with pudding chunks (布丁奶茶) and more traditional fruit juices.

spots.name: Orange Town Shake
spots.desc: A tea shop nearby the Beixianghu park and the botanical garden with a wide offering of drinks, e.g. Taiwanese boba tea. What sets this place apart is the very friendly, enthusiatic and helpful staff.

spots.desc: European restaurant with European prices.

spots.desc: Popular with many foreigners in Hualien.

spots.desc: A free museum housed in a 1960s Catholic church building.

spots.desc: The city's main athletics stadium.
