spots.name: Chiayi City Music Hall
spots.local: 嘉義市政府文化局音樂廳

spots.name: Shakadang Trail
spots.desc: 4.1 km, 3- to 4-hr round trip. Shakadang Trail is also known as "Mysterious Valley Trail", which is named because more than 40 years ago a group of young folks entered the river valley and found it very secretive. This place has attracted more and more travellers, and thus everyone is used to calling it "Mysterious Valley". However, its name was reverted to "Shakadang Trail" in 2001, according to…

spots.name: Cave of Water Curtains / Baiyang Trail
spots.desc: An easy 2.1-km trail, 2-hr round trip. Named for the cave at the end of the trail, where water literally pours down in sheets from the roof. Pack a poncho or use one discarded by other considerate hikers (or inconsiderate, depending on your point of view). Hiking to this point on the Baiyang Waterfall Trail takes you through many very long, completely unlit tunnels — an experience in and of…

spots.name: Zhuilu Old Trail
spots.desc: A strenuous hike that used to be part of an old cross-mountain trail through Taroko Gorge, starting near Swallows Grotto as it winds upwards through the green forest and coming out on a narrow cliffside path 700 m above the road but not more than a meter or two across. Not for anyone with fear of heights, but offers stunning views of the mountains on the other side of the gorge. Fortunately…
spots.price: NT$200, NT$100 for students; paid on arrival

spots.name: Xincheng Night Market
spots.desc: Definitely quieter than the popular night markets in Taipei, but still a lively enough place to get dinner, a snack, or a drink. Don't expect a lot of English.

spots.name: Qingshuiyan Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: A large area of forest area with a great deal of biodiversity. The area contains a number of hiking trails.

spots.name: Tianwei Highway Garden
spots.desc: A large botanical garden area with a variety of paths and cycle tracks.
spots.addr: No. 156, Section 1, Minzu Road, Tianwei Township

spots.name: Changhua Great Buddha Statue of Bagua Mountain
spots.desc: The main attractions in the scenic area include the Baguashan Great Buddha, the Anti-Japanese Martyrs Monument Park and the Healthy Trail etc. It is one of the “Eight Views of Changhua”. The statue of the Buddha was completed in 1961. The original site was the Palace of the Kitashirakawa Yoshihisa Prince, and it was 23 meters high. It is known as the largest Buddha in East Asia. Surrounded by…

spots.name: Changhua Wude Hall
spots.desc: Built in 1929 as a martial arts training centre, the building was converted to a 'martyr's shrine' after the end of the Japanese colonial period.

spots.name: Spring of Youth
spots.desc: Once one of the primary sources of water to the city, the building is now a monument to how the city's residents once lived.

spots.name: 1895 Baguashan Anti-Japanese Martyrs' Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the Battle of Baguashan, the pivotal battle of the 1895 Japanese invasion of Taiwan.
spots.addr: No. 500, Section 2, Zhongshan Rd (中山路二段500號)

spots.name: Confucian Temple of Changhua
spots.desc: The complex was constructed in 1726 with a temple and a school, although only the central structure remains.

spots.name: Kaihua Temple
spots.desc: It was built in 1724 as a temple to Guanyin. It has served many uses over the centuries and has been damaged and rebuilt several times during its history.

spots.name: Yuanching Temple
spots.desc: Constructed in 1763, it is perhaps the first temple in Taiwan to venerate the Jade Emperor.

spots.name: Nanyao Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1738 as a temple to Mazu, the structure has been added to since then.

spots.name: Changhua Papaya Milk King Founding Store
spots.local: 彰化木瓜牛乳大王創始店
spots.desc: Shaved ice and Papaya milk shop, they sell red bean soup in winter.

spots.name: Nantou Bamboo Museum
spots.desc: The museum has exhibitions related to bamboo, weaving, and other related industries.

spots.name: Taiwan Mochi Museum
spots.desc: There are a variety of mochi to learn about and to taste and many booths hand out free samples.

spots.name: Lantian Academy
spots.desc: A very old building which used to be used to train advisors to the government.

spots.name: Nantou Lychee Tree King
spots.desc: The oldest Lychee tree in Taiwan that is considered sacred by locals. Researchers from a local university have estimated the age of the trees to be between 270 and 472 years.

spots.name: Bald Pine Forest
spots.desc: A small pine forest that is good for a brief stroll through the trees, particularly in autumn when the colours are changing.

spots.name: Nantou County Stadium
spots.desc: The major sports venue for the city with a grandstand for those who wish to spectate.

spots.name: Nantou Market
spots.desc: A covered market selling a variety of food, homewares, and other items.

spots.name: Nantou Wednesday Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwan-style night market that runs every Wednesday night in the streets around the Carrefour.

spots.name: Elephant Steak House
spots.desc: A large steak house opened by the owner of Fala Steak House. Elephant Steak House is much larger and the prices even lower, making it very popular (it gets crowded sometimes) with people in Nantou. There is a buffet area with all-you-can-eat noodles, salad, fruits, etc.

spots.name: Fala Steak House
spots.desc: A classy western style steak house that has very fair prices and excellent quality food. There are four rounds to a typical meal, starting with salad, soup, the main course, and a dessert. Drinks are refillable and include sodas and tea, and there are snacks available for taking.

spots.name: Duofu Dohua
spots.desc: a sweets shop on Janguo Road which is just behind the County Gym Field. It's a franchised branch of a chain, but they make most of their products by themselves. Their Dohua (sweet soft beancurd) is made with much care and is very nice. They also provide many kinds of other desserts, kinds of shaved ice and drinks which are all cheap and worth the money you pay.

spots.name: Tianci Vegetarian
spots.desc: A small, cheap vegetarian restaurant nearby the sports stadium.

spots.name: A-bao
spots.desc: A breakfast restaurant service both western and Taiwanese fare.

spots.name: Nantou Winery
spots.desc: A winery and distillery where visitors can learn about the production process and pick up a bottle or two.

spots.name: Ci-en Pagoda
spots.desc: This Chinese style pagoda is a must and the best place to overview the lake. It's 46 m tall and was built by the Chiang Kai-shek in memory of his mother. It was completed in 1971 and sits on the hill southeast of the lake.

spots.name: Ita Thao
spots.desc: The village of the Thao Aborigines, and also called Dehua village (德化社). The boat shuttle between Suishe and Ita Thao goes twice an hour, takes 10 minutes and costs $100 per person.

spots.name: The Eternal Spring Shrine
spots.desc: The Changchun Shrine (Eternal Spring Shrine) recognizes the personnel who died during the construction of Central Cross-Island Highway. Rivers adjacent to the Changchun Shrine become the scattering falls, and the Highway Bureau named it after "Chanchun Falls" which is now the significant landmark on Central Cross-Island Highway. In 1987 the cliffs of the rivers destroyed the pavilion nearby the…
spots.hours: 2 km, 1-1.5 hr round trip. The shrine and its walkways are sometimes closed, due to (supposedly) Typhoons. It seems…

spots.name: Swallow Grotto
spots.desc: 1.37 km, 20 min. The Swallow Grotto is a short easy walk along very nice views of the gorge, finishing under the impressive Zhuliu cliffs. Kiosk with restrooms available halfway. Closed as of December 2019.

spots.name: Lushui Trail
spots.desc: 2 km, 1 hr. Great and picturesque view. Further down the road in addition a great view from the .

spots.name: Lushui-Heliu Trail
spots.desc: An easy 2-km, 45-min walk from the park office at Lushui to Heliu. Winds around short cliffs above the main road. Does pass through one dark tunnel, so bring a flashlight.

spots.name: Dali Datong Trail
spots.desc: The trail starts near the Visitor Center and goes up through a forest, offering expansive views of the area and the Liwu river. The trail is of medium difficulty, consisting of mainly stairs and dirt paths. Once arrived at the top, you will hit some restricted areas. It takes 10.6 km and 2-3 hr one way and 6-7 hr round trip.

spots.name: Sanjhan
spots.desc: River tracing is available from the community centre in the nearby town of Sanjhan. There is a community centre from which you can rent all relevant gear for about NT$500. However, if you want to rappel down waterfalls or do anything complicated, it is recommended that you contact a tour agency as the community centre of Sanjhan does not arrange tours.

spots.name: Tianxiang
spots.desc: There are a couple of options in the Silks Place Hotel in Tianxiang. The café there is reasonable for a snack and an air-conditioned break from the heat if you are so inclined, but prices are high. The restaurant proper is quite fancy and expensive. Just across the parking lot from the Hotel are some several reasonably cheap food stalls, and one very small grocery store. A few small restaurants…

spots.name: Shakadang Trail
spots.desc: Right before the Shakadong Trail turns into a wilderness trail (about 1.5 km), there are a few food stalls run by members of the Taroko tribe. The food's cooked fresh, tastes good, and is fairly priced for the location. Wild boar sausage and mochi with ground nuts are NT$40 each, and a can of apple juice is NT$30. Closed promptly at 16:30 in November.

spots.name: Jimavonot
spots.desc: A rock arch and rock pillar, sometimes associated with male and female anatomy. Hence known by names like Couple Rock, Ying and Yang Rock, Virgin/Maiden Rock, or more innocent names like Torch Rock. The Tao name Jimavonot means reed bundle.
spots.addr: Right next to the road in the north-east of the island, about 1 km east of Iraraley

spots.name: Datienchih
spots.desc: A lake inside the crater of a dormant volcano, covered in vegetation which feeds on the rich volcanic soil.

spots.name: Lion Couple Rock
spots.desc: A popular fishing spot, despite the dangers posed by the sharp rocks. The unique rock formation lies on the northern part of the island and faces out into the Pacific Ocean.

spots.name: Ye-Yin Old Tribe
spots.desc: A village consisting of a unique local architectural style, where the houses are built partially above and partially below ground.

spots.name: Rover
spots.desc: A seaside restaurant serving a variety of more international cuisine.

spots.name: 262 Bar
spots.desc: This outdoor restaurant serves a combination of local seafood specialities and local Taiwanese favourites.

spots.name: A Li Gei Breakfast Restaurant
spots.desc: A popular breakfast restaurant, just down the road from the airport.

spots.name: Taitung Culture and Tourism Center
spots.desc: Two buildings really, one houses the tourism center and library. The other has exhibition spaces, one of which houses the Aboriginal Artifacts Exhibition.

spots.name: Liyushan Park
spots.desc: With its trails and lookouts Liyu Shan offers a panoramic view of Taitung. Also, Long Feng Tower near the monastery gives a great panoramic view of the city.
spots.addr: Next to the old train station, on the southwest side of downtown

spots.name: Bombing of Master Han Dan
spots.desc: On the 15th of the first lunar month (right after Chinese New Year) is the Festival which in Taitung is played out with a unique and spectacular display known as the Bombing of Master Han Dan. In the course of this display a man wearing nothing more than a pair of shorts and a face mask stands upon a sedan chair while onlookers lob strings of lit firecrackers at him. It is unique to Taitung and a…
spots.addr: All over Taitung, but at night on Nanjing Rd

spots.name: Makapahay
spots.desc: Every mid-July several aboriginal groups, though of primary importance to the Amis, celebrate the millet harvest. This culminates in the long and colorful celebrations of dancing and merry making by Rukai, Paiwan, and Amis depending on which village or which part of the city you are in.
spots.addr: Throughout Taitung City, Taitung County, and the East Coast

spots.name: Taitung City Bikeway
spots.desc: Rent a bike at the beach (or bring your own) and bike the Taitung City Bikeway. The bikeway does a 32-km loop around the city. It follows the old train track out to near the new train station before heading back along the river eventually going through the Forest and Seashore Parks.

spots.name: Taitung Seashore Park
spots.desc: Taitung Seashore Park and the attached Taitung Forest Park are extremely popular with both locals and tourist alike. With miles of cycling and walking trails as well a beautiful and surprisingly undeveloped seashore these parks offers a perfect chance to experience Taitung's laid back lifestyle and clean ocean air. There are bicycles for rent at several places along the beach and at the entrance…
spots.addr: On the North and East sides of town

spots.name: Ata Aboriginal Culture Craft
spots.desc: Located in one of the buildings of a now defunct sugar factory this glass bead studio and handicraft center sells a variety of aboriginal handicrafts. Including textiles, leather work, and handmade glass beads. Since the Ata glass bead studio is located on site you can also watch glass beads being made.
spots.addr: Jhongsing Rd. 2nd Section 200th alley #7 (中興路2段200巷7號)

spots.name: Carrefour
spots.desc: This Taitung-sized hypermarket should cover you for most of your daily needs and provides the best selection of imported food and drinks in town.

spots.name: Eslite Bookstore
spots.desc: The largest bookstore in Taitung. If you want a book it is the best place to go.

spots.name: 陳記 'Mochi'
spots.desc: This unassuming little shop sells glutinous rice desserts that are as good or better than any of the more famous shops up the coast (and have been since the 1940s). It is quite popular with Taiwanese tourists.

spots.name: Seaweed Deli Dessert
spots.desc: A very popular and excellent quality noodle house; Offering a variety of fresh, healthy noodle dishes and dumplings in a friendly and clean environment.

spots.name: Mutton Barbecue
spots.desc: Proper goat, grilled, fried, as you want it. Highly recommended.

spots.name: Yun Jhan
spots.desc: This Puyuma restaurant offers a unique setting with dance performances and excellent aboriginal food. Best for groups so one should find some friends or family to accompany one and to share the taxi.

spots.name: Mibanai
spots.desc: This Amis restaurant located in the Malan section of town provides a taste of aboriginal food not too far from the center of the city. It is set up groups so once again bring friends or family.

spots.name: Denim Elephant
spots.desc: This artsy cafe has Taitung coffee as well as other coffee and teas and a small but interesting menu.

spots.name: cheela cafe
spots.desc: A very hip cafe with a modern artsy vibe that is conveniently located right on the bikeway and only a block away from the Taitung Theater. It serves a large range of coffees, teas, mixed drinks, and a fine assortment of Belgian beers. It serves daily freshly home-made bread by various products. Hot chili roll on Friday, hot brownie with ice cream on Saturday and cinnamon rolls on Sunday are the…

spots.name: Water Geothermal Square
spots.local: Chingshui Geothermal Field / 清水地熱
spots.desc: It is the largest geothermal area in Taiwan. The geothermal power comes in the form of hot springs. The spring is rich in sodium bicarbonate and its temperature is 95°C or above, which is too high for bathing. People can take advantage of the hot springs to boil eggs and other foods because the temperature is up to 95°C, higher than other hot springs. The foods boiled in hot spring water are…

spots.name: Wild Smoke
spots.desc: Yuan Shan. Good food and great views of Shuanglianpi - a lake near Fushan Botanical Garden. Caters to groups.

spots.name: Fenqihu Old Street
spots.desc: A small street with a number of old houses selling a range of take-away food and snacks.

spots.name: Tomb of Wang De Lu
spots.desc: The tomb of Wang De-lu, a soldier of the Qing dynasty. Because of his success as a soldier, he was ennobled by the imperial court, which also donated money for a lavish funeral and a huge tomb - the largest extant in Taiwan.

spots.name: Tree Spirit Pagoda
spots.desc: Although it is named the Tree Spirit Pagoda, it is actually a cenotaph. Japanese believe that trees have a divine spirit in the Kodama folklore.

spots.name: National Palace Museum, Southern Branch
spots.local: 國立故宮博物院南部院區
spots.desc: The southern branch of the National Palace Museum in Taipei, with a smaller collection than its counterpart, but beautifully presented in a modern building.
spots.price: NT$150 adults, free for visitors under 18

spots.name: Wanbei Fengshan Temple
spots.desc: Shuixian Temple was built in 1739 for residents to pray for the safety of the boatsmen, but later destroyed in a flood in 1803 and rebuilt in 1814. Shuixian Temple is dedicated to Shuixian Zunwang. The five figures (Yu the Great, Xiang Yu, Wu Zixu, Qu Yuan, and Lu Ban) are housed in the main hall, with Yu the Great in the middle. The front hall is dedicated to Mazu, while the rear hall is…

spots.name: Zhaoqing Buddhist Temple
spots.desc: A small, but storied Buddhist temple that has a strong link with Taiwan's Japanese colonial history.

spots.name: Ahou City Gate
spots.desc: A brick and cobblestone city gate built in the 19th century.

spots.name: Pingtung Night Market
spots.desc: The city's main night market, filled with a variety of stalls selling snacks and an assortment of small items.

spots.name: Central Traditional Market
spots.desc: A large, circular market building with stalls inside and around the outside. The market sells a variety of food and lifestyle necessities.

spots.name: Ruiguang Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwanese night market full of snacks and other assorted items.

spots.name: Taiwan Indigenous Peoples Cultural Park
spots.desc: The cultural park exhibits the lifestyle and cultural heritage of the nine main aboriginal tribes in Taiwan.

spots.name: Foen Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple that is striking in that it is painted entirely black.

spots.name: Shuangliu Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: The forest spans an area of 6½ km² at 175–650 m altitude featuring a number of hiking trails.

spots.name: Vase Rock
spots.desc: The 9-m tall rock was formed by the rising of the coastal coral reef.

spots.name: February 28 Incident Monument
spots.desc: A monument to the anti-government uprising in 1947 which sparked the decades-long White Terror in Taiwan.

spots.name: Wangkung Story Museum
spots.desc: A museum of local history and seafaring.

spots.name: Tianzhong Shushan Shrine
spots.addr: No. 435, Section 3, Dongmin Road, Tianzhong Township

spots.name: Beidou Riverside Park
spots.desc: A tranquil area of parkland beside a river.

spots.name: 1895 Taiwan Resistance Peace Memorial Park
spots.local: 乙未保臺和平紀念公園

spots.name: Nan Guan and Bei Guan Center
Yuan Ching Kaun Tradition Art Museum
Balloon House
spots.desc: Balloon specialty store.

spots.name: Shan Jiao Elementary School
spots.desc: An old Japanese-style schoolhouse.

spots.name: Houtanjing Recreation Area
spots.desc: An area picturesque parkland.

spots.name: Taiwan Governmental Golf Club
spots.local: 中華民國公教人員高爾夫研習會
spots.desc: A public golf course on the outskirts of the city.

spots.name: Wenwu Temple
spots.desc: The biggest temple on the northern bank of the lake.

spots.name: Tenshubar Black tea And Tea Liquor Tasting Laboratory
spots.local: 天首閣 紅茶．茶酒試驗所

spots.name: Dekalun Trail
spots.desc: 1.3 km, 3 hr. Challenging trail with lots of birds.

spots.name: Lushui-Wenshan Trail
spots.desc: 5.5 km, 5 hr.

spots.name: Ban Tian Hong
spots.desc: Spicy dishes.

spots.name: Lover Cave
spots.desc: A natural stone archway with association with young love.

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: One of the two 7-11 on the entire island.

spots.name: Yuziwu
spots.desc: Good, simple, home style Korean food.

spots.name: Minxiong Night Market
spots.addr: No. 5, Section 1, Jianguo Road, Minxiong Township

spots.name: Pingtung Martyrs' Shrine
spots.desc: A memorial dedicated to fallen soldiers erected in 1967.

spots.name: Pingtung Taiwanese Aborigines Museum
spots.local: 屏東縣政府原住民行政局原住民文化會館

spots.name: Pingtung Extreme Sports Ground
spots.desc: Despite the name, the area is largely a skating park.

spots.name: Zhongshan Huanghun Market
spots.desc: An indoor market selling a variety of food and homewares.

spots.name: Cycling the Dapeng Bay Bikeway
spots.desc: A cycling course that runs alongside the Dapeng lagoon.

spots.name: Patty's Outdoor Bar
spots.addr: No. 716-13 Heng Road, Hengchun Town, Pingtung County, Taiwan 946

spots.name: Peninsula • Four sets
spots.addr: No.114, Zhongshan Road, Hengchun Town, Pingtung County, Taiwan 946
