spots.addr: 1F, No. 114, Zhongshan Road, Hengchun Town, Pingtung County, Taiwan 946

spots.name: Button warehouse
spots.addr: No.12 Hengxi Road, Hengchun Town, Pingtung County, Taiwan 946

spots.name: Long Chill Bar
spots.addr: 142-2 Hengnan Road, Hengchun Town, Pingtung County, Taiwan 946

spots.name: Pekingese Dog
spots.desc: A rocky island only slightly offshore which is said to be in the shape of a Pekingese dog.

spots.name: Baiguoshan
spots.desc: An area of parkland with a shrine, with a fair number of stairs to climb to reach it.

spots.name: Dreamy Three Food Stalls
spots.desc: It's actually a row of three small, long-established food stalls. They offer inexpensive food, and serve very similar dishes. Locals collectively refer to them as the "Dreamy Three".

spots.name: Eight-Treasure Taro Ball Ice Dessert
spots.desc: Besides the classic Eight-Treasure Shaved Ice with Glutinous Rice Balls, this shop is best known for its grilled mochi, which comes in peanut, sesame, or mixed flavors.

spots.name: Toufen Old Village
spots.desc: An area of old red-brick style houses that has been partially preserved as a tourist attraction.

spots.name: Shangshun World
spots.desc: A large shopping centre that also has a number of small carnival-style amusements for children, such as bumper cars and a carousel.

spots.name: Little Carpenter Studio
spots.desc: A smaller 'western-style' restaurant serving ribs, chips, milkshakes, ice-cream, etc.

spots.name: Chung-tai Shan Monastery
spots.desc: 33 stories make it possibly the tallest Buddhist monastery in the world, and it is a landmark in the area and quite a sight from a few kilometres apart. Maybe find a hill nearby to fully capture it – it will be hard to put its size onto a picture standing right in front of it. Apparently, locals do not like the monastery too much, because the they demand money/donations for everything. But…

spots.name: Carp Lake
spots.desc: A great place to relax and watch clouds melt into green mountains and egrets dance in the cool summer breeze.

spots.name: Kuanghsing Paper Factory
spots.desc: Following ancient methods of production, this factory turns out a variety of hand made paper favored by calligraphers. This factory has a do-it-yourself lesson and participants can keep their own work as a souvenir.

spots.name: Lungnan Natural Lacquerware Museum
spots.desc: A memorial to Puli's historical connection with lacquerware. Demonstrations can be arranged.

spots.name: Tiger Head Mountain
spots.desc: At night, this little hill northeast of Puli centre gives a wonderful view over Puli and its "lightshow" inside the middle of the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Su MaMa Rice Ball
spots.desc: This place is highly recommended and a name in town. Speciality: meat filled rice balls, sweet rice balls, and ground pork noodles.

spots.name: Shrimp Fishing Court
spots.desc: Take a fishing rod, sit down, have a beer and hunt for shrimps in a large pool. This is great fun in a group.

spots.name: Bade Food Market
spots.desc: During the week when there is no night market, you could head for this food market of small stalls preparing food. However, the variety is not too large and you might prefer strolling through the centre of Puli, looking for food there.

spots.name: Eurasian and Philippine Tectonic Plate Border
spots.desc: This is an information area marking the border of the both tectonic plates.

spots.name: Taiwan Black Bear Education Center
spots.desc: A volunteer-run educational centre focusing on the fauna of Eastern Taiwan, particularly black bears. There is very little material available in English here.

spots.name: PuShi Arts Hall
spots.desc: A display hall used to showcase a local artform, originally using the offcut materials from the local rock quarries, which was later developed to more fully utilise the variety of materials available in the area.

spots.name: Chike Mountain
spots.desc: A mountain that is famed for its floral blooms. Be aware that the road up the mountain is often narrow and can be unsettling for some.

spots.name: Yuli Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwan-style night market offering a wide range of snack stalls.

spots.name: Youzihu
spots.desc: The remains of the first known settlement on Green Island, although little is left.

spots.name: Fanchuanbi Grassland
spots.desc: A high plateau which offers panoramic views out to sea on one side, and of many of the unique rock formations on the other.

spots.name: Historic Mountain Trail
spots.desc: This trail was the only way to cross the mountain of the island, before the ring road was completed. The trail is now only used for recreation. The whole trail takes around 90 minutes and includes some steep parts, so a fairly high degree of physical fitness is required.

spots.name: Green Island Underwater postbox
spots.desc: Unveiled in 2018, the landmark is essentially what the name suggests: it's a postbox that's underwater. The box itself is shaped like a white seahorse.

spots.name: Shilang Diving Area
spots.desc: A popular diving spot to see the coral reefs, supported by the warm currents coming up from the volcanic area below the island.

spots.name: Atayal museum
spots.desc: A fairly new building built to promote the Atayal culture. The exterior and interior of the building are designed and decorated with unique Atayal totems.

spots.name: Nan'ao Ecocenter
spots.desc: A 90-hectare park that features an information centre, and a number of facilities to allow visitors to explore and understand the surrounding narural environment.

spots.name: Fishing bay of Nan-ao
spots.desc: Began to work to build in 1993, in addition to the whole ground, the manufacture of rhombus piece, building the south, north outside breakwater, and wharfs for 300 m. Located the fishing bay of Nan-ao of a sea shore of Chao-Yang neighbor, the north contain Wu-shi-bi for natural cover. Due to the Abundant water resource nearby, the fishing bay of Nan-ao can be used as the fishing place to snare…

spots.name: Sha-yun Memorial Park
spots.desc: At a resting spot next to Ye-jia-xiang exhibition center, with the view of the beautiful mountain mist of Nan-ao, half-way along Suhua Highway. The visitors can visit and understand the meaning of the Bell of the Sha-yun for Nan-ao.

spots.name: Guanyin Coast Major Wildlife Habitat
spots.local: 觀音海岸野生動物重要棲息環境
spots.desc: A picturesque seaside area of beaches and caves (featured in the page banner).

spots.name: Nanao Natural Farm
spots.desc: Volunteers can choose to work and in-exchange for accommodation and meals.

spots.name: Jian Hua Ice Shop
spots.desc: Serves ice dessert. Their most famous dessert is the "Chuan Dao Bing".

spots.name: Nanfangao Lookout
spots.desc: An observation platform offering views of the surrounding mountains, sea, and settlements.

spots.name: The Mountain Highway Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the construction of the highway network in Taiwan.

spots.name: Yilan Cake Factory
spots.desc: A small cake factory with a series of exhibits related to traditional cake-making and a store where visitors can buy the produce of the factory.

spots.name: Mediterranean CASA
spots.desc: A Mediterranean-themed restaurant styled to look like a Santorini villa.

spots.name: Yilan Railway Station Old Warehousing Facilities
spots.local: 台鐵宜蘭車站舊倉庫群
spots.desc: There were 9 warehouses built in 1919, providing numerous businesses with a place to store their goods. It is used for selling famous products from Yilan. It is on the right hand side of Yilan train station. Exiting the train station, turn to the right. The building is on the right hand side.

spots.name: Former Office, Taiwan Railway Administration, Yilan Transportation Section
spots.local: 台鐵宜蘭運務段舊辦公室
spots.desc: This building was constructed in 1959. The building served as a transportation office for the Taiwan Railway Administration. It is now a Visitor Center where you can get information. Turn left when leaving the train station. The building is on the left hand side.

spots.name: Former Rice Inspection Bureau Yilan Branch Office
spots.local: 舊米穀檢查所宜蘭出張所
spots.desc: It was constructed in 1930 for use in the process of inspection, evaluation, and distribution of local rice. The characteristics of the building include an arched entrance, rectangular windows, British style brick walls, and a Japanese-style roof. From the train station, go straight and you will find it to your left.

spots.name: Former Official Residence of the Magistrate of Yilan
spots.desc: It was built as the official residence for Japanese magistrates in 1911. There is huge camphor tree inside the premises of the building that has been there for at least 100 years. It was reconstructed for tourists to visit in 1997.
spots.addr: No. 3, Lishing 3rd Lane, Jiocheng S. Rd

spots.name: Xianguo Monument
spots.desc: A stone monument erected during the period of Japanese occupation dedicated to the Chinese killed by the indigenous inhabitants during the early period of Chinese migration into the Yilan area.

spots.name: Chian Li Guang Herbal Garden
spots.desc: The focus of this place is on traditional herbal medicine, holding two greenhouses, an eco-museum and an exhibition center. The owners are trying pass down the use of traditional herbal medicines to the next generation. They also provide many herbal products (drinks, cookies and herbal meals, for example). There is a NT$100 consumable entrance fee towards a guided tour, a D.I.Y. activity or…

spots.name: Agrioz
spots.desc: It is the first government-authenticated tourism factory in Taiwan, with an area of around 9915 m². Agrioz is a modern tourism factory which produces fine kumquat products and collects kumquats from local farmers to provide quality products to the public. Agrioz provides several activities to their guests, such as D.I.Y., factory tours, visits to the kumquat museum and a souvenir shop.

spots.name: Yadian Cake Factory
spots.desc: A small cake factory that has a number of exhibits related to cake-making. You can also take a tour of the factory itself.

spots.name: Jimmy Park
spots.desc: A small, quirky park on the site of an old train station, and themed accordingly.

spots.name: Yilan Sports Park
spots.desc: A large park area with a stadium, running track, and other sports facilities.

spots.name: Yoai Department Store
spots.desc: From Yilan Train Station: Go straight and turn right on Jiucheng E. Rd. Walk for three blocks and look for the tall building.

spots.name: Luna Plaza
spots.desc: From Yilan Train Station: go straight and turn left on Jiucheng S. Rd. Then turn left on Sec. 2, Shennong Rd.

spots.name: Dark ice cream shop
spots.desc: A famous small ice cream shop located near Luna Plaza. The shop offers only five flavors, but is well known for using high-quality ingredients, attracting both locals and visitors.

spots.name: Dongmen night market
spots.desc: The Dongmen night market attracts many tourists since the local media regularly does reports about it. At the very front, there is a yakitori shop called Liang Dai Pon (梁大胖), where some of the products are only NT$10 each. The first booth on the left side is green onion pancake (蔥油餅). It is always full of customers because they use the high quality green onion from local producers. The second…

spots.name: Garlic meat broth
spots.desc: A local specialty shop known for garlic-flavored thick pork broth, a famous dish in Yilan.

spots.name: Pasta Kitchen
spots.desc: Casual Italian eatery known locally as Pasta Kitchen, serving pasta and other Western-style dishes.

spots.name: Everyday Smells Great (每日香)
spots.desc: This is a traditional lunch shop aimed at local workers. Expect it to be very busy around 11:00. You can pick from probably over 30 fresh vegetables, as well as meat and fish. Customers can also drink soup inside for free. The cashier is very friendly and talkative, and is quite likely give you compliments on your looks.

spots.name: Rakuzan Ramen
spots.desc: A popular Japanese ramen restaurant in Jiaoxi, well known for its rich broth and location near the hot spring district.

spots.name: New Tile House Hakka Cultural District
spots.local: 新瓦屋客家文化保存區
spots.desc: A small area containing a number of traditional Hakka-style houses.

spots.name: Reptiles and amphibians park
spots.desc: A well laid out park with a number of stone statues of various reptiles, as well as a small amphitheatre.

spots.name: Luwuxianzheng Native Plant Park
spots.desc: A moderately-sized park that contains a number of sculptures and examples of local flora. Signage is almost exclusively in Chinese.

spots.name: Tofu Rocks
spots.desc: An area of the river where a number of large concrete blocks have been eroded smooth resembling bricks of tofu. The area is a popular place for couples to take photos.

spots.name: Cultural Bureau Performance Hall
spots.local: 新竹縣政府文化局演藝廳
spots.desc: Run by the local government, this venue hosts a number of arts performances for the public.

spots.name: Chubby Brunch & Burger
spots.desc: Delicious, affordable American food! Huge selection of salads, burgers, pasta, wraps, and brunch all day!

spots.name: Titty Tea
spots.desc: American owned cafe. Great coffee, tea, beer wine, and excellent sandwiches. Quaint, stylish atmosphere.

spots.name: Bistro 302
spots.desc: Elegant, fine-dining, American chef with a modern, fresh style.

spots.name: Bali Left Bank Park
spots.desc: The newest waterfront park in the left bank of Danshui River. This park, along with the bicycle path pass through it, is now the land mark of Bali and offers great view of Danshui river.

spots.name: Tang Spa
spots.desc: A separate spa amusement park owned by Formosa Fun Coast. Themed as China's Tang Dynasty, it features hot springs, spas and Chinese styled decorations. Some of the facilities do not open during Formosa Fun Coast's season of operations. A swimsuit is required for certain facilities.
spots.price: NT$600 for adults (NT$500 on weekdays, extra fee required for the use of private hot spring room)

spots.name: Banqiao Flower Market
spots.desc: A long market selling plants and gardening ware which is located under an elevated roadway.

spots.name: Andy Cuisine Restaurant
spots.desc: This is the main restaurant but they have other branches at the Xinpu MRT stop and Jiangzicui MRT stop. Food is out of this world. Curries, Bbq'd chicken/pork, salads are good. Spicy though, just ask for "xiao la" (pronounced "shaow la") if you would like it not as hot. It's off two MRT stops on the Yongning-Nangang MRT station just minutes from downtown Taibei.

spots.name: Jiufen Old Street
spots.desc: A series of stores and restaurants running along Jishan and Shuqi Streets, which are built into the side of the coastal hills. The area is known for its collection of shops, eateries, and teahouses, allowing visitors to sample local specialties and purchase handicrafts and other knick-knacks. The area also provides spectacular views of the harbors and the Pacific Ocean below. The most popular…

spots.name: Taiyang Co. Ruifang Mining Operation Office
spots.desc: This historic building just below Shuqi steps at the bus parking lot. Yen Yun-nian (1882-1923), a Jiufen merchant, got the business authority from Japanese "Itoda Gumi" during the Japanese era. The company was established in 1948 by his brother, quarrying gold since 1914 till 1971. The Bafan Tunnel mine entrance remains inside the office, but not open to visitors.

spots.name: Songde Park
spots.desc: A small memorial park west of the town. There are monuments to praise the great achievement of Yen Yun-nian who founded Jiufen's mining culture. Creative artistic sculptures can easily be seen in the park. Also the early Mining Tunnel can also be found next to the park.

spots.name: Wufan Tunnel
spots.desc: Next to the park, this tunnel has been excavated in 1927. The coal transported out from the tunnel was smashed in the mine-smashing area and carried by high altitude transporting pipe. There is a light railway passing through the tunnel, which was run by a Japanese company and then contracted by Jiouda Co. when the Japanese left Taiwan in 1945. In 1971, in order to protect the security of the…

spots.name: Ghost Lore Museum
spots.desc: A museum all about ghosts and the undead. Contains lots of horror props, including numerous life sized monster sculptures.

spots.name: Xiaojingua Peak
spots.desc: Along Line 102 to Shuangxi Highway to the highest point of Mt.Jilong, you can see the Xiaojingua Peak on the hilltop. It opens the first page of Jiufen gold digging history.

spots.name: Amei Tea House
spots.desc: Supposedly the inspiration for the ornate bathhouse in Spirited Away.

spots.name: City Of Sadness Restaurant
spots.desc: Just on the corner of Shuqi and Qingbian Roads. This restaurant was featured in Hou Hsiao-hsien's film A City of Sadness.

spots.name: Jioufen Teahouse
spots.desc: Jioufen Teahouse was once the meeting place for many great Taiwanese writers and artists when it first opened. When you enter from the narrow crowded street, you come into a spacious and calm interior. On the right are steaming iron kettles nestled in a long fiery bank of coals. Bundles of tea and high quality ceramics and tea implements fill the first level. The host will lead you to a quiet…

spots.name: Antler Creek Constructed Wetland
spots.desc: A large riverside park with a number of walking trails and other amenities.

spots.name: Singren Garden Night Market
spots.desc: A night market with a difference: it is more uniformly laid-out than most night markets in Taiwan and is partially indoors.

spots.name: Museum of Tamsui Fishiegoodies
spots.desc: A very small establishment by the harbour with some information about fisheries in Taiwan.

spots.name: Tamshui Yuandao Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: A temple to the goddess Guanyin with pleasant gardens and a restaurant.

spots.name: Wuji Tianyuan Temple
spots.desc: An impressive multi-storey pagoda-style temple surrounded by gardens. The temple is a popular destination, particularly when the cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

spots.name: Red Castle 1899
spots.desc: A colonial building sits on the hillside, built in 1899. This is the best view cafe in Tamsui. They serves both Western and Chinese dishes. The entrance is just east of the Mackay statue, atop a hill reached by 106 stone steps.

spots.name: Pause Landis
spots.desc: This hot spring hotel has several open air themed rooms. Their public baths are also open-air overlooking the cliff side across a river. The establishment is clean and well designed with a modern and Zen-like feel.

spots.name: Proto Spring
spots.desc: A public hot spring resort on the middle of Wulai Old Street. Offers a no-frills but well-maintained public Japanese-style (gender-segregated, nude) baths with four pools for NT$300.

spots.name: Wulai Hot Springs Resort
spots.desc: Large hot spring resort with both private and public pools. Public pools are gender-segregated, are enjoyed Japanese-style (in the nude) and with an excellent view of the mountains. The public pools contain two hot pools, a sauna, a jacuzzi and a steam room. A NT$500 package allows for one-hour in the public pools - with a free meal in the resort cafe included (tea and toast). Towels, lockers and…

spots.name: Taiya Po Po (泰雅婆婆美食店)
spots.desc: Literally "Atayal Grandmother," this restaurant specializes in Aboriginal dishes such as Wild Mountain Boar (山豬), Bamboo Tube Rice (竹筒飯), Wild Mountain Yams (山藥), and Pickled Pork (damamein; 的麼面). Featured on Travel Channel's "Bizarre Foods: Taiwan"

spots.name: Helen's Coffee
spots.desc: The seating is mostly outdoors, so you can enjoy the fresh mountain air and a view over the river and town while sipping your latte.

spots.name: Fuhe Flea Market
spots.desc: An outdoor market selling second hand items, fruit, and a number of other odds and ends.

spots.name: Dz Dzai lin
spots.desc: Yuxi Street. A reasonably priced and laid back restaurant serving vegetarian and natural food dishes.

spots.name: Lehua Night Market
spots.desc: Founded in the 1970s, Lehua Night Market offers a rich mix of snack stalls, including Taiwanese food such as rice cakes, tempura, oyster omelet, shrimp and meat stew and shaved ice, as well as shopping and entertainment facilities.

spots.name: Soy Milk King of the World
spots.desc: Sec. 2. Near the MRT Dingxi Station. It's the original "Yonghe Doujiang" (from which all other places copied); it's open 24 hours a day and it's cheap!

spots.name: National Immigration Agency
spots.desc: Visa applications/extensions for foreign residents of New Taipei City should be made at this agency.

spots.name: Beitou Hot Springs Museum
spots.desc: Built during the Japanese occupation, this beautiful Euro-Japanese style building was once the main public bath in Beitou. It has been lovingly restored and was re-opened in its current form in 1998. Through the twelve rooms, the story of Beitou's romantic years of steam and mystery are revealed in interesting displays.

spots.name: Ketagalan Cultural Center
spots.desc: This ten-story building is dedicated to the Aboriginal culture that once flourished in the Beitou area.

spots.name: Beitou Park
spots.desc: A long, narrow park. Within the park are fountains, the Beitou library, the Beitou Hot Springs Museum and an outdoor hot spring. Due to its central location, the park is a useful landmark for locating Beitou's other attractions. The park is also featured in the Hong Kong movie Turn Left, Turn Right, starring with Takeshi Kaneshiro and Gigi Leung.

spots.name: Geothermal Valley
spots.desc: This is one of the most famous spots in Beitou, a natural sulfur hot spring where water temperatures can reach 100°C (212°F).

spots.name: Millennium Hot Spring
spots.desc: An outdoor public mixed-gender hot spring. A great choice for the budget minded. Swimwear is required; you can purchase it on-the-spot, but choices are limited and somewhat expensive. They have a number of rules, available on English signs; it would behoove you to follow them lest the guy in the red shirt blow his whistle at you.

spots.name: Emperor Spa
spots.desc: Traditional Japanese-style sex-segregated nude hot spring. Entry is free if you spend at least $400 at their restaurant; the seafood porridge is particularly famous. Private spa rooms are also available. Both this and neighboring Kawayu Spa have a reputation for being gay cruising spots.

spots.name: Amalfi
spots.desc: A cozy Italian vegetarian restaurant. Excellent pizza. Friendly and fast service. Coffee/tea.

spots.name: Shanxi Beef Noodles
spots.desc: A small noodle shop that serves beef with hand-cut noodles in tomato broth and other simple delicious meals.

spots.name: Yummy Vegan Home
spots.desc: Delicious vegan cuisine. Burgers, pasta, hummus, healthy drinks. Bright and pleasant interior. English menu.

spots.name: Discover Center Of Taipei
spots.desc: Located just inside the main entrance of Taipei City Hall, this is a good place to know the history and culture of Taipei City.

spots.name: Taipei 101 Indoor Observatory
spots.desc: The world's second fastest elevators will zip visitors up to the 89th-floor observation deck in a mere 37 seconds. It's worth taking a ride up, as the views are stunning. The best time to visit would be in the late afternoon when you spend a couple of hours and see both day and night views of Taipei. Don't forget to look toward the middle of the Indoor Observatory, where you'll see the world's…
spots.price: NT$600 for adults, NT$370 for kids under 12

spots.name: Taipei 101 Outdoor Observatory
spots.desc: You can also go up to the outdoor observatory on the 91st floor (while it's possible to go to the outdoor observatory in a wheelchair, the view is negligible, as the concrete railing is too high to see over). Often only the elevator side remains open and you cannot walk a circle—if this is important to you, ask ahead.

spots.name: Yongkang Street
spots.desc: The lanes and alleys around Yongkang Street and Yongkang Park are packed with specialty restaurants, gift shops selling Taiwanese handicrafts, and distinctive cafes. A great place to spend a few hours strolling around.

spots.name: Elephant Mountain Hiking Trail
spots.local: Xiangshan Hiking Trail / 象山步道
spots.desc: A short walk from Taipei 101 in Xinyi District. Very steep steps lead up into a shaded, forested hill overlooking the city. Elephant Mountain, about 200 m high, is one of the Four Beasts Mountains, and paths from here go up to higher peaks in Nangang.

spots.name: Taipei 101 Mall
spots.desc: Attached to the tower is a large, upscale mall. While most of the stores are from the same brand-names as stores in other major cities around the world, the mall also features several homegrown Taiwanese luxury brands, and even the international brands often have items designed exclusively for the Taiwanese market. Even if you don't plan to buy anything, the open and spacious design of the…

spots.name: Shin Kong Mitsukoshi
spots.desc: Xinyi branch of the department store chain, this is the largest department store in Taiwan, occupying four different buildings.

spots.name: Fingertip Art
spots.desc: A two-storey (first floor and basement) handicraft and local souvenir shop. Stylish and affordable goods. Friendly and very helpful staff.

spots.name: Jianguo Holiday Jade Market
spots.desc: Located under an elevated expressway, reaching from Renai Road & Jianguo South Road intersection down Jianguo Road, till Xinyi Rd. In addition to jade, flowers and many other kinds of handcrafts and jewelry can be purchased. There are actually three different markets, the Weekend Jade Market, Weekend Flower Market and Weekend Handicrafts Market in this same location. As the names suggest, they…

spots.name: Potala
spots.desc: A wide selection of Buddha statues, prayer flags, Buddhist chanting CDs. Staff speak English.

spots.name: Xunyilu Art Boutique
spots.desc: An interesting and eclectic mix of traditional handicrafts with contemporary souvenirs. Helpful staff.

spots.name: Tong Hua Night Market
spots.desc: This night market caters for the more adventurous eaters. The market featuers not only local foods but dozens of exotic delicacies, including inexpensive Malaysian, Japanese and Taiwanese snacks.
spots.addr: Alley 1, Lane 40, Linjiang Street, Da’an District

spots.name: AiYu's Dream Journey Grass Jelly
spots.desc: Great Ai Yu Jelly, Grass Jelly, and Tofu Flower desserts. Recommendations: 愛玉綜合冰 (ai yu zong he bing);仙草綜合冰(xian cao zong he bing);豆花綜合冰 (dou hua zong he bing -- warning: this contains peanuts, but you can ask for it without them -- "不要花生" (bu yao hua sheng)). Ai Yu is only found in Taiwan.
spots.addr: Tonghua Street No. 56 (臺北大安區通化街56號)

spots.name: Kiki Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant serves authentic Szechwanese peppery hot pot.

spots.name: Thanh Ky
spots.desc: Always busy and popular with Vietnamese expats and locals. Rice noodle soup with spicy beef and curried beef or pork is a specialty.

spots.name: The Pengs' Traditional Hong Kong Cuisine
spots.desc: Opened in the 1980s, the food and the decor of the restaurant have not changed since. Known for being more authentically 1980s Hong Kong than most restaurants in Hong Kong today.

spots.name: Yongkang Beef Noodle
spots.desc: One of the top-twenty beef noodle shops in Taipei. Yongkang Beef Noodle occupies the former location of Lao-Zhang Beef Noodle, which is now located next to it.

spots.name: KingSpicy J
spots.desc: The infamous restaurant known for its spicy noodle challenge, with rare people able to pass. If you are a fan of spicy foods, you will enjoy their spicy noodle, with four levels and the Challenge level. The third level is considered very spicy in other Taiwanese restaurants. Anyone interested in the Challenge level must have tried the fourth level, then challenge the Challenge level the next day.…

spots.name: Alleycat's Pizza
spots.desc: Generally considered by expats to be the only edible and best traditional Italian pizza in Taipei.

spots.name: Din Tai Fung
spots.desc: Famous for its steamed pork dumplings. Worth a detour. Several locations in Taipei and worldwide, but this is the main branch. Gets very crowded even on weekdays so book in advance, or go to other branches such as the one under Taipei 101

spots.name: Niu Ba Ba (688 Beef Bowl)
spots.desc: The most expensive beef noodle soup to be had in Taiwan. On average this dish costs N$120. Owner Tony Wong has bowls ranging from a few hundred all the way to $10,000. The simple decor belies the intricate process Wong uses to deliver beef noodles for Taipei's foodies.
spots.addr: No. 149, Section 6, Minquan East Road, Neihu District

spots.name: Flavors restaurant
spots.desc: Located on a back street of busy Renai Rd with a lush garden in front and warm and cozy atmosphere inside. Flavors serves great grilled steaks including rare meat like venison, amazing selection of appetizers in a casual fine dining way.
spots.addr: Ren Ai Rd. Sec.4 No.13 Alley 26 Lane 300

spots.name: Peking Do It True
spots.desc: This is the place to go if you crave good Beijing cuisine. Visitors may be surprised to see a large photo of former U.S. President George H.W. Bush on the wall, taken when he ate at the restaurant during his trip to Taiwan in 1994.

spots.name: Shang Palace
spots.desc: Specialize in Cantonese and regional Chinese cuisines. Dim sum is available for lunch only.

spots.name: San Niu
spots.desc: Fresh sashimi and tempura shrimp. Less expensive than most Japanese restaurants of this quality. Clean, comfortable environment.

spots.name: Whalen's
spots.desc: Whalen's offer delicious Canadian cuisine such as Poutine and Quiche Lorraine, as well as breakfast omelets and waffles. They also offer a variety of beers. Reservation is recommended since the restaurant is considerably small.
spots.addr: No. 145, Section 2, Ānhé Rd, Daan District

spots.name: a.se Cafe
spots.desc: Elegant and relaxed interior. Distinctive mismatched furniture. Charcoal gray walls. Warm lighting, Outdoor seating. Excellent coffee. Very friendly and warm service. Dull, elevator music.

spots.name: Cafe Moda Taipei
spots.desc: For people who prefer the new concept of a boutique cafe, the specialty of this place by far are the 100% Organic Guatemalan quality coffee beverages they offer in a cozy ambient mixed with art fashion and great music. A small but fancy terrace is perfect for enjoying beverages on a fresh day. They also have imported beer, wine, tea, juices and other snacks in their menu, including cheese and…
spots.price: Coffee beverages between NT$120 and NT$200
spots.addr: 1F, No 11, Lane 49, Sec 1, Anhe Road, Daan District

spots.name: Minimal Cafe
spots.desc: This cafe is famous for having many resident cats living inside of it (49, according to the wait staff). In fact, the owner of this cafe loves cats so much, stray ones are adopted, spayed/neutered, then allowed to live in the cafe. Thus, as you drink your beverage, don't be surprised if cats are checking you out. This cafe is indeed clean despite all the cats, and has tasty mid-range priced…
spots.addr: 106台北市Taipei泰順街2巷 Tai4Shun4 Jie1 Lane 2, #42, Daan District

spots.name: Martinez Coffee
spots.desc: A coffee shop and supplier of high quality coffee. Elegant and relaxing interior. Outdoor seating. Cakes and dessert

spots.name: Out of Office Coffee Roastery
spots.desc: A Zen minimalist cafe. Spacious. Great coffee. Cakes and snacks

spots.name: Saturn Landing Turkish Coffee
spots.desc: Spacious and light. Outdoor seating at the rear. Excellent Turkish coffee, along with standard coffees. Healthy meals. Turkish interior design and background music.

spots.name: Carnegies
spots.desc: With an outdoor patio, it's perfect for those who prefer a quieter and less smoky atmosphere. The scene is geared toward the 30+ expats and locals.

spots.name: Club Myst
spots.desc: One of the hottest night club in Taipei. Often cited as having the best view of the Taipei 101 building. Large and active dance floor. Open all nights, Wednesday night is ladies night with free entry.
spots.addr: No. 12, 9F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist

spots.name: Elektro
spots.desc: Another large and popular nightclub, previously was called Spark but was closed down due to some police controversy.
spots.addr: 6F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist

spots.name: Fourplay Cuisine
spots.desc: A quiet bar/restaurant with creative drinks. Your shot may include a helium balloon, a water pipe, fire or dry ice.

spots.name: Luxy
spots.desc: One of the most well-known clubs in Taipei. Luxy has two levels: the lower level has a side room playing house/techno and a main room playing hip-hop; the upper level is a lounge with a small dance floor overlooking the main room. Cover charge goes up after 23:00. Get there early to avoid a line.
spots.addr: 5F, 201 Zhongxiao E. Rd Section 4, Daan District

spots.name: Ziga Zaga
spots.desc: This club specializes in cocktails and Italian cuisine - both the service and food are excellent. It's popular with locals and expats. Ladies Night is on Wednesday nights.
spots.addr: No.2, Song Shou Road Grand Hyatt Taipei

spots.name: Stop By Teahouse
spots.desc: A tea cafe in a modern setting, offering a full range of brewing options. Ask to see the private tearoom in the basement.

spots.name: Wistaria House
spots.desc: Wistaria is set in a traditional house, complete with tatami mats, and is a great place to spend an afternoon relaxing with friends and soaking up the atmosphere of Taiwan.

spots.name: Happy Fruit Juice Bar
spots.desc: Happy Fruit Juice Bar is a fresh fruit juice bar decorated with a Greek cafe interior. The store is family owned and run by a mom and four sisters. They serve tea, fresh fruit juice, milk pearl tea and other drinks. It's a great place to grab something cool and refreshing on a hot day. Also, Happy Fruit Juice bar's right beside the Mofo burger joint, so it's a perfect place to get a healthy drink…

spots.name: Academia Sinica
spots.desc: Home to several research institutions, such as the Genomic Research Center, the Institute of Biomedical Sciences, and the Institute of Cellular and Organismic Biology.

spots.name: Tomb of Hu Shih
spots.desc: The tomb of Hu Shih, famous philosopher, essayist, and diplomat who was influential on the May Fourth Movement that toppled the Qing dynasty in China.

spots.name: Hu Shih Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A small museum dedicated to the archeologist Hu Shih which contains a number of artifacts related to ancient Chinese history. There is an audio guide available in English.

spots.name: Bishan Temple
spots.desc: The largest Taoist temple in Neihu. It offers spectacular views of Taipei on a clear day. It is possible to spend the night here by offering a donation. There are other interesting Buddhist and Taoist temples nearby. Ride the local Red 2 bus to the Temple. Attractions include a golden statue and beautiful architecture. Walk down from the temple to the city for addition appreciation of the flora…

spots.name: Dahu Park
spots.desc: A popular area for recreation. It boasts a large lake with a famous Chinese-style arched bridge. There complementing the lake is a lakeside swimming pool and Egret Mountain which is adjacent to the lake a great hiking location. The swimming pool is a little outdated and in needs some refurnishing, but it's only NT$110 for a swim which includes access to the jacuzzi, steam room, sauna and the…

spots.name: Huo Guo Shi Jia
spots.desc: Shabu Shabu restaurant behind the McDonalds by the mall next to Neihu Station. Good seafood and prices.

spots.name: Paradise Thai
spots.desc: Best Thai place in town, better than Thai Town and Spice World. They have Taipei's only micro-brewry built into their restaurant. Great spicy Thai food and cold beer to wash it down. Prices are upper-end, but worth it.

spots.name: National Palace Museum
spots.local: 國立故宮博物院 - Short name is 故宮
spots.desc: Probably Taiwan's top sight, displaying the finest collection of treasures formerly owned by the Emperors of China. During the Sino-Japanese War, the Nationalist Government took artifacts from Beijing so they wouldn't be harmed by the invading Japanese. After the war ended, the Chinese Civil War continued and thus the Kuomintang shipped them to Taiwan. The Communists weren't very happy about…
spots.price: NT$350 for adults, free for under 18s. NT$150 for students (with ISIC or Youth Travel card), and NT$320 per person for…

spots.name: Taipei Astronomical Museum
spots.desc: This modern museum offers a hands-on introduction to our universe. In addition to the permanent exhibits, there is also an Imax dome theater, an observatory and a 3D movie theater. Entrance to the observatory is free, while NT$100 (adult) NT$50 (child) is charged for a show at each of the two theaters.

spots.name: Shung Ye Museum of Formosan Aborigines
spots.local: 順益台灣原住民博物館
spots.desc: This museum houses exhibitions of Aboriginal culture and lifestyle. An English audio guide is available.

spots.name: National Taiwan Science Education Center
spots.desc: Science center with hands-on exhibits and bilingual displays.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, 09:00-18:00 on weekends and during school vacation periods, closed Mondays

spots.name: Shilin Residence
spots.desc: It was one of Chiang Kai-shek's abodes during his Taipei years, and the sprawling grounds were opened as a park in 1996. This residence is famous for the European style of its architecture and gardens.

spots.name: Zhishanyan Cultural and Ecological Garden
spots.desc: A small hill is in the south of Tianmu's Yangming Hospital, and north of the Shuangxi river. The Zhishan Hill (Zhishanyan 芝山岩), one of the oldest archaeological excavation sites in Taiwan. Along the trail, you can see many historic heritages in this hill, the Huiji Temple (惠濟宮), Fortified Gate, small temple and an old camphor tree over 300 years old. Getting there: MRT Zhishan Station (Danshui…

spots.name: Aborigine Culture Park
spots.desc: The theme of the park is the aboriginal culture. There are sixteen stone-slab sculptures stand in the entrance of the park, depicting the people of Taiwan's sixteen tribes in their traditional costumes.

spots.name: Shilin Night Market
spots.desc: To really taste the flavor of Taiwanese life a trip to a night market is a must, and Shilin is one of the largest. The market began in the 19th century as a collection of vendors trading their goods near a small harbor along the Keelung River. Today the harbor is long gone but the night market has become what is quite possibly the largest collection of vendors and eateries in Taiwan. The night…

spots.name: Dayeh Takashimaya
spots.desc: A 12-story department store with food court in the basement and bookstore on the 4th floor. A free shuttle connects the store to Shilin and Shipai MRT Stations.
spots.addr: No.55, Zhongcheng Rd, Sec 2, Tianmu (忠誠路二段55號)

spots.name: Caves Books
spots.desc: One of the original book stores specializing in English titles, especially strong on novels and English language text books.

spots.name: Juice Meal Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Dine-in service is no longer available; instead, vegetarian rice dumplings are available for takeaway.”
spots.addr: No.34, Ln. 505, Sec. 5, Jhongshan N. Rd

spots.name: Jingxing Vegetarian Kitchen
spots.desc: Simple, tasty Chinese vegetarian meals. Choose a set meal from the menu and it is served on a tray. Owner speaks English, and there's a picture menu in English and Chinese.

spots.name: Cafe Onion Restaurant
spots.desc: Cafe Onion serves pastas and steaks. Tea or coffee are also available. Germany pork knuckles are good.

spots.name: Fangs Restaurant
spots.desc: Popular amongst Taiwanese and expats, this 2-story restaurants offers excellent quality local dishes. There is an open kitchen where people can watch dumplings being made.

spots.name: Sanxitang Space
spots.desc: Well-hidden slick teahouse/restaurant atop the Palace Museum, which looks more expensive than it is. Most people stop by for a pot of oolong and tiny pastries, but the menu (available in English) also covers dim sum and enough savouries to make a meal.

spots.name: Orange Cafe
spots.desc: Pining for a cafe with a backstreet atmosphere and pumping out Indian, Middle Eastern, folk or Floyd type music? Check out Orange Cafe. In addition to coffee/tea etc, they also offer a simple menu that includes vegetarian dishes, and from 22:30 on Friday evening the place comes to life with a fire dance performance on the roof.

spots.name: Vagabond Cafe
spots.desc: A spacious art-style cafe with large windows overlooking green space - documentary movies screened on Wednesdays and Saturdays at 19:30 - excellent coffee and home-made (including vegetarian) dishes.

spots.name: The Maokong Gondola
spots.desc: Runs from Taipei Zoo MRT station to Maokong, with stops at the Taipei Zoo South and Zhinan Temple stations. There are two types of cable cars - regular and crystal, which has a clear bottom. You have to select which type of car to board. There's no difference in ticket or price, only in waiting time. The line for the crystal cars takes much longer. However, it's not worth the wait as the view…
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat Sun 08:30-20:00. Closed Mondays, except every first one of the month
spots.price: NT$70/100/120 (1/2/3 station(s)), NT$20 off with EasyCard during weekdays

spots.name: National Chengchi University
spots.desc: NCCU, often abbreviated to Zhengda (政大), is Taiwan's leading national university focused on humanities and social sciences. It is large with lots of greenery and open spaces. There are hiking trails up the mountains in the back of the campus with teahouses and temples all over the hills. The campus grounds are surrounded by shops, bookstores, eateries, cafes and teahouses popular with students…

spots.name: Zhang Nai Miao Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A small and intimate museum built in memory of tea master Zhang Nai Miao, who brought the first Tieguanyin plants from Anxi, Fujian to Zhanghu, Muzha, which marked the beginning of Tieguanyin tea cultivation in the area.

spots.name: Jingmei Jiying Temple
spots.desc: Jingmei Jiying Temple honors Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, both of whom fought and died bravely during the An Shi rebellion. It is one of Taiwan's designated historic monuments and a great example of Qing dynasty temple architecture.

spots.name: Zhinan Temple
spots.desc: One of the most important of Taiwan's early Taoist temples, Zhinan Temple is dedicated to main deity Lu Dongbin, one of the Eight Immortals, and various other deities.

spots.name: Tian'en Temple
spots.desc: A 4-storey Taoist temple dedicated to an eclectic mix of deities.

spots.name: Taipei Tea Promotion Center
spots.local: 台北市茶研發推廣中心
spots.desc: Offers introduction to tea picking, processing, brewing and free taste testing.

spots.name: Xianjiyan hiking trail
spots.desc: Many curious visitors come here to see a footprint supposedly left by the Taoist deity Lu Dongbin. The view from Xianjiyan trail includes natural vistas as well as a bird's eye view of the southern districts of Taipei. Located on the hill behind Jingmei Night Market, this nicely built and well-marked network of trails also features a temple located along the trail. The main trails are all paved…

spots.name: Zhinan Temple & Cihui Temple hiking trail
spots.desc: In addition to the beauty of the temples, visitors can also enjoy an excellent view of the Taipei Basin, Danshui River, and Guanyinshan.

spots.name: Zhangshan Temple hiking trail
spots.desc: Offers spectacular views of the Taipei basin and Taipei 101 from in front of Zhangshan Temple.

spots.name: Ergeshan
spots.desc: This is an excellent choice for a moderately strenuous hike lasting several hours. Ergeshan is the highest peak along a ridge trail extending from Shiding in the east to Ankeng in the West. The peak of Ergeshan is at the border of the Wenshan District and Taipei County. The hike to the ridge can be a challenge, but the ridge trail is excellent, offering spectacular views and the occasional…

spots.name: Riverside Park
spots.desc: Not a hiking trail, but popular among those out for a relaxed stroll. The various sections of the park run most of the length of Jingmei Stream, the main body of water in Wenshan District. The park is characterized by large grassy areas interspersed with public sports facilities (such as tennis courts and softball diamonds). It's a good place to go for casual exercise or for viewing the bird life…

spots.name: Muzha Park
spots.desc: If you come at the right time of year, this is a good place to see fireflies.

spots.name: Zhang Xie Xing Tea Company
spots.desc: Famous for its Tieguanyin tea (Iron Goddess of Mercy) and tea candies.

spots.name: Jingmei Night Market
spots.desc: Many small street vendors and shops selling items including various snack foods, clothes, and accessories. Businesses in the night market typically open around 16:00 and stay open well past midnight.

spots.name: Yao Yue Teahouse
spots.desc: Offers creative tea cuisine with restful views over the surrounding countryside.

spots.name: Xing Hua Lin Teahouse
spots.desc: Estimated best time for apricot blossom viewing - February to March. The best time for viewing varies according to the weather conditions.

spots.name: National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The memorial hall is a famous but controversial symbol of both Taipei and the Republic of China, as expected of its namesake. Every morning, at 06:00 in the summer and 06:30 in the winter, the nation's flag is raised in the square in front of the memorial. The huge courtyard serves as a place for both national celebrations as well as a platform to voice one's disapproval of the government. The…

spots.name: National Museum Of History
spots.desc: This museum is in Taipei Botanical Garden, and is famous for its varied selection of exhibits, including Tang dynasty tri-color pottery and Shang dynasty bronzes.

spots.name: National Taiwan Museum
spots.desc: This museum is in 'Peace Park' (near Taipei Main Station) in a splendid Baroque and Renaissance style building. Opened in 1899, it was Taiwan's first museum and focuses on anthropology and the fauna and flora of the island.

spots.name: 228 Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Commemorates the 228 incident that occurred on February 28, 1947, in which locals revolting against Chinese rule were brutally massacred by the Kuomintang. This incident continues to be a key impetus behind the Taiwan independence movement to this day.

spots.name: National Taiwan University
spots.local: 台灣大學, or 台大 for short
spots.desc: Taiwan's pre-eminent institution of higher education. The campus grounds are surrounded by several blocks of shops, bookshops, cafes and tea houses popular with students and scholars. Browse through the stalls and booths directly across the street from the main entrance of the university (don't forget there is a lot more just behind the main street), grab a bite or two of the popular snacks, such…

spots.name: Presidential Office Building
spots.desc: It was built during the Japanese colonial period as the residence of the Governor-General of Taiwan. It is now the official workplace of the President of the Republic of China. Public access is generally restricted to specific open house days which are published on the web-site.

spots.name: Museum of Drinking Water
spots.desc: The Museum of Drinking Water was completed in 1908, and is the first pumping station and filtration plant in Taipei. The museum is in the Taipei Water Park.

spots.name: National Taiwan Arts Education Center
spots.desc: Formal Kenkō Jinja (Chienkung Shrine), whose architecture is a mixture of Chinese (such as three-gated torii), Japanese, and Western (such as dome-shaped roof) elements. After World War II, it was renovated to National Central Library. Now it is repurposed to serve as National Arts Education Center and there are two theaters (one indoor and one outdoor) and three exhibition rooms.

spots.name: 228 Peace Memorial Park
spots.desc: This park is on the north side of Katagalan Boulevard and the MRT station 'National Taiwan University Hospital' on the Danshui line. The park was founded by the Japanese in 1907 as New Park (新公園). The name was changed in 1996 to commemorate those killed in the 228 Incident of 28 February 1947, in which locals revolting against Chinese rule were brutally massacred by the ruling Kuomintang under…

spots.name: Taipei Botanical Garden
spots.desc: This beautiful garden has inspired the citizens of Taipei for over one hundred years. The lotus ponds are a hallmark of the park and are especially captivating when these symbols of peace are in full bloom and swaying in the summer breeze. The gardens are close to the National Museum of History.

spots.name: Hua Shan Cultural and Creative Industry Center
spots.desc: This former brewery has been transformed into a creative space in a park. The exhibitions are well presented and imaginative and the theater performances, while less formal than those at the National Theater, are first rate. The center also has a number of cool cafes - some with outdoor seating - an art movie theater and a number of shops selling innovative crafts.

spots.name: Taipei Artist Village
spots.desc: This village provides residency programs for Taiwanese artists and others from around the world. They provide gallery and studio space for artists. They also have a few cafes which are excellent for a mid-day break while exploring Taipei.
spots.price: You are free to roam around the village

spots.name: Zhongshan Hall
spots.desc: The buildings were completed in the period of Japanese rule on December 26, 1936. In 1945, The former Taipei City Hall was renamed as Zhongshan Hall. In 1992, the building has been identified to Second monuments of the country. Later it was assigned as a cultural space that hosts cultural and art events.

spots.name: National Theater Hall and National Concert Hall
spots.local: 國家戲劇院 and 國家音樂廳
spots.desc: Located in the grounds of the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial, it is an excellent place to see performances of a Taiwanese play or a dance troupe. They also host many international events. Taiwan's National Symphony Orchestra performs at the National Concert Hall. The building's neo-classic Chinese architecture is especially stunning when flood-lit at night.

spots.name: Guanghua Digital Mall
spots.desc: A six-storey mall specializing in computers and other electronic devices. The facility also comprises an exhibition pace to show case new products and a food court.

spots.name: Huashan 1914 Creative Park
spots.local: 華山1914文化創意產業園區
spots.desc: This park has several upscale gift shops (including a science-themed store and a flagship Wooderful Life for wood decorations) as well as a small artisan market.

spots.name: Taipei Zhongshan Metro Shopping Mall
spots.desc: A long underground shopping area that houses several stores selling all manner of items, not necessarily limited to electronics. A few stores in the Easy Mall carry current and vintage video games, hardware and software.

spots.name: Rockland
spots.desc: An excellent selection of outdoor gear, including trekking shoes, backpacks, and many accessories. Helpful service.
spots.addr: No. 5, Lane 94, Section 3, Xinsheng South Road, Gongguan

spots.name: Happy Farm Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.local: Kai Xing Nong Tsung (開心農場素食店)
spots.desc: Offers simple and tasty Chinese buffet style vegetarian meals.
spots.addr: 2F, No 16, Lane 683, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguang

spots.name: Su De Su Shi
spots.desc: A buffet style restaurant offering a wide range of Chinese vegetarian dishes.
spots.addr: No 21, Lane 283, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguan

spots.name: Mary Jane's Pizza
spots.desc: No. Taipei (near Taida). Great thin crust pizza at reasonable prices, they also do delivery.

spots.name: Among Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe with an alternative vibe. Excellent coffee served in distinctive clay cups. Alternative music. Warm lighting. Excellent selection of books. Healthy and freshly cooked food options. Cool and laid back owner and staff.

spots.name: Aura Cafe
spots.desc: A chic and stylish cafe. Excellent coffee, including drip. Friendly and helpful service.
spots.addr: No9, Lane 269, Roosevelt Road, Sec 3, Gongguan.

spots.name: Coffee Lab
spots.desc: This small coffee shop roasts their own beans on site. 3 resident cats keep patrons company as they sip carefully crafted lattes.
spots.addr: No. 6, Lane 64, Section 2, Zhōngxiào East Road

spots.name: Notch Cafe
spots.desc: A two storey cafe with a backstreet vibe. Excellent coffee. Innovative light meals and snacks.

spots.name: Trilobite Cafe
spots.desc: Serves excellent coffees offering a wide selection of espresso. The two resident dogs are very friendly too.

spots.name: Taipei Brewery
spots.desc: A godsend for the thirsty budget traveler in a city of pricey bars, this is most certainly the cheapest bar in town. This is a great place to find the rare Taiwan Draft Beer, which has a 2-week expiration and usually can only be found in a few restaurants and stores in the same city as the brewery. It's attached to the brewery where Taiwan Beer is made, close to the intersection of Bade and…

spots.name: The Wall Live House
spots.desc: The biggest venue for independent live music - Taiwanese bands playing everything from rock to reggae.

spots.name: Revolver
spots.desc: Just across the road from the monument to Chiang Kai Shek, this is a bar on the ground floor and a live music venue on the second floor. The indoors part is often full and partrons will stand outside chatting. This bar also has Taiwan Beer Gold Label on tap.

spots.name: Zhuzihu Lookout
spots.desc: This observation platform has a great view of Taipei, especially at night.

spots.name: Qingtiangang Grassland
spots.desc: The best grassland in Taipei. This area is popular with picnicking students and families.

spots.name: The Lin Yutang House
spots.desc: Lin Yutang (林語堂), the Master of Humor, was one of the well-known scholars in China and Taiwan. His former residence is one of the most popular tourist spots in Yangmingshan.

spots.name: Yangming Shuwu
spots.desc: Also often called Yangming Villa, is an historical building built by former President Chiang Kai-shek for receiving foreign dignitaries.

spots.name: Yangmingshan Hiking Trail (blue)
spots.desc: Distance: 8.1 km, hilly. Altitude range: 554 m. Duration: 2-4 hr, depending on the side tours, time spent at the hot springs (opening times see below) and personal fitness for climbing the 550 m altitude. Grade: Medium. Recommended: comfortable clothes and boots for walking.This trail covers most of the above mentioned scenic sights, like Mt. Cising (Qixing), Lengshuikeng (hot springs)…

spots.name: Lengshuikeng Public Baths
spots.desc: Nude, men and women in separate buildings. Make sure to bring your own soap and wash cloth. The rules insist that you much pre-wash before entering the smallish 40°C tub, and the attendees will insist too. Not many foreigners find this place, so if one, be ready to intimately meet the locals.
spots.hours: Daily: 06:00-09:00, 10:30-13:00, 14:30-17:00, 18:30-21:00. Closed every first Mon of the months and a few Tuesdays per…

spots.name: Lavander Garden
spots.desc: This vegetarian restaurant is in Tianmu directly at the base of the Tianmu trail. Good place to go when starting on a hike up or to relax when finishing a hike down.

spots.name: Shiyang Culture Restaurant
spots.desc: Taipei's classiest creative cuisine, near Lengshuikeng area.

spots.name: Tropic of Cancer Avenue
spots.local: 虎井嶼北回歸線追日大道
spots.desc: A decorative concrete 'avenue' which marks the point at which the Tropic of Cancer passes through the island.

spots.name: Hijing Military Observatory
spots.desc: A decommissioned military obersvation point with a number of rooms set up as they would have been when the facility was in use.

spots.name: Penghu Martyrs' Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine to those who lost their lives in the service of Taiwan, built on the site of a previous Japanese colonial era temple to Prince Kitashirakawa Yoshihisa.

spots.name: Hujing Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: A temple to the Goddess of Mercy, Guanyin, with a highly decorated roof on the island of Hujing.

spots.name: Guanyinting Recreation Area
spots.desc: An outdoor area of sports grounds, beaches, parkland, and the multi-coloured Xiying Rainbow Bridge.

spots.name: Guanyin Park
spots.desc: A park on the western side of Hujing island which features a large statue of Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy.

spots.name: One House
spots.desc: Small pub with a full bar and a larger upstairs area. Thursday night is Tourist Night, 20 percent off on all drinks. No English menu.

spots.name: Freud
spots.desc: Old fashioned pub, good mixed drinks, good selections of beers. (You can even get a Guinness here!) Also serving food with a full menu in English.

spots.name: Southernmost point of Taiwan
spots.desc: A sculpture representing the southernmost tip of Taiwan. Famous with the locals for pictures and a great sunset spot.
spots.price: No admission, but parking fee NT$50

spots.name: Eulanbi Lighthouse
spots.desc: The surrounding park area is well worth the trip past Kenting. The lighthouse is pretty bland, but the easy hiking trails are pleasant and near the ocean.

spots.name: Longpan Park
spots.desc: A scenic geological formation formed by levels of the coast separately lowering and getting washed away by the sea. Now, a very green and picturesque coast line and cliff. Also check out .

spots.name: Fongchueisha (Dune)
spots.desc: A large and picturesque dune. You can walk down it on its right flank.

spots.name: Chuhuo Eternal Fire
spots.desc: An interesting sight where natural gas escapes from under the earth through porous rock. It is alighted and constantly burns. You can even alight smaller spots by yourself with a lighter – there are about 6-7 of them where gas emerges. Best time to come here is during sunset when the place dives into the night and allows for great pictures, given you have the right photo equipment.

spots.name: Maobitou
spots.desc: A beautiful black cliff and coastal area, which is great for sunsets. The rock formation is supposed to look like a lying cat, with a lot of imagination. Nevertheless, the price is probably not worth the tiny walkway, seems more like a tourist trap. You should rather go for Longpan Park instead – equally or more beautiful.

spots.name: Houbihu (Marina)
spots.desc: A mildly picturesque and small harbour. Just nearby, also a coral and power exhibition can be found – quite obvious with the nuclear plant right to the east.

spots.name: Chuanfan Rock
spots.desc: A huge rock at this stony beach, which allows for pretty pictures.

spots.name: Sheding Natural Park
spots.desc: There is a free trail (about 1½-2 hours of walking) but you have to pay a small parking fee. The gorges are fairly interesting to look at and there are views of the southern tip of the coast.

spots.name: Kenting National Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: A beautiful forest and jungle area, but it seems quite expensive, unless you are a botanist. The Stalagmite Cave closed as of Nov 2017. Also, the Fairy Cave does not seem to be open constantly – best to inquire at the entrance. If you must do this park, you definitely need to do the extended walk until the "First Ravine" – the backmost part is much more worth it.

spots.name: Afei Surf
spots.desc: Surf courses, tours and board rental. They also run two Balinese-style hostels, one in Nanwan, the other in Jialeshui.

spots.name: Kenting Night Market
spots.desc: At night the main road in Kenting becomes a night market, with all kinds of food sold from stalls.

spots.name: Gelato (?)
spots.desc: Delicious gelato and a great place to have an afternoon snack. There is seating in front of the storefront.

spots.name: Chinese Seafood
spots.desc: The seafood is delicious and worth ordering the fish of the day. It is very reasonably priced unlike some of the other seafood eateries offering live fish.

spots.name: Santosa Restaurant
spots.desc: Cheap Thai food that is delicious and filling. Try the seafood fried rice and the basil chicken. The restaurant owner is very friendly.

spots.name: Warung DiDi
spots.desc: Seems to be the most popular restaurant in Kenting, serving a variety of pan-Asian food. A little hard to find, and fills up quickly, but worth a visit.
spots.addr: No. 26 Wenhua Lane, Kenting Rd, Kenting

spots.name: The Rock Garden
spots.desc: Lovely place in a garden setting, great for a lunch outdoors.

spots.name: Bossa Nova beach cafe
spots.desc: Cool beach cafe with one of the rare ocean view in the area. Solid menu with a large Asian selection and a western section as well. Wine, coffee, desserts. Look for Claire, the owner. She is a local and a longtime body boarder, always ready to help you with any info you might need.

spots.name: Beach Bistro
spots.desc: Beach Bistro is a Greek-style seaside restaurant which offers a mixture of Asian and European recipes. The owner, Chang Chung-Ho, was born in Kenting and travels to France every year, so his cooking inevitably has become French-oriented but with an Asian touch, resulting in an Asia-Euro "Nouvelle Cuisine" with unique dishes in a particularly relaxed and friendly atmosphere.
spots.addr: No.230, Changfun Rd.Eluan village. Hengchun Township, Pingtung County

spots.name: Chez Papa
spots.desc: Moroccan-style restaurant which offers a mixture of Asian and European recipes. The owner, Gillou, was born in France, so his food is French-oriented, but with an Asian touch. Also features a big selection of Belgium beers and wines, and cocktails. Relaxed and friendly atmosphere.

spots.name: 人和素食館
spots.desc: This vegetarian restaurant offers succulent Taiwanese delicates. The mushroom-dish, a must try, is recommended by the owner.
spots.price: Your plate is weighed to calculate the price. A good plate costs about NT$100

spots.name: Taiping Street

spots.name: Hushan Temple

spots.name: Nansheng Temple

spots.name: Douliu Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: A 15,000 seat stadium which has hosted a number of games of the CPBL as well as of the Asia Winter Baseball League.

spots.desc: The fumaroles in this area are particularly notable.

spots.desc: An old family residence built for the Hsu family.

spots.desc: An ornate, dark red temple on Tongpan island.

spots.desc: Nice for a stroll around the centre.

spots.desc: This is either coral or volcanic rock.
