spots.desc: Decent and beautiful beach to take a dip.

spots.name: White Sand Bay
spots.desc: Remote and beautiful beach.

spots.name: Hengchun Night Market
spots.desc: Not as busy as Kenting, but worthwhile staying in Hengchun.

spots.name: Soy Sauce Brewing Museum
spots.desc: A soy sauce factory where visitors can tour the facility.

spots.name: Lugang Mazu Temple
spots.desc: A famous Mazu Temple, after many expansions and renovations, completed today's exquisite and magnificent Lugang Mazu Temple. In the palace there are plaques of Emperor Qianlong and Emperor Guangxu.

spots.name: Tropic of Cancer Marker
spots.desc: A white landmark has been built to mark the Tropic of Cancer passing through Hualien County here. The most popular time to visit the landmark is noon on summer solstice, when the sun is right above you and does not cast a shadow. There are parking spots and public toilets nearby.

spots.name: Memorial Sclupture to the Victims of the South-link Highway
spots.local: 南迴公路罹难者慰灵碑
spots.desc: A stone memorial to those who have lost their lives on the highway.

spots.name: Ai Garden
spots.desc: An area of traditional gardens featuring a number of local trees and plants.

spots.name: Yilan Martyrs' Shrine
spots.desc: A memorial complex featuring a shrine to fallen soldiers, a long staircase up to a temple, as well as some decomissioned military hardware surrounded by parkland.

spots.name: Loyalty Arch
spots.desc: A large stone wall with a doorway set into it which visitors must pass through to access the village. There is a bronze statue of an ROC soldier atop the arch.

spots.name: Matsu Distillery
spots.desc: As every region in Taiwan is famous for something, Matsu is known for its rice wine, Gaoliang. It is incredibly strong and the smell can not be missed. The Distillery can be found by just using your nose. They will have you watch a movie and then liberally provide you with shots. It is a definitely recommended trip, that you may potentially forget (be careful!).

spots.name: Wuliaojian
spots.desc: A very strenuous and challenging hike, including many steep rocky sections with ropes to pull yourself up. But the hard work is rewarded with incredible views of the mountains, including segments of the trails that go along knife-edge ridges. Bring gloves (to protect your hands from rope burn), snacks, and plenty of water. Takes about six hours for experienced hikers; inexperienced hikers should…
spots.price: No permit or entry fee is needed

spots.name: Yuanxing House
spots.desc: A small building behind the visitor's information centre which was the birthplace of the first democratically elected President in Taiwan's history.

spots.name: Ningxia Night Market
spots.desc: Crowded, narrow, and busy with customers including lots of tourists—Ningxia Night Market is one of the oldest night markets in Taipei, and specializes in Taiwanese snack foods, like stinky tofu and oyster and egg omelets. Most stalls have English signs as well as Chinese. Try the taro balls!

spots.name: Yenping Old Street
spots.desc: A street where a few old buildings have been preserved. There are a number of stalls here selling local snacks and specialities.

spots.name: Husheng Temple (Glass Temple)
spots.desc: A unique temple that resembles the traditional temple architecture, but is made of glass. The temple is dedicated to the goddess Mazu. The temple is across the road from the Taiwan Glass Gallery.

spots.name: Yongjing Public School Dormitory
spots.desc: A Japanese-style dormitory building which housed students of the public school. The building was constructed in 1929.

spots.name: Fourways Cheese Museum
spots.desc: A small museum that exhibits various aspects of the dairy industry and cheese-making.

spots.name: Matsu temple
spots.desc: The largest Matsu statue in Taiwan can be seen here. To get here from the train station, leave by the west exit and go down Bo-Ai Street (the main road running out the west exit) and make a right on Longfeng Rd. It takes 20-30 minutes walking.

spots.name: Desheng Temple
spots.desc: An ornate, multi-storey temple originally constructed in 1870.

spots.name: Guotai Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwan-style night market featuring a number of snacks, games, and other stalls selling a variety of wares.

spots.name: Zhunan Second Market
spots.local: 竹南第二公有零售市場
spots.desc: A covered market featuring food, homewares, and other items.

spots.name: Red Forest
spots.desc: 紅林 (pinyin: hóng-lín) means Red Forest in English. Popular with locals, Hong Lin is a teppanyaki or tiě bǎn shāo (鐵板燒) restaurant that serves a variety of meat, vegetable and seafood dishes cooked in full view on a flat grill. Dishes include pork, beef, lamb, cuttlefish, shrimp, cod, mushrooms and omelettes. Main courses can be had as a set with rice, vegetables and soup. Prices vary between…

spots.name: MínZú Street
spots.desc: There are lots of cheap street food stalls and small restaurants on this street, particularly near Wellcome supermarket. The "Ji Pai Fan" (black pepper chicken plate) from 2nd shop to the right of Wellcome is particularly good, as are the bantiao (flat noodles) & dumplings from the cart under the purple-signed clothing store. This cart is usually next to a guabao "Taiwanese hamburger" kiosk which…

spots.name: Fantastic Thai
spots.desc: Authentic Thai food. This is a small, family run place with friendly service. English menu available.

spots.name: Guo Ding hot pot shop
spots.desc: A hot pot shop, good indoor atmosphere, delicious meat and soup good.

spots.name: TTL Jhunan Brewery Product Display Center
spots.desc: An outlet for Taiwan's largest brewery where you can browse and buy from their range of beverages and related paraphrenalia.

spots.name: Jo Ku
spots.desc: a bar, restaurant and bakery a little bit away from the center of town, but one of the few places to get decent Western-style food in Zhunan.

spots.name: Taiwan Craft Cultural Park
spots.desc: A complex featuring a number of stores selling locally made handicrafts.

spots.name: Fang Shi Lu Ang Glass Gallery
spots.desc: A museum/gallery which specialises in coloured glass and leadlighting works.

spots.name: Yoshantea Tea Culture House
spots.desc: Housed in an old tea factory, the Culture House has a number of exhibits on the history of tea production in Taiwan.

spots.name: Xitou Forest
spots.desc: Jhushan is the closest town to Xitou, one of Taiwan's most popular mountain weekend destinations, at 1,000m above sea level in a 100-year-old artificial cedar forest. Accessible by direct bus routes from town. Owned by National Taiwan University, which does forestry research there. Next door is the "Monster Village", a Japanese-enchanted-forest themed tourist village. See article for more…

spots.name: Qinglong Waterfall
spots.desc: A 116m high waterfall that lies along a popular hiking trail.

spots.name: Thursday Night Market
spots.desc: A variety of local snacks are available here, such as: octopus balls, milk tea, Dongshan duck head, and fried chicken.

spots.name: Mingxin Academy
spots.desc: Built in 1885 during the Qing Dynasty rule as the first private school within the area, the complex is a well-preserved example of the pre-colonial educational system in Taiwan.

spots.name: Jiji Wuchang Temple
spots.desc: The remains of a temple that collapsed during the earthquake in 1999. No one died, and staff risked their safety to recover the deity statues from the collapsed building - a deed that they believe has brought good fortune. And sure enough, an even bigger temple, impressive on its own, has been been rebuilt in front of the collapsed on.

spots.name: Taishun Gallery Bridge
spots.desc: A picturesque life-sized replica of one of the historic covered bridges of Taishun County in Wenzhou, Mainland China, built from wood without any nails. The bridge was built for Wuchang Temple as a gift from an associated temple in China. Free entry during daylight hours.

spots.name: Jiji Military History Park
spots.desc: An open-air museum featuring examples of Republic of China military hardware.

spots.name: Wujie Dam
spots.desc: A concrete gravity dam which diverts water towards the reservoir in Sun Moon Lake. Construction on the dam began in 1919 and was completed in 1934.

spots.name: Huisun Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: An area of forest land managed by the Department of Agriculture of National Chung Hsing University.

spots.name: Main Peak
spots.desc: It should take no more than 45 min to go up to the top and down again from the road. An alternative to just walking back is the trail that continues northeast towards the same road but further north – the place there is called , it is where many tourist make a stop and where also you can find the Song Syue Lodge. This alternative trail leads 300 m through an army area at the end (see…

spots.name: East Peak
spots.desc: This should likewise not take longer than 45 min. The track either start at the Wuling Bus Stop, directly in Song Xue Lou at the main road or just behind the Song Syue Lodge. Getting down, choose one of these three routes.

spots.name: North Peak
spots.desc: This peak is the more difficult one. It takes at least 2 hr to go up to the north peak and down again from the road. In spring and fall take something warm for the head, long pants and a wind-breaker jacket, and maybe a pair of gloves. You can continue further after the peak. The trail eventually lead to the road leading to Lishan.

spots.name: Qingjing Skywalk
spots.desc: A high-altitude scenic walkway at an elevation of approximately 1,800 meters.

spots.name: Swiss Garden
spots.desc: A small outdoor area with a cafe and campsite that takes inspiration from Swiss architectural style and ambiance.

spots.name: The Yushan National Park Headquarters
spots.desc: Not within the National Park, but along the road on the way to it by car

spots.name: Shuili River
spots.desc: The river that runs through the middle of Shuili town and along the edge of Checheng village.

spots.name: Minghu Dam
spots.desc: A concrete gravity dam on the Shuili River 7 km (4.3 mi) north of Shuili Township. Upon completion, it became Taiwan's first pumped-storage hydroelectricity power plant, officially named Takuan Power Plant.

spots.name: Mingtan Dam
spots.desc: A dam that spans the Shuili River about 4 km downstream from the outlet of Sun Moon Lake. Good views of the bottom of the dam from Checheng village. The reservoir above it is walkable from Checheng Station, but you can't get close to the top of the dam.

spots.name: Daguan Tunnel
spots.desc: Built around 1919 as a railway tunnel and later converted into a road tunnel, this old brick tunnel was constructed to serve the Sun Moon Lake hydropower plant.

spots.name: Checheng Logging Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: Taiwan banned all logging of natural forests in 1991, so the timber industry is now a topic of historical interest.

spots.name: Nitakayama Monument
spots.desc: A boundry marker erected during the Japanese occupation of Taiwan.

spots.name: Shuili Snake Kiln Ceramics Cultural Park
spots.local: 水里蛇窯陶藝文化園區
spots.desc: A ceramic kiln in Dingkan Village built in 1927. The park now has a workshop where visitors can try their hand at pottery-making.

spots.name: Batongguan Mifumisa
spots.desc: Yushan National Park Souvenir Shop, Application Summit/Climbing Certificate

spots.name: Checheng Old Street
spots.desc: Straight up the hill from the railyard and museums is the original Checheng village, now with food and other shopping along a central stairway, a bit like a lesser version of Jiufen.

spots.name: Shiti Fishing Port
spots.desc: There are 3 whale watching ships in the port, which together can carry almost 150 people.

spots.name: Jici Beach
spots.desc: A scenic crescent-shaped beach popular for swimming in the summer and surfing in the winter.

spots.name: Rafting
spots.desc: A portion of Xiuguluan River, from Rueisuei Bridge to Changhong Bridge, is the most popular destination for rafting in Taiwan.

spots.name: Ina flyingfish restaurant
spots.desc: Seafood shared dishes restaurant, Smoked dishes will also be available from 15:00 to 17:00, including flying fish, pork, swordfish, and flying fish roe sausages.

spots.name: Guangfu Night Market
spots.desc: A small, but typical Taiwanese night market where you can get snacks, play a few games, and browse through the stalls selling a variety of different wares.

spots.name: Cifadahan Traditional Amis Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves food in the traditional style of the indigenous Amis people.

spots.name: Mainland Dumplings
spots.desc: A variety of handmade dumplings. The menu is in Chinese only.

spots.name: Mongolian Danbing
spots.desc: A Taiwan-style breakfast restaurant specialising in danbing.

spots.name: Saoba Stone Pillars
spots.desc: The site consists of two adjacent stone pillars standing with 5.75 meters and 3.99 meters of height. The stone pillar are artifacts from Beinan culture since Stone Age era around 3,000 years ago.

spots.name: Ruisui Hot Springs
spots.desc: Ruisui's pristine natural beauty is a must to experience during a trip to Hualien. Ruisui Hot Springs originated from the upper stream of Hongye Stream. The water from Ruisui Hot Springs is alkaline sodium carbonate, perfect for osmosis detox and cleansing, with a pH ranging between 6 and 7. The high altitude of Ruisui Hot Springs offers a magnificent view of the surrounding mountains and plains.…

spots.name: Ningcheng Temple
spots.desc: The temple is the only temple to the 'King of the Three Hills' and also serves the local land god.

spots.name: Yushui Beach
spots.desc: A beach popular with couples. Gemstones can occasionally be found on the beach, although it is illegal to remove them.

spots.name: Shimen-Changbin Bicycle Trail
spots.desc: This 27-km-long cycling trail begins in Fongbin Township and ends in Changbin. The track passes through the Shihtiping Scenic Area.

spots.name: Xiaoma Tunnel
spots.desc: A small tunnel that is a remnant of the Japanese colonial period that you can walk through.

spots.name: The Marine Environmental Education Center of Chenggong Yacht Marina
spots.desc: A small exhibition center showcasing a variety of objects of the marine industry in the area. The staff are able to help visitors navigate the exhibits if requested.

spots.name: Man Stone
spots.desc: A large stone plateau that features a small shrine in a cave beneath that contains a large stone phallus statue.

spots.name: Chishang Waterwheel
spots.desc: A wooden water wheel which was constructed to help irrigate the surrounding farmland.

spots.name: Rice Village Museum
spots.desc: The museum was established by Wan'an Community Development Association in 1994 by transforming an unused fertilizer warehouse. The museum regularly holds various activities such as guided tours of rice farming and travel as well as painting activities.

spots.name: Taitung County Hakka Museum
spots.desc: A small museum showcasing the history and culture of the Hakka people in the area.

spots.name: Great View Pavilion
spots.desc: A wooden pavilion which offers clear views of the fields in the surrounding area.

spots.name: Mr Brown Road
spots.desc: A long and picturesque road that cuts through the rice fields. The name itself comes from a brand of coffee sold in Taiwan.

spots.name: Nine Dragons Guanyin statue
spots.desc: A small religious site featuring a large white statue of Guanyin perched on the hillside and facing out to sea.

spots.name: Paiwan House
spots.desc: A cultural attraction showcasing the traditional culture of the local indigenous peoples.

spots.name: Dawu Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwan-style night market selling snack and a variety of other things.

spots.name: Dengxian Bridge Recreation Area
spots.desc: A rest area which is common for people who come to feed the monkeys that live in the area.

spots.name: Dulan Park
spots.desc: Various agricultural product souvenirs and handicraft DIY courses.
spots.hours: 09:00–17:00, closed on the last day of every month.

spots.name: Marino's Kitchen
spots.desc: Excellent fresh baked bread and homemade sauces all week, Saturday and Sunday fresh pasta meals, including soup/salad, fresh bread and drink. Owned and operated by Dave and Rolly Marino.

spots.name: Wu-Lu Ancient Fort
spots.desc: An old fort that contains two old cannons left from the Japanese colonial period.

spots.name: Wulu Gorge
spots.desc: A gorge carved by the Wulu river through the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Atayal Life Museum
spots.desc: Atayal Life Museum of Datong Township is the largest cultural and historical museum displaying the life of the Atayal tribe. The main exhibition is about the knitting technique and the working life of the Atayal people. In the museum, you can try on the traditional Atayal costumes and take pictures. There is also a small souvenir shop inside the Atayal Living Museum.

spots.name: Tuchang Railway Station
spots.desc: A former lumber train station that is now an open-air museum to the rail history of the area.

spots.name: Qilan Forest Recreation Area
spots.desc: The forests consists of Taiwan's largest giant tree cluster. It also contains a villa used by former President Chiang Kai-shek.

spots.name: Bong Bong Train
spots.desc: A reproduction of an older train that was used to transport timber from Taipingshan. The small train now takes tourists to Maosing Station. Spaces on the train are limited.

spots.name: Jiuzhize Nature Trail
spots.desc: A short (1.5 km) trail that begins on the far side of the Jioujhihze Bridge. It offers an introduction to some of the native flora of the area.

spots.name: Jancing Historic Trail
spots.desc: A short (0.9 km) hiking trail that runs beside an old timber mining train track.

spots.name: Cueifong Lake Circular Trail
spots.desc: A 4 km trail that follows the old logging trails around Cueifong Lake.

spots.name: Maosing Reminiscent Trail
spots.desc: A short (1 km) trail that winds around the area surroundiing Maosing Station (at the end of the Bong Bong train) that features a number of lookout platforms to let you take in the mountain views.

spots.name: Dongshan Old Street
spots.desc: A historical street near the train station which features some older buildings, as well as a number of murals painted onto the walls.

spots.name: Kites Museum
spots.desc: A small museum near the train station dedicated to kites and kite-making.

spots.name: Dongshan Mr. Brown Avenue
spots.desc: A road that runs through a farmer's fields which is a popular spot for locals to take photographs.

spots.name: Wofongci Waterfall
spots.desc: The site has three waterfalls. At the lower waterfall, there is a small pond where visitors can take a rest. Then they can keep walking for about 15 minutes to reach the second waterfall, where there is a pavilion for resting. If you want to see the waterfall at the top, you will need to walk for a further 30 minutes.

spots.name: Longtan Lake
spots.desc: Longtan Lake is the biggest of the five major lakes in the Lanyang plain. It is enclosed with hills on three sides. There are several temples on the hillsides and a trail encircles the lake. It’s located in Jiaosi Township (礁溪鄉) and 6 km away from Yilan center. It attracts many tourists especially during weekends, and people go fishing and picnicking there in spring and summer.

spots.name: Catholic Sanctuary of Our Lady of Wufengqi
spots.desc: Round Catholic sanctuary building perched on a hillside with picturesque views.

spots.name: Shengmu (Marian) Hiking Trail
spots.desc: After entering in the Wufongci Scenic Area, walk down the industrial path where you’ll see a Catholic church. Keep walking uphill for about 3 to 4 km and there’s a wood stele in front of the trail entrance.

spots.name: Luodong Sports Park
spots.desc: The biggest attraction in Luodung. There are basketball courts, tennis courts, a professional baseball field, a track for exercise, in addition to areas for strolling, fish feeding (Japanese Grass Carp) and other outdoor activities.

spots.name: Luodong Forestry Culture Park
spots.desc: Located on the north side of Luodung. It is built around two logging ponds from the Japanese logging era. The main attractions here are the old train engines and the giant tree stump sculptures.

spots.name: Luodong Cathedral of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
spots.desc: The city's Catholic cathedral located in the central-eastern part of the town.

spots.name: Luodong Cultural Working House
spots.desc: An area of open parkland where there are often arts performances and workshops.

spots.name: Yilan County Natural History Education Center
spots.desc: A national level museum dedicated to the natural environment with both indoor and outdoor attractions and exhibits.

spots.name: Luodong Night Market
spots.desc: located on three sides of Jungshan Park, is full of food stalls all with traditional Taiwanese cuisine. Try the oyster omelette, fried rice noodles, or filled tapioca starch balls. For the brave at heart, or smelling impaired, try the stinky tofu. Good buys are dried fruit from Yilan County and an abundance of costume jewelry.
spots.addr: intersection of Xindong Rd and Minsheng Rd

spots.name: Military Tunnels
spots.desc: A historical relic from the period when Guishan Island was under military control. The tunnel is 800 meters long and stays pleasantly cool inside.

spots.name: Gengfang Southwest Coastal Scenic Area
spots.desc: A scenic coastal area offering open sea views, rocky shorelines, and coastal walking paths. It is especially popular at sunset and provides a peaceful place to enjoy the ocean landscape.

spots.name: Wai'ao Rocky Shore
spots.desc: Wai'ao Rock Reef is a dramatic stretch of rocky coastline, known for its volcanic rock formations and ocean views. The area is ideal for seaside walks, photography, and wave watching, with easy access from the main coastal road.

spots.name: Hill 401
spots.desc: The highest point on Guishan Island, at an elevation of 398 meters, with a 3-meter-high bunker at the top. It takes about an hour to reach the summit via the hiking trail. Advance registration is required to access the summit.

spots.name: Xietian Temple
spots.local: 頭城大坑里協天宮關聖帝君
spots.desc: A historic Taoist temple dedicated to Guan Yu, known for its traditional architecture and role as a local center of worship. Visitors can observe daily rituals and enjoy a quiet, atmospheric stop while exploring Toucheng.

spots.name: Lanyang Museum
spots.desc: The Lanyang Museum showcases the natural landscape and cultural history of Yilan County. Its architecture reflects the coastal landforms of the region, and the exhibitions provide useful background on local geography, industry, and daily life.

spots.name: Qing Dynasty Wushi Harbor Relics
spots.desc: A small exhibition space introducing the history of Wushi Harbor and its role in regional trade and maritime development.

spots.name: Toucheng Cultural and Creative Center
spots.desc: A local exhibition venue hosting rotating displays related to regional culture, crafts, and community history.

spots.name: Toucheng Ghost Grappling Competition
spots.desc: A traditional folk event held in Toucheng during the Ghost Festival in the seventh lunar month. The main competition is typically held around central Toucheng, with ritual activities, bamboo tower climbing, and community ceremonies.
spots.hours: Seventh lunar month (main competition held on the final day; dates vary annually)

spots.name: Toucheng Old Street
spots.desc: Small local shops selling traditional snacks, dried seafood, and simple souvenirs. A convenient place to pick up local products while exploring the historic old street.

spots.name: Wushi Harbor Seafood Market
spots.desc: Seafood stalls and small vendors offering dried fish, squid, and other seafood products sourced from the nearby harbor. Prices and selection vary by season.

spots.name: Toucheng Farmers’ Association Agricultural Products Center
spots.local: 頭圍農驛品牌館-頭城鎮農會農特產展售中心
spots.desc: A local market where vendors sell seasonal fruits, vegetables, and regional agricultural products. Availability depends on market days and seasons.

spots.name: Shengshi Teppanyaki
spots.desc: An upscale teppanyaki restaurant offering set meals prepared at the counter, suitable for special occasions or a formal dining experience.

spots.name: Toucheng Station Abo Scallion Pancakes
spots.local: 頭城車站阿伯炸蛋蔥油餅
spots.desc: A popular street food stall near Toucheng Train Station specializing in Taiwanese scallion pancakes with egg. A convenient stop for a quick snack while arriving or departing by train.
spots.addr: Near Toucheng Train Station, Zuanxiang Rd

spots.name: Jiang Ke Fu Brunch & Pasta
spots.local: 匠客福／早午餐義大利麵
spots.desc: A casual restaurant serving brunch dishes and Italian-style pasta, with a small dining area suitable for a relaxed meal near the old town.

spots.name: Qiduguowu Hot Pot
spots.desc: A hot pot restaurant offering individual hot pot sets with a variety of meats and vegetables, suitable for a casual meal near the old town area.

spots.name: Tea Tree Bistro
spots.desc: A Japanese-style restaurant offering set menus that vary by day, focusing on seasonal ingredients in a quiet dining setting.

spots.name: Crown House
spots.desc: A casual café and bistro offering coffee, light meals, and barbecue dishes, with both indoor and outdoor seating available.

spots.name: Sukiyaki
spots.desc: A sukiyaki restaurant serving set meals featuring sliced beef and vegetables, suitable for sit-down dining in a modern setting.

spots.name: Lanhai Italian Kitchen
spots.desc: An Italian-style restaurant serving pasta and Western dishes, suitable for a relaxed meal near the harbor area.

spots.name: Xiaohau Seafood
spots.desc: A seafood restaurant near Wushi Harbor serving a variety of fresh local seafood dishes, popular with visitors exploring the harbor area.

spots.name: Beiguan Seafood City
spots.desc: A seafood restaurant near Beiguan Coastal Area serving a range of local seafood dishes, convenient for travelers visiting the nearby tidal park and coastal attractions.

spots.name: No. 9 Coffee Stone Castle
spots.desc: A café along the coast near Shicheng offering coffee and light meals, with sea views popular among travelers driving along the northeastern coastline.

spots.name: MR.BROWN Cafe
spots.local: Mr. Brown 伯朗咖啡館 - 城堡二門市
spots.desc: A branch of Taiwan’s well-known Mr. Brown Coffee chain located near the coast. The café offers a comfortable indoor seating area, a full range of coffee drinks, light meals, and desserts. A convenient stop for a break after visiting Wai’ao Beach or the Lanyang Museum, with reliable Wi-Fi and a relaxed atmosphere.

spots.name: Drifters Pizza Pub
spots.desc: A relaxed pizza pub near Wai'ao Beach, popular with surfers and travelers. Serves pizza along with beer and other alcoholic drinks.

spots.name: Kanea Garden Pizza Bar
spots.desc: A casual outdoor pizza bar with a garden setting. A good place to enjoy beer and light drinks in the evening.

spots.name: Opposite the Island Yakitori & Izakaya
spots.local: 島的對面 串燒&居酒屋
spots.desc: A Japanese-style izakaya serving grilled skewers, beer, and sake. A good option for drinks with food.

spots.name: Lucas Bistro
spots.desc: A bistro-style bar offering alcoholic drinks along with Western and local dishes. Suitable for dinner and drinks.

spots.name: Dr-Duck
spots.desc: A smoked duck factory where visitors can take guided tours of the facility.

spots.name: Duck Shack Museum
spots.desc: A museum about ducks where visitors can feed the ducks that live on the premises.

spots.name: Yilan Tang Zheng Hot Pot Restaurant
spots.desc: Hotpot restaurant where you cook your own food in a pot in the centre of the table.

spots.name: Kingcar Orchid Garden
spots.desc: A plant nursery, founded in 1988, which showcases a wide varieties of orchid. The facility also offers guided tours.

spots.name: Yuanshan Hangar
spots.desc: A small museum dedicated to the history of the airforce based in the area.

spots.name: Bee Farmer
spots.desc: A small establishment which feature a number of exhibits related to bee-keeping. The facility also produces honey and visitors can buy products made on-site.

spots.name: Wanglong Lake
spots.desc: An area around the Wanglong lake which features bridges across the water, sitting out areas, and hiking trails.

spots.name: Baima Zunwang Temple
spots.desc: A small free-standing temple. The name means 'White Horse King'.

spots.name: Qinbi Tianhou Temple
spots.desc: A temple to the goddess of seafarers Tianhou, also commonly called 'Mazu' in Taiwan and Japan.

spots.name: Daqiu Island
spots.desc: Accessible during peak season by ferry, boats can also be chartered to get there during the off-season. The island is now uninhabited and is known for its population of Formosan sika deer.

spots.name: Ganen Pavilion
spots.desc: A small gazebo situated on an island in the middle of the bridge which links the two islands. The gazebo covers a statue of the former President of the ROC, Chiang Ching-kuo.

spots.name: Sanshan Strongpoint
spots.desc: At the end of the peninsular there are a number of gun emplacements that the public can access for taking photos.

spots.name: The Northernmost Frontier
spots.desc: This is the northernmost point of land controlled by the ROC government. In 2006, it was developed into a scenic spot and a stone monument inscribed with Northernmost Frontier (國之北疆) was erected. Out from the observatory, the north is the endless sea, and the west is the famous Luohanping (Lohan Flat) (羅漢坪), aka Three-Colored Stone (三色石).

spots.name: Xiyin Triumph Monument
spots.desc: A large monument painted on the hillside to extol mankind's struggle over nature.

spots.name: Suicide Cliff
spots.desc: It is said that in Qing Dynasty a fisherman’s wife was kidnapped by mobsters to this island. Resisting, she escaped to this cliff, jumped off, and died. To commemorate her chastity, this cliff is named Suicide Cliff.

spots.name: Qingshui'ao
spots.desc: An area worn flat by erosion from the sea where local sit and contemplate.

spots.name: Houao
spots.desc: Features a number of unusual rock formations which have been carved into unusual shapes by eons of erosion from the sea.

spots.name: Crouching Crocodile
spots.desc: The long peninsular, when viewed from the land opposite, resembles a semi-submerged crocodile.

spots.name: Dongyong Sports Park
spots.desc: An outdoor sporting facility featuring a running track and grassed area.

spots.name: Dongyin Matsu Distillery
spots.desc: A working distillery making Moutai. There is an information centre which outlines the history of the industry, as well as a shop where visitors can buy some.

spots.name: Dapu Inscription
spots.desc: The stone carving was done in 1617 to commemorate the achievements of the local garrison in dealing with pirates which were harassing the local population.

spots.name: Ching-kuo Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Built in a similar vein to the Chiang Kai-shek memorial in Taipei, this complex is built to honour his son, Chiang Ching-kuo.

spots.name: Daao Old Street
spots.desc: An old area of the island featuring a number of old stone buildings.

spots.name: Blue Tear Museum
spots.desc: A small museum focusing on the marine life in the area. This museum has very little material available in English.

spots.name: Nioujiao (Fuxing) Village
spots.desc: Beautiful granite village built at the edge of a mountain on the sea. Check out the temple on the harbor and spend hours getting lost in its tranquility.

spots.name: Leemo's Restaurant
spots.desc: A local restaurant in Niujiao village, operating in a traditional-style stone building.

spots.name: Furen Cafe
spots.desc: A small cafe by the sea which is housed in an old, traditional-style stone house.

spots.name: Cosmos De Isla
spots.desc: A cafe built by an old couple of painters who went to Spain to study art. Rosario and Kai, the local artists, built this cafe with two decades of art creations including paintings, sculptures, and art book collections.
spots.addr: 連江縣南竿鄉復興村26號

spots.name: Jiang A-Sin Ancient House
spots.desc: An old, historic house. There are guided tours of the house available.

spots.name: Beipu Cold Spring
spots.desc: A scenic area which contains a waterfall, fish pong, and a number of picnic facilities.

spots.name: Shang Ping Old Street
spots.desc: A somewhat run-down street of historic brick buildings that give some idea of what the area looked like in a by-gone era.

spots.name: Xiao Ru-Song Art Park
spots.desc: An exhibition of art from the area housed in historic, Japanese-era buildings.

spots.name: Hwei Chang Temple
spots.desc: The San Shan Kuo Wan Temple, means the Temple worship three kings from mountain. The Temple was established by Hakka cultivators on 1810. Mr. Pon Chin Ho rebuilt it on 1821. At the same year, the Dan Shwei Governor(Northern Taiwan), Mr. Lee gave the Temple an honorable name "Kins of Justice". After few years, Mr. Pon Tian Lai and the other twelve members utilize wooden constructional to renew the…

spots.name: Zhudong Ecological Riverside Park
spots.desc: A pleasant riverside park that contains a number of historic structures and old, disused water wheels. There is also a cycle path.

spots.name: Zhongyang Market
spots.desc: A varied market selling a variety of snacks, homewares, and other items.

spots.name: Zhudong Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwanese night market with all manner of local snacks, games, and bric-a-brac.

spots.name: Northern Noodles
spots.desc: A reasonably-priced restaurant specialising in 'northern-style noodles'.

spots.name: Bao Sir
spots.desc: A noodle and dumpling shop that is popular with locals and often has a long line.

spots.name: Hidden Garden Elemental Soup Noodles
spots.desc: A home-style vegetarian restaurant decorated with calligraphy that also has its own snack shop.

spots.name: Yuquan Breakfast Restaurant
spots.desc: A typical Taiwan-style breakfast restaurant service local fare.

spots.name: A Pang's Soy Milk
spots.desc: A popular spot for Taiwanese-style breakfast. Expect long lines.

spots.name: Mango House
spots.desc: A take-away dessert place; most options are a combination of fruit, ice, and ice-cream but there is also a variety of other options.

spots.name: Old Caoling Tunnel
spots.desc: A tunnel which you can walk through, or rent a bicycle and cycle through.

spots.name: Aodi
spots.desc: A small fishing village popular for its scenic setting and many seafood restaurants.

spots.name: Fulong Dongxing Temple
spots.desc: A seaside temple with a number of large, colourful statues of dragons at the sea-facing side.

spots.name: Longdong
spots.desc: A scenic fishing settlement also known for its interesting rock formations.

spots.name: Longmen Park
spots.desc: A sports park that contains a large suspension bridge and has facilities to hire canoes.

spots.name: Jinbaoli Trail
spots.desc: A long hiking trail that goes into the Yangmingshan National Park. There are a number of stone bridges, abandoned dwellings, and small shrines to see along the route.

spots.name: Linkou Wenhua Garden Night Market
spots.desc: A night market that operates on the streets behind the MRT station.

spots.name: Luzhou Breeze Park
spots.desc: A large park around a lake with a number of sports and leisure facilities.

spots.name: Luzhou Civil Sports Center
spots.desc: A large sports complex and gymnasium. There is no membership required, you just pay per hour.

spots.name: Pinglin Old Street
spots.desc: This pedestrian street is lined mostly with small tea stores.

spots.name: Chen Family's Old House
spots.desc: A historic old house built by Chen Jie Sheng. The house is made of bricks sitting on top of a stone foundation, which was common of houses of wealthier residents at the time.

spots.name: Old Japanese Style Police Station
spots.desc: The police station was built during the period of Japanese occupation and is over a century old.

spots.name: Stone Carving Park
spots.desc: A park on a hillside containing a number of carved stone statues.

spots.name: Shifen Old Street
spots.desc: An unusual market street with a train track running through the middle of it.

spots.name: Zhongpu Iron Bridge
spots.desc: Built in the 1940s, the bridge is used as a 'love bridge' where people can hang messages of love written on bamboo from the railings.

spots.name: The Tsai Mansion
spots.desc: The former residence of the Tsai (蔡) family, built by Tsai Chuan, a local businessman who made his money in mining, in 1939. The house is still maintained by his descendants, although most of the family has since left the area. The house is built in a western red-brick style, which is unusual for the area.

spots.name: Pingxi Guanyin Temple
spots.desc: A temple dedicated to the Goddess of Mercy, Guanyin. The temple itself sits atop a tunnel that leads to a bomb shelter which is also accessible.

spots.name: Golden Waterfall
spots.desc: A stepped series of waterfalls known for its unique golden-brown colour. The water of the waterfall contains high level of toxins due to its proximity to the nearby gold mining area.

spots.name: Shen'ao Elephant Trunk Rock
spots.desc: A rocky outcropping near the sea that used to resemble an elephant's trunk. The trunk and face collapsed in December 2023, losing everything that made it interesting.

spots.name: Nanya Rock
spots.desc: Nanya is renowned for the wind and sea sculpted rock formations scattered along its shores. Facilities in this area include a parking lot, footpaths, and pavilion viewpoints. Nanya is the northern gateway to the Northeast and Yilan Coast National Scenic Area. Here you can take in miles and miles of sea and wind eroded rocks formations and outcroppings dotting the vibrant and pristine coastline…

spots.name: Zhibo Artist’s Village
spots.desc: A small area where there are many artist studios and workshops.

spots.name: Qianshuiwan Seaside Park
spots.desc: A seaside park on the coast which offers views out to sea, but has a reputation for being windy.

spots.name: Datun Nature Park
spots.desc: A large park situated to the south of the city which is a popular hiking spot for locals.

spots.name: Sanzhi-Shimen Cycling Route
spots.desc: An 11km train running from Sanzhi to the neighbouring Shimen district along the waterfront.

spots.name: Pretty Devil
spots.desc: Serves a mix of Taiwanese style breakfast fare and some local takes on 'western' cuisine.

spots.name: Shenkeng Night Market
spots.desc: A typical Taiwanese night market containing food stall, small wares, and games.

spots.name: Da Tuan Yuan
spots.desc: A Chinese-style banquet-style restaurant set in a traditional-style garden. They also have an iguana for some reason.

spots.name: Bagua Tea Plantation
spots.desc: Viewpoint overlooking hills of tea fields extending down to the winding Fetsui Reservoir.
spots.addr: 北宜路六段獅仔頭坑巷16號

spots.name: Luku Incident Memorial Park
spots.desc: A park commemorating one of the worst incidents of the white terror in Taiwan where over 400 people were arrested by the military government of the ROC and about 35 people were eventually executed.

spots.name: Huangdidian
spots.desc: A strenuous trail along a ridge, with many sections of ropes, ladders and exposed cliff sides.

spots.name: North Coast Exploratorium
spots.desc: A tourist centre with a marine theme containing various exhibits and games.

spots.name: Fuji Fishing Harbor
spots.desc: Here you can buy fresh fish and have to prepared in one of the nearby restaurants.

spots.name: Green Mountain Clouds Abode
spots.desc: An open temple set into the hillside with spectacular views and a very unusual gate.

spots.name: Shuangxi Market
spots.desc: A covered market selling snacks, homewares, and a variety of other items.

spots.name: Yehliu Geopark
spots.desc: A peninsula with the interresting rock formations that resemble human heads (Queen's Head), cut tofu, a dragon head or gorilla (with a decent amount of imagination). As of 11/2024 it also contains a large wrecked cargo ship on the north-west of the peninsula.

spots.name: Queen's head
spots.desc: A natural rock formation inside the Geopark which resembles a woman's face.

spots.name: Lin Tian-jen statue
spots.desc: A statue of Lin Tian-jen who drowned nearby attempting to save some students who had fallen into the sea.

spots.name: Futuro House
spots.desc: Also called the "UFO house", a series of odd shaped experimental houses which were built in the 1960s but have since been abandoned. The houses were designed by Finnish architect Matti Suuronen and are one of the few remaining examples left in the world.

spots.name: Lingyun Zen Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple that contains a statue of the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, which is the largest indoor Buddhist statue in Taiwan. The temple serves vegetarian food to visitors on Saturdays and holidays.

spots.name: Lingyun Temple
spots.desc: The oldest temple in the Wugu area, the original temple building was constructed in 1739. Several temples were built and destroyed over the past few centuries and the current building was built in 1933. The temple building itself was constructed of stone from the nearby Guanyin mountain.

spots.name: Shuidui Park
spots.desc: A large area of parkland which contains a number of walking trails snaking up into the nearby mountains where a number of viewing platforms offer good views of the nearby township, and of the natural surrounds.

spots.name: Chaozong Park
spots.desc: The park backs onto the Shuidui park. There is an observatory atop the mountain which has good views of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Yinghe Cave Hiking Trail
spots.desc: A scenic mountain hiking trail that passes under a waterfall.

spots.name: Taiping Temple
spots.desc: A very popular, multi-storey temple on the opposite side of the river to Bintan. It can often get crowded in this temple.

spots.name: Green Hornet Café
spots.desc: Mexican bar/restaurant. A great place to eat some nachos, burritos, enchiladas, pasta, steak with some friends around a beer or some cocktails. The food is great and a relaxed ambiance.
spots.addr: 23147 Taipei, Taiwan1F, 108 Xindian Road - 新北市新店區新店路108號1樓

spots.name: Bruce Kitchen
spots.desc: Rustic reds, French cafe blues and outdoor decking among trees define the decor of this hillside restaurant. Bus number 839 (Danan bus company) stops nearby. Otherwise, private transportation is required. Excellent international vegetarian meals. Prior reservations essential, especially at weekends.

spots.name: Miao-xin
spots.desc: An excellent and cheap menu-type vegetarian restaurant serving traditional Chinese dishes. Cost is NT$100-200 per person.

spots.name: Original Vegan Restaurant
spots.desc: Pure vegan. Clean and simple decor. Japanese cuisine. Great desserts. OK coffee. Fast service.

spots.name: Xiang-gu
spots.desc: 2F, (near the junction with Beixin Road, sec 2). One of Xindian's best vegetarian restaurants - excellent and cheap, specializes in Chinese cuisine, but has a few extra international dishes.

spots.name: Waterside Bistro
spots.desc: a good, albeit expensive place to enjoy tea or coffee. Located on the promenade at Bitan, the cafe offers great views over the lake and the green mountains beyond.

spots.name: Bi-ting
spots.desc: (Emerald Pavilion) at Bitan is a tea house located on the opposite bank of the river to the MRT station (cross pedestrian bridge, immediately turn left and go up stones stairs. Bi-ting Tea House is at the top). While the decor of the tea house is not inspiring, the tea is good and, being located on the top of a cliff, the views of the river and bridge are second to none.

spots.name: Dzongtung
spots.desc: A funky tea house serving various kinds of teas (though don't expect top notch oolong), coffee, freshly made juices and light meals. The interior of the two story cafe is all wood and has some interesting features.

spots.name: Om-Para
spots.desc: The especially comfy chairs make up for the rather drab decor of this cafe. Serves a varieties of coffee brands and simple, but well prepared meals.

spots.name: Shi Yang
spots.desc: Fine dining restaurant serving Taiwanese cuisine with a nice Japanese-inspired ambience, located in the mountains.

spots.name: Sanying Arts Village
spots.desc: A park filled with different sculptures, covered walkways, and other forms of artwork.

spots.name: Wangyang House
spots.desc: An old, and not particularly well-maintained, house nearby the train station. The building was constructed in 1916.

spots.name: Hongde Temple
spots.desc: A temple to the Spring-Autumn Warring States period general Sun Bin.

spots.name: Sanhu Temple
spots.desc: A somewhat unusual temple in Taiwan dedicated to three Emperors which were worshipped to bring prosperity in the early days of Han Chinese migration to the island.

spots.name: Yingge Rock
spots.desc: A short trail (~20 minutes) leads to Yingge Rock (Parrot Rock), the town's namesake. The trail has three entrances. The main trail lifts up to the level of Yingge Stone, from which people can overlook the centre of Yingge area, Dahan Creek and parts of Sansia.

spots.name: Grandma's Sushi
spots.desc: a famous sushi booth in the centre of Yingge. It is located in front of the OK Mart, 10 minutes away from train station on foot. Although it looks like just a small booth, there is a big basement seating area. Usually, people order to go, although some dine in the basement. A box of sushi costs NT$25. Other than sushi, they also have miso soup (NT$10), steamed egg (NT$10) and some other typical…

spots.name: Wenshui Visitor Center
spots.desc: The headquarters of this national park, it is equipped with a display hall, audio-visual room and gift shop. There is the best place to understand anything of the park within a short time. The Visitor Center is open Tu-Su 09:00 to 16:30.
spots.addr: 100 Shueiweiping, Fuxing Village, Dahu Township, Miaoli County

spots.name: Bopiliao Old Street
spots.desc: One of the few, and probably best preserved, examples of Qing dynasty architecture in Taipei. The street features historic red brick buildings which have been well restored and are used for a variety of cultural purposes.
spots.hours: Outdoors Tue-Sun 09:00-21:00, Indoors Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00. Mon closed.

spots.name: Dadaocheng Presbyterian Church
spots.local: 台灣基督長老教會大稻埕教會
spots.desc: The architectural design of this church represents a fusion between traditional Chinese and late 19th-century Western style architecture. It maintains a unique position in the modern architecture of Taiwan, being one of only three extant Presbyterian churches in Taipei built during the Japanese occupation period. Historically, men would enter and exit through the left door, and women would enter…

spots.name: Gui-de Street
spots.desc: Previously called Western Houses Street, this lane once fronted the Danshui River. In the 1880s, the world famous Formosa Oolong Tea came from a nearby wharf. At the time, many wealthy merchants invested in building along the lane in order to attract international trading firms. One was Chen Tian-lai (AD 1872-1939), a Taiwanese tea merchant, who was fabulously rich for his time. His home was one…
spots.addr: West of Dihua Street and Xining North Road

spots.name: Sin Hong Choon
spots.desc: A former tea factory and storefront built in 1934 with blended east-west architecture, now a museum on the history of Taipei tea markets and Taiwanese tea production. The upstairs cafe offers introductory tea tastings.
spots.addr: No. 309號, Minsheng W Rd, Datong District

spots.name: Xiahai City God Temple
spots.desc: This historic Taoist temple was built in 1859 to worship Xiahai, the City God (城隍爺), who watched over the citizens in the district and decided a person's fate after death. It might be small, with an area of only about 46 square meters, but it one of Taipei's most important places of worship, and is the area's religious and social center. In addition to Xiahai, this temple is dedicated to 600…

spots.name: Machangding Memorial Park
spots.desc: The park features an artificial mound on the approximate site where a number of people were executed during the period of marshal law. The park is dedicated to those who lost their lives during this period.

spots.name: Yongle Fabric Market
spots.desc: Established in 1928 by the Japanese, this market originally sold food, but over time it evolved into a cloth market. Today, this market contains over 100 different cloth shops selling all kinds of fabrics and cloth wares.

spots.name: Red House
spots.desc: The Red House is both a teahouse and a venue for small-scale theater productions. The two-story high red brick building is shaped into an octagonal cylinder. The first and second floors of the Red House now are the art exhibition, restaurants, cafes, shops, and theaters. During weekends, the outside of the Red House become somewhat of a bazaar, where several booths are set up for college…

spots.name: Huaxi Street Night Market

spots.name: Yengsan Night Market

spots.name: Dalong Street Night Market

spots.name: Ah Chung Mee Soa

Don't forget to add the condiments provided at the side…

spots.name: Calcutta Indian Curry House

spots.name: Miniatures Museum of Taiwan

spots.name: Taipei Story House
spots.desc: On the same plot of land as the Taipei Fine Arts Museum, this tea merchant's 19th-century European style house has been converted into a gallery and museum space with visiting exhibitions and the occasional traditional music concert. The patio serves as a tea garden, which offers pleasant views over the Danshui River and beyond.

spots.name: Dajia Riverside Park
spots.desc: This park is a 12-km-long green belt on the south bank of the Keelung River. One of the beautiful banks in Taipei. Basketball, tennis, and badminton courts are available, as are bicycles for rent.

spots.name: Zhongshan Fine Arts Park
spots.desc: This park is south of the Taipei Fine Arts Museum. The open green space and many stabiles are on display in the park.

spots.name: Children's Recreation Center
spots.desc: It is an amusement park on Zhongshan North Road Sec. 3, nearest MRT station is 'Yuanshan' on Danshui Line. The center was created by city government in 1991. It has old-fashioned rides, folk art museum, IMAX theater and more. This place is great for younger kids.

spots.name: Miramar Entertainment Park
spots.desc: This up-scale shopping mall in the suburb of Dazhi operates a large Ferris wheel that offers great views over the city. It is especially spectacular at night, when not only the city but also the Ferris wheel is illuminated. The 15-minute ride costs NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends. The same complex also houses a 3D Imax movie theater and a multi-screen Warner Village cinema.
spots.price: NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends

spots.name: Spot - Taipei Film House
spots.desc: The former residence of the U.S. Ambassador has been transformed into an art center that focuses on independent films. In addition to screenings, the house also has great cafes and restaurants that spill out onto balconies and into the garden. The bookstore offers a good selection of hard-to-get art/independent films on DVD, though for other movies, prices are lower at regular DVD rental stores.

spots.name: TaipeiEYE
spots.desc: The venue is recognized for its traditional Chinese and Taiwanese performing arts. Following a tradition that dates back to the 18th century. The 90-minute evening show is a form of Chinese opera that incorporates mime, dance, acrobatics and martial arts. During the live performance, the dialogue and even the songs are translated into multiple languages, including English.

spots.name: Eslite Spectrum

spots.name: Eslite Underground Bookstore

spots.name: Wang Steak House

spots.name: Standing Room

The in-flight break-up was caused by improper repairs to the aircraft 22 years earlier. It remains the deadliest in Taiwanese…

spots.name: Jhushan

spots.name: Giant Trees Trail

The original 52 m Sacred Tree fell in 1998 to become a massive nurse log, passing the sacred designation to the 47 m Xianglin Giant Tree. The small Cihyun Temple, which was built by…

spots.name: Two Sister Ponds

The southern end is home to the Art Museum with Modern and Traditional exhibits, a cafe on the third floor and a garden…

spots.name: Dakeng Scenic Area (hiking)
spots.desc: DaKeng in BeiTun District has several hiking paths along elevated wooden walkways. Trails are connected and some loop to connect with other trails. In summer, come early to beat the heat. Trails are numbered with some gaps (closed/disappeared trail? No more 5). Initial and more popular trails from farmers market are 9, 9-1, and 10, the latter two, more stairs-intensive. Mostly well-maintained…
spots.addr: Lane 383, Section 1, Dongshan Rd, Beitun District

spots.name: Jianguo Market
spots.desc: This is the biggest traditional market in Taichung. The market runs for about two blocks along Bade Street, and there are also many vendors along the side streets off of Bade Street. Aside from being a market for everyday shoppers, it is also a wholesale market, supplying other traditional markets and restaurants in Taichung. Look for signs that say 寄車 (Ji Che), which are for pay parking. These…
spots.addr: 臺中市東區建國路 224 號 No.224, Jianguo Rd., East Dist., Taichung City

spots.name: Second Market
spots.desc: At Second Market all of the vendors are under a roof. There is a map of the layout of the market at each entrance. Second Market assigns numbers to all of the vendors. In the descriptions of selected vendors below, the ‘vendor number’ is the number assigned to the vendor by the market authority. The numbers include the Chinese characters 臨 (lin) and 內 (nei). For example, if a vendor’s number is…
spots.addr: 臺中市中區三民路2 段87 號 No.87, Sec. 2, Sanmin Rd., Central Dist.

spots.name: Third Market
spots.desc: The area has a covering of colorful plastic streamers stretched between the buildings over the streets.
spots.addr: 臺中市南區臺中路 90 號 No.90, Taichung Rd., South Dist.

spots.name: Fifth Market
spots.desc: The market has stalls, vendors and shops along both Daming and Tzli Street, as well as on 樂群 (Luchuen Street). There are many different vendors and shops inside the building. There is a parking lot on Luchuen Street near Tzli Street. You can also park a scooter on the streets, lanes and alleys.
spots.addr: 臺中市西區大明街 9 號 No.9, Daming St., West Dist.

spots.name: Xiang Shang Market
spots.local: 西昌街觀光夜市, 向上市場
spots.desc: There is a parking lot about 100 m from the intersection of Zhongmei and Xianshang Roads. Of course you can park a scooter just about anywhere, but the streets, lanes and alleys are small and jam packed.
spots.addr: 臺中市西區向上路一段218巷 Ln. 218, Sec. 1, Xiangshang Rd., West Dist.

spots.name: The old good tone
spots.desc: Good place for breakfast with a menu in both Mandarin and English. Also, an English map of where to go around (see, eat). Seems popular and radish cake can be sold out after 09:00.

spots.name: Rururi pirate rice ball
spots.desc: While it's not cheap in terms of a breakfast meal (thus the name "pirate"), its rice ball is pretty delicious. They also provide sandwiches and drinks.
spots.addr: No. 136-6, Section 3, Sanmin Rd, North District

spots.name: Weng's Goose
spots.desc: This restaurant offers goose cooked in three different ways: smoked goose, drunken goose, and salt-water goose. No matter which flavour you choose, the meat is tender and juicy
spots.addr: No.99-1, Sec. 1, Siangshang Rd, West Dist

spots.name: Little India Muslim Restaurant (Halal)
spots.desc: This little hole-in-the-wall is more about good honest food and less about decorations.

spots.name: Chilliesine Indian Restaurant Chaofu Branch
spots.desc: Actually, there are five Chilliesine restaurants in Taichung, and all of them are the nice Indian restaurants in town. Aside from food, they also have good service and atmosphere. It received a Michelin Bib Gourmand for years for a good reason.

spots.name: Uptowner Taichung
spots.desc: American-style diner, providing good Western-style dishes, while customers can watch sports as well.

spots.name: Mr. Chicken Head
spots.desc: A very popular restaurant that attracts a lot of teenagers. The decorations on the walls are very cute and special. The restaurant is filled with energy and good cheer.

spots.name: Fifth Market
spots.desc: A marketplace for fruits and vegetables, and a great place to find local snacks.

spots.name: Match Cafe
spots.desc: Match provides a pleasant atmosphere where one can have a cup of coffee, a bagel or a sandwich and work on one's computer.
spots.addr: No.902, Sec. 2, Taiwan Blvd. Situn Dist

spots.name: The Naked Cafe
spots.desc: The Naked Cafe serves up coffee, tea, great sandwiches and fries in a somewhat Euro-inspired atmosphere.

spots.name: UZO Mediterranean Bar & Grill
spots.desc: Fresh Mediterranean specialities: kebab wraps, gyros, falafel, hummus, baba ghanoush, dolma, pizzas, salads and a selection of appetisers. Large selection of imported beers. Comfy outdoor seating. Staff speak great English and the service is good. Relaxed and easygoing atmosphere, rowdy kids and adults are not tolerated.

spots.name: Golden Jaguar
spots.desc: Probably the most infamous high-end nightclub in Taichung. Known for its luxury facilities, regular headline of local news, and hostessing services, you can see its four-story building from the Taiwan Boulevard, and you will never forget its glaring spotlight at night. However, a customer needs at least TWD $3200 (USD $100) per hour even when choosing the most affordable options, while choosing…
spots.addr: No. 960, Sec Taiwan Rd, Situn District

spots.name: Chun Shui Tang
spots.desc: One of the two rival claimants to having invented bubble tea.

spots.name: Gaomei Wetlands
spots.desc: Popular spot for sunset. If low tide, can walk on wet sand at the end of the dock. If high tide or near, may have a nice sky mirror effect. Walking the dock one-way is about 15 min and may see small crabs and mud keepers, eventually migratory birds depending on the seasons. The path between the dock and No. 18 windmill is about 30 min walk. If staying late and depending on the seasons, have some…
spots.hours: Dock 08:00-19:00 (closing per sunset, sooner or later and possible closing around high tide)

spots.name: Container "Mountain"
spots.desc: If you are going to the Gaomei Wetlands, take a stop at this surreal place where dozens of containers are stacked up and offer an interesting photo opportunity.

spots.name: Taiwan Printing and Discovery Museum
spots.desc: A museum of a printing factory. A reservation is required, and only a group can apply for it, so backpackers may not be able to visit. But don't be disappointed, there are some facilities for backpackers nearby, such as a library, an art plaza, and parks.

spots.name: Dian Song Pi Antique Culture Gallery (天送埤文物館)-
spots.dest: Tian Song Pi Agricultural Leisure Area
spots.desc: Displays ancient tools to show the history of the logging industry and early life of residents. If tourists want to visit, they have to make a reservation before going. #13 Ticket information: adult 30NT$, children NT$10 per person.

spots.name: Wei Zhen Xiang Po-Ba Store (卜肉店)-
spots.dest: Tian Song Pi Agricultural Leisure Area
spots.desc: It sells the most famous dish in Sanshing township, Po-Ba (a kind of fried pork).

spots.name: A Po's Green Onion Pancake (阿婆蔥油餅)-
spots.dest: Tian Song Pi Agricultural Leisure Area
spots.desc: Pancakes filled with green onion are a local specialty. The vendor also sells uncooked pancakes to take home for NT$100/5 pieces. Sanshing Green Onion is well-known in Taiwan for its taste.

spots.name: Twenty-one tea house (21茶坊)-
spots.dest: Tian Song Pi Agricultural Leisure Area
spots.desc: Sells several kinds of drinks such as bubble tea, green tea, coffee and hot chocolate.

spots.name: Jinguashi Shinto Shrine
spots.desc: The Jinguashi Shinto Shrine, also called the “Mountain God Shrine,” is dedicated to the three deities of “ôkuninushinomikoto, kaneyamahikonomikoto and sarutahikonomikoto. In 1933, after the Japan Mining Company took over the management of Jinguashi mine, it commemorated the event by building a Shinto shrine half way up the mountain below Siping lane. The original shrine included a main hall…

spots.name: Wuhu Speedway
spots.desc: A small go-kart track within walking distance of the main wharf.

spots.name: Yongan Watersports
spots.desc: A shop on the beach where you can rent various watersports equipment.

spots.name: Jibei Beach Park
spots.desc: A long beach-covered peninsula popular with both locals and tourists to enjoy the sunshine and the sea.

spots.name: Zaodian
spots.desc: A small shop selling Taiwanese style breakfast fare such as danbing.

spots.name: Chi Ma Military Trail
spots.desc: A hiking trail that passes through some old, disused military tunnels.

spots.name: Fire and Water
spots.desc: A part of the hot spring that releases methane, which has been on fire for over three centuries now!

spots.name: Delicacies From Land and Sea
spots.desc: Wood-paneled restaurant easily spotted by the flaming torch outside, specializing in dishes from mountain ingredients.

spots.name: Dachu Coffee Estate (Daichu Farm)
spots.local: 大鋤花間咖啡生態農場
spots.desc: The organic family-run coffee farm that started Dongshan coffee route. Calm refreshing scenic sunny mountain views, plenty of friendly cats, filling food and coffee.

spots.name: Bandao Tie He Dim Sum Restaurant
spots.desc: Good and inexpensive Dim Sum restaurant

spots.name: JL Studio
spots.desc: Singaporean cuisine, Michelin three-star restaurant.
spots.hours: Sat Sun 12:00–14:30, Wed–Sun 18:00–22:00, closed Mon Tue
spots.addr: 2F., No.689, Sec. 4, Yifong Rd. Nantun Dist

spots.name: Gaomei Wetlands Visitor Center
spots.desc: Few shops, toilets, water fountain.

spots.name: Meifang ice cream
spots.desc: A tasty ice cream is available here.

spots.name: Dasyueshan National Forest Recreational Area
spots.local: 大雪山國家森林遊樂區
spots.desc: This forest is home to Dasyueshan.

spots.name: Gu-Guan Hot Spring
spots.desc: A nice hot spring at north side of Taichung.

spots.name: Huang’s Tea Factory (黃記茶廠)-
spots.dest: Tian Song Pi Agricultural Leisure Area
spots.desc: It sells tea grown in Yilan.

spots.name: Neiwan Theater
spots.desc: Movie theater and restaurant.

spots.name: Wusheng Temple
spots.desc: An ornate temple perched atop a stone staircase.

spots.name: 小萍的店
spots.desc: Small noodle and seafood place near the Geological Museum.

spots.name: University Pond
spots.desc: The nature area's most popular (if least natural) point of interest, this is a landscaped pond with a footbridge, surrounded by messy greenery including many tree ferns. Well-suited for unambitious walkers, it's accessible from the entrance by a short walk along a wide paved road or a pretty evergreen forest path.

spots.name: Xitou Giant Tree
spots.desc: A massive, old-growth Taiwan Red Cypress tree stood here for thousands of years, standing out as the only remaining natural-growing evergreen conifer tree in the area until it fell in 2016. Today there's a boardwalk that allows to you walk around part of enormous fallen log, which is being allowed to return to nature, covered with thousands of smaller forest understory plants.

spots.name: Giant Rock
spots.desc: A house-sized boulder that tumbled down the mountain during the 1999 Jiji Earthquake (921). Now already partially overgrown with plant life. Access via a short but steep paved trail.

spots.name: Ginkgo Bridge
spots.desc: Maybe the most photogenic architectural feature in the nature area - a wooden footbridge in a wavy shape with two humps.

spots.name: Overlook and Astronomical Observatory
spots.desc: For more ambitious visitors, this is the place for expansive views of the surrounding mountains, located atop the mountain ridge bounding the nature area to the east. A 750-meter climb from the nature area entrance via steep stone steps or long switchback roads. (Not something to aim for late in the day unless you're a fast hiker.)

spots.name: Bird Watching Trail
spots.desc: A good strenuous short hike: 1.4 km along a well-maintained trail with a climb of about 200 meters (stone steps), passing through something like the area's natural montane broadleaf forest.

spots.name: Hiking Trail
spots.desc: A strenous short hike, climbing 400 m in 1.3 km from where it branches off the Bird Watching Trail to its end near the Observatory, crossing the switchback roads in a couple of places

spots.name: Phoenix Mountain (Fenghuangshan) North Ridgeline Trail
spots.desc: For serious hikers: one of several longer treks that can be done from Xitou, this route follows the mountain ridge from the Observatory across several peaks of Pheonix (Fenghuang) Mountain.

spots.name: Sky Walk
spots.desc: A wooden canopy walk among the cedar trees.
